# Change ledger: November 2026

What changed in November 2026, newest first. The [index](../CHANGELOG.md) says how the ledger is kept.

## 23 November 2026

### Release 0.7.0: drawn pieces at any size and angle, texture mapping, Align, diagonal cover kept, Map settings and smaller baked maps

At the user's ask ("let's prepare for a new release, this will be a minor 0.7 release"). Made on main, 9 commits
ahead of `origin/main`; nothing pushed.

- [version.py](../tools/viewer/version.py) 0.7.0. [lighting_size.py](../tools/bake/lighting_size.py)'s docstring
  no longer names a 0.6.1 that was never released.

  0.6.0.
  - **Upgrading:** close the editor first (0.6.0 holds no mutex for Setup to see); every map is read again on its
    first open (export 39, 0.6.0 had 36); a project or prefab saved in 0.7.0 can't be opened in 0.6.0 (project
    schema 5, 0.6.0 reads 1 to 4; prefab schema 4, 0.6.0 reads 1 to 3, and every prefab is written at 4); a cleared
    project's next Build takes the map's triggers out unless kept; a map pack exported by 0.6.0 or earlier names the
    computer's folders in its manifest (KB-16); a baked build with a `.tfc` beside it is built again before it is

    Taller than its look), Texture mapping, Align to grid, level and game pose, diagonal cover shown and kept, Map
    settings with the background sound, Clear map taking the triggers, how a made wall in a tile row plays.
  - **Changes:** Snap for every move, size and turn; Play in game under play names; smaller baked maps; lighting
    inside every map; the path limit checked before a Build.
  - **Bugs fixed:** lost diagonal cover (F-149), the quicksave crash (F-156), civilians in the air (F-157), black

    all, a prefab's made pieces, Save as's picture, a project with a piece that can't be drawn).

## 22 November 2026

### No build, pack or install ships a texture cache: every map holds its baked lighting inside it

Builds have put their baked lightmaps inside the map since 19 November 2026, but three places still let a `.tfc`
through. All three are gone, so every map is built and shipped the same way.

- **The Build** ([build.py](../tools/editor/build.py) `lighting_inside`): a map whose lightmaps can't be put
  inside it used to ship its `<Map>_Lighting.tfc` beside it, with a note. Now that fails the build, saying why, and
  the last good package stays. The relight still writes its cache in the build's work folder, and the cache is moved
  into the map there. The manifest's `cache` is always None, and the README no longer has a "lightmaps in a .tfc"
  case. A build's cache name is no longer an output name: [outputnames.py](../tools/viewer/outputnames.py) claims
  `<map>_Lighting` for no project, and a file of that name stops no build.
- **The map pack** ([manager.py](../tools/viewer/manager.py)): the export no longer converts an older build's cache
  into its map (`_inline_lighting`), and no longer puts a cache beside the pack's folder. `pack.json` loses
  `cacheFiles`, and the READMEs and the [pack scripts](../tools/viewer/pack_scripts.py) lose their cache lines.
  Every file of a pack is in its folder.
- **The installs** ([installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py) `read_package`): a package whose files include a
  `.tfc` (a build from before 19 November 2026) is refused by Play in game, Install in the game and the map pack:
  "has its lighting in a texture cache beside the map ... build the project again". The project manager's list warns
  about such a build. The play's cache guard and [play_names.py](../tools/viewer/play_names.py)' branch for files
  that keep their names are gone, since every file of a package is now a map package. A cache an earlier install put
  in the game is still the editor's, and Remove from game takes it out.

The lab's [pack_test.py](../tools/lab/pack_test.py) no longer copies caches beside a pack's folder. Its `take`
still removes the ones an older note lists. The game's own shared caches (`Lighting.tfc` and the like), which the
game's maps and the lightmaps a build leaves as they were read, stay where the game keeps them.

Checked: the play, play-name, manager, pack export, output-name and build tests rewritten for it (a package with a
`.tfc` refused for a play, a campaign install and a pack, with the warning in the list; a map that can't take its
lightmaps in fails its build and leaves the last package), and the viewer, editor, lab, repo, release and node suites.

Known gaps: a project whose last build is from before 19 November 2026 has to be built again before it can be played,
installed or packed. The lab's bake-fixture tools still write caches for their own fixtures.

### Play in game installs a build under play names of its own, so a map pack of the same map no longer stops it (F-161)

A player reported that a project could not be played from the editor while the same map was installed in the game
through a map pack. Play in game installed the build under the project's own names, which the pack's copy holds too:
a drop-in pack put a second package of each name under CookedPCConsole and, under Long War Rebalance 3, its line
(merged by display name) took the place of the play's record; a pack installed with Install.cmd left a record and
files of the map's name that the install step refused to replace.
[F-161](../research/findings-register.md) has the details.

A play now installs every package of the build under its name with a play suffix,
[play_names.py](../tools/viewer/play_names.py): `<Map>_Play`, or `_Play2` and on when one of the names is in the
install (a file anywhere under CookedPCConsole, a pack's folder included; a map name of DefaultMaps.ini; the editor's
ledgers, [installs.play_taken](../tools/viewer/installs.py)). What the project's own earlier play holds is replaced,
as before. The map, its patch and its stream copies are copied as they are under their new names; each intro copy is
written again with its Switch Strings naming the play's map (`intro_copy.make` with the map's name as the base), so
the landing plays. The record is the Build's line for the mission under the play's name, its display name starting
with it (the words Long War matches after the name stay), streaming the play's copies; landing zones and the drop-in
exclusion name the play's map ([mapsini.renamed_maps](../tools/viewer/mapsini.py) renames a line's map names). A
texture cache keeps its name, since textures find it by name: a play refuses one that differs from a campaign
install's of that name, which the campaign's map reads.

Because a play no longer shares names with the project's campaign install, a play of a newer build leaves the
campaign's files as they are (before, it replaced them), the project manager reads a play's `variant` to show it in
the game ([manager.py](../tools/viewer/manager.py)), and the Game maps window's Undo of a build takes its play out
with it (`installs.remove_rotation`). A play no longer takes the place of a record the lab's patchtool deploy wrote
for the map; it goes beside it. Play's dialog, the Installs line and the [guide](../tools/release/guide/guide.html)
say the play name.

Checked: [test_play_names.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_play_names.py) (a play beside a drop-in pack and beside a
pack installed the classic way, each left byte for byte; a name the pack holds takes the play to `_Play2`; the game's
own intro copied by the Build and renamed for a play reads back with the play's name in its switches), the play,
recovery and manager tests brought to the play names, and the viewer, repo and node suites.

Known gaps: not played in the game yet. A build whose lightmaps could not go inside the map ships a texture cache under
its own name: a pack that carries a different build's cache of that name beside its folder still stops a play, with
the install step's message.

### A clear takes the map's triggers out; a project can give the map another background sound (F-159, F-160; export 39, project schema 5)

The trimmed part of the triggers investigation (the full Triggers view stays on the reference branch
`editor-triggers`): the Build's side of both, the Clear map window's tick, and the page carrying the background sound
(its control waits on the user's choice of design).

- **A cleared map's triggers** (F-159). [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py) `clear_level` takes the
  level's trigger volumes and sight points out (`CLEAR_TRIGGERS`, which `CLEAR_KEEP` kept until now) and switches off
  every sequence event whose Originator is a volume it took (`switch_off_events`, `bEnabled` false; the cleared
  record's `eventsOff`), unless the cleared mark says `keepTriggers`. The project's `clearKeepsTriggers` sets it
  ([mission_edits.py](../tools/editor/mission_edits.py) `cleared_mark`, [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py)).
  A cleared project saved before has no such field, so its next Build takes them out.
- **The map's background sound** (F-160). The export reads it ([background_sound.py](../tools/viewer/background_sound.py):
  the scene's `backgroundSound`, with `triggerCounts` from [scene_metadata.py](../tools/viewer/scene_metadata.py);
  export 39), and [background_sounds.json](../tools/viewer/background_sounds.json) lists the game's 26 beds with the
  base map that plays each. The project's `backgroundSound` (`{cue, volume?}`, a cue or null; schema 5 in
  [projects.py](../tools/viewer/projects.py), [project.js](../tools/viewer/web/project.js) and the compiler) is
  checked by [effect_edits.py](../tools/editor/effect_edits.py) `background_sound_mark` (left out where it can't
  be built: its shape, an export before 39, a map with none, a cue off the list) and goes into the native edit's
  `backgroundSound` lane ([native_edit.py](../tools/editor/native_edit.py)) with the map it comes from as its
  donor. [transplant.py](../tools/bake/transplant.py) brings a cue from its map as assets (`closure` and `bring`
  with `assets`; `stage_edit` for the lane's donor), and [native_sounds.py](../tools/bake/native_sounds.py)
  `background` points the map's level-loaded `SeqAct_PlaySound` at it, or at none, with its volume, read back by
  `verify_background`. [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py) runs the transplant for it, counts it as work that
  changes no light (it goes with the effects) and writes the manifest's `backgroundSound`.
- **The page.** The Clear map window has "Keep the map's triggers and scripts" (remembered, as the scenery tick is;
  hidden on a map with none), and its plan names the map's touch triggers, water volumes and sight points as going
  or staying, and says the background sound stays ([clear_map.js](../tools/viewer/web/clear_map.js), from export
  39's `triggerCounts`). The project's `clearKeepsTriggers` and `backgroundSound` are kept, saved, recovered, undone
  with the clear or Reset all ([editor_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/editor_state.js),
  [document_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/document_state.js),
  [document_session.js](../tools/viewer/web/document_session.js),
  [delete_reset.js](../tools/viewer/web/delete_reset.js), `validBackgroundSound` in project.js), so a page saving
  a project never drops them; test hooks `clearKeepsTriggers` and `backgroundSound`.
- [clear_bar_project.py](../tools/editor/examples/clear_bar_project.py) takes `--keep-triggers`, `--sound`,
  `--volume` and `--cache`; [build_outputs.py](../tools/editor/tests/build_outputs.py)'s bar-clear input gives it
  the forest bed, so the new lane is covered. The examples that save into a store write the current schema.
- Records: [editor-contracts.md](../research/editor-contracts.md) (schema 5's two fields, export 39's),
  [findings-register.md](../research/findings-register.md) F-159, F-160,
  [EXP-94](../research/experiments/EXP-94-background-sound-and-clear.md), [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md).

### An effect copy's panel keeps its number fields in view; a collectible's copy reads as mission loot

Two reports from the Discord feedback list (B6 and S15).

- **B6: a copied effect's particle parameters lost their number fields.** In the Effects panel of an effect's copy,
  the value rows ran past the panel's right edge, so the number beside each slider (and Velocity's z) was cut off;
  the original's panel was fine. The panels on the right (`#effectPanel`, `#spawnPanel`, `#volumePanel`,
  `#landingPanel`, `#gridPanel`) are grids with no column set, and an implicit grid column is as wide as its widest
  unwrapped line: the About fold's one-line summary (`.foldval`, no wrap), which for a copy reads "A copy of
  Emitter_38: the Build makes it an actor of its own.", made the column, and with it every row, about 80 pixels wider
  than the panel, whose `overflow-x: hidden` then cut the fields off. [style.css](../tools/viewer/web/style.css)
  gives those panels one column no wider than the panel (`minmax(0, 1fr)`); the About summary now ends in an ellipsis
  there, its full text in its title as before. The screen's size played no part: the panel is 300 pixels wide at any.
- **S15: a collectible's copy said "Not loot".** The piece panel's chip ([pieces.js](../tools/viewer/web/pieces.js)
  `lootNote`) still described the copier's copies of before 7 November. Since EXP-20 run 8 the Build makes a
  collectible's copy a collectible in the level's actor list, which the game's loot count walks, and takes a deleted
  one out of it ([compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `LOOT_NOTES`). The chip now reads **Mission loot** for
  a copy as for an original, and its title says that a copy counts, a moved one still counts once, a deleted one no
  longer counts and a damaged one counts as the damaged item. The [guide](../tools/release/guide/guide.html)'s chip
  table and its kinds of pieces table said the same wrong thing and are corrected.

Checked:
- On a test server (URB_Bar, export 38): Emitter_38's copy, before the fix, laid its panel out 368 pixels wide in a
  288-pixel box with every number field 63 pixels past the edge (as reported); after it, nothing past the edge and
  the original unchanged.
- [browser_smoke.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_smoke.py): `check_effect_values` now checks that the copy's
  panel is no wider than it shows and no value row or field crosses its right edge (it fails without the fix:
  80 pixels wider, 46 rows and fields cut); `check_adding` checks a collectible's copy's chip. The checks
  effect-values, adding, spawns, text-select, floor-boxes, map-buildings, tile-grid, pivot and typed-pose pass.
- The node, repo and release suites.

Known gaps: the browser smoke's effects check didn't run whole here (its wave preview needs a server with a piece
library, and this test server served one export). That a copy counts at the loot screen has still not been seen in
the game (EXP-20 run 10 couldn't end Temple Ship's mission); the chip says what the Build makes.

### Terror civilians no longer start in the air where deleted pieces had floors, and baked copies no longer show black where something stands on their original (F-157, F-158; KB-18 and KB-19 out)

A user's skyscraper map (a CLrgScout_City variant with its UFO deleted and a helipad in its place) showed both.

**Civilians in the air (F-157).** The game places the terror civilians on the map's stored cover points (within 960
units of a pod), and a pod's other aliens on the nearest valid places, before it runs the battle's tile rebuild; a
Build left a deleted piece's floors and cover points stored for that rebuild to clear. The Build now writes the tiles
near its changes as the rebuild will leave them:

- [start_tiles.py](../tools/bake/start_tiles.py) (new): for the tiles a rebuild volume reaches that lie near a
  change (the boxes its rebuild volumes were made for, with a tile round them, a level under and two over) or round a
  floor whose piece was taken out of the level, passes 1 and 2 of the game's tile build
  ([tile_build.py](../tools/bake/tile_build.py)) against the built map; each tile whose stored state differs gets
  the result (no floor or cover where nothing stands now, the floors and cover points new pieces make) and a seed
  bit, so the battle's rebuild, which clears a queued tile and works it out afresh, still has the last word.
- [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py): the grower gathers the `changed` boxes of its rebuild volumes
  (`change_boxes`); `rewrite_tiles` (was `forget_taken_out`) rewrites the written map's tile data once after the
  diagonal tiles: these tiles first, then the references to taken-out actors cleared (F-156), so a build with
  deletions writes its tile data as often as before and a build of copies alone once more; the native record's
  `startTiles` and a log line say what it wrote. `rebuild_order(p, queued=False)` gives every tile of the volumes'
  reach.
- It also seeds the tiles the battle used to leave stale for good: 32 tiles inside the deleted UFO's hull kept only
  "sight blocked upward" (a bit the rebuild's queue test does not read) and are now worked out.

**Black patches on baked copies (F-158).** [relight.py](../tools/bake/relight.py) lit a copy of one of the map's
own pieces as a change on its original's lightmap and kept the original's bake for a texel buried at either place;
a texel buried only where the original stands (a floor under a staircase) is black there, so the copy showed that
footprint in the open. Now only a texel buried where the copy stands keeps the original's bake; one buried only
where the original stands is relit as the floor under a removed piece is (its light before comes out near zero), and
the record counts it as `opened`.

Also: [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)'s tile row names the new module; [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md):
KB-18 and KB-19 out; [findings-register.md](../research/findings-register.md): F-157 and F-158.

Checked: the bake suite (`test_start_tiles`: on the bar with its upstairs floor strip deleted and a dumpster copied
onto open street, the strip's ten tiles keep no floor or cover point and stay queued, the tiles beside the dumpster
have cover points from the start, tiles more than four tiles away keep their bytes; it fails with the step left out.
`test_native_copy` `CopyBuriedWhereItsSourceStands`: a ground slab copied 480 units east, its 1,857 texels buried
where the source stands lit about as the open slab round them; it fails on the old rule), the upk and repo suites.
The reported project rebuilt (quick): no cover point above the ground left on a deleted piece's floor (56 within a
pod's reach before), the tiles beside the helipad open air, its top a floor with cover points; the step took 4.0 s
over 15,015 tiles. Rebuilt with the bake: the floor copy's black patches gone (897, 308 and 940 black texels to 158, 0
and 140, those left under the pieces standing on it now). In the game
([EXP-92](../research/experiments/EXP-92-civilians-and-copy-patch.md), hidden terror battles in the lab copy): on
the project built without the fix 2 of 18 civilians started in the air, one at the deleted UFO's roof; on the fixed
build none of 36 in two battles, and the floor south of the helipad shows no patch.

Time: on a cleared map nearly every tile lies round a deleted floor, but empty tiles are cheap: the bar with its
733 pieces deleted had 13,118 tiles worked out and 8,582 written in 1.9 s.

Known gaps: the pods' other aliens, placed from the same stored tiles, were not looked at in the game.

### Two bugs from a user's report recorded: terror civilians in the air, a black patch on a baked copy (F-157, F-158, KB-18, KB-19)

A user's map pack (a CLrgScout_City variant with its UFO deleted and an EXALT helipad in its place, built with
0.6.0 and baked) showed civilians starting in the air beside the helipad, and a dark patch on the floor by it. Both
were read offline; nothing in the tools changed.

- [findings-register.md](../research/findings-register.md) F-157: the game places terror civilians on the map's
  stored cover points (within 960 units of a pod) in `InitPlayers`, before `DoWorldDataRebuild`; a Build leaves a
  deleted piece's tiles, floors and cover points, for that rebuild (`native_copy.hide_tiles`). The reported build
  keeps 75 cover points on the UFO's floors above the ground (z 64 by the helipad, z 414 to 451 on its roof) and 20
  under the helipad.
- F-158: the patch is the Build's copy of the map's own floor `XComLevelActor_526`; its black texels are those buried
  under a staircase where the original stands, and `relight.py` keeps the original's bake for a texel buried at
  either place. Two more such patches lie on the same copy by the map's east edge.
- [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md): KB-18 and KB-19, with their workarounds.

### Worktrees and branches are removed when their work is merged

[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) gains a rule: the turn that merges a branch into main removes its worktree and deletes
the branch (`git branch -d`, which refuses an unmerged one), the worktrees subagents make under `.claude/worktrees`
included; one stays only while its work is not merged or when the user asks to keep it.

The rule follows a clean-up of what the refactor, the follow-ups and the custom geometry work left: 69 worktrees
and 158 local branches, every one already in main. Each worktree's commit was checked to be an ancestor of main
before it went; the only files not committed in them were nine resume checkpoints of finished agents.

Checked: `git worktree list` and `git branch` show the main checkout and `main` alone; the `repo` suite.

### A built map no longer crashes the game on saving when its tiles named deleted pieces (F-156 verified, KB-17 out)

A quicksave on the reported city project's built map crashed the game, in every build of it. The map's tile data
names actors by their place in the package: each floor tile its floor piece and floor volume, each link its path
object, each interact point its actor. A Build that deletes a piece takes it out of the level's actor list and the
tiles still named it; the game frees such an actor after loading, and where the battle's rebuild does not work the
tile out again, saving followed the tile into freed memory
([F-156](../research/findings-register.md), [EXP-91](../research/experiments/EXP-91-smaller-built-maps.md)).

- [world_grid.py](../tools/upk/world_grid.py) `forget`: the tile model with no tile naming an actor of a set: a
  floor piece or floor volume becomes none, a link through a path object among them is dropped, as an interact point
  of one (a tile left with none saves none).
- [world_links.py](../tools/upk/world_links.py): `encode_floor` and `encode_interact`, a floor and an interact
  element written from their fields ([diagonal_keep.py](../tools/bake/diagonal_keep.py) uses `encode_floor`).
- [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py): `taken_out` (the exports under the level not in its list) and
  `forget_taken_out`, run on the written map after the diagonal tiles, in quick and baked builds alike; the native
  record's `tilesForgot` and a log line say what it cleared.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md): a row for it. [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md): KB-17 out.

Checked: across the install's 96 maps no tile names anything outside its level (so the step changes no map but a
Build's); the upk suite (`test_world_grid` `Forget`: the elements encode back to their bytes on URB_Bar, nothing
gone changes nothing, a floor piece and volume become none, a link and a door's interact points dropped) and the bake
suite (`test_native_copy`: no tile of the shared bar builds names an actor taken out, the record says what was
cleared). In the game (EXP-91, hidden runs): the project's quick build crashed; the same with those references set
to none saved and loaded; the full build with the fix saved, loaded and saved again.

Known gaps: a tile outside every rebuild volume whose floor piece was deleted keeps its floor, now naming no piece
(the rebuild volumes decide which tiles the battle works out again, as before). The rewritten tile data is appended
and the old bytes stay in the package (3.3 MB in that map), as for the diagonal tiles.

### A copy's lightmaps the size of what it reads, and no folder of a computer in a pack or a build's manifest (F-151; KB-15 out, KB-16)

A baked Build gave every copy a clone of each lightmap and shadow-map texture its source reads, a whole 1,024-texel
atlas for a rectangle of a few dozen texels, and since 0.6.0 the map holds them uncompressed: a reported map pack's
city variant with 166 copies was 336 MB (F-151, KB-15). Now each copy, piece from another map and made piece gets
textures the size of what it reads (smaller built maps plan, `private/plans/done/smaller-built-maps-plan.md`, stages
S0 to S3 and S5; decisions D1 to D6 at their proposals).

- [lightmap_textures.py](../tools/bake/lightmap_textures.py): `crop_box` (the rectangles a copy reads with the
  writer's one-texel ring, on whole DXT1 blocks, a power of two each way, at least the game's smallest),
  `cropped_texture` (the source's bake over the box, its top mip's blocks or bytes copied as they are, its lower mips
  made from it), `blank_texture`, `moved_record` (a coordinate scale and bias pointed into the box, exact in the
  records' 32-bit floats). Each is a texture as the game's own small ones are inside a map: every mip inline and
  uncompressed, the chain down to one texel with DXT1 sides stored no smaller than 4, MipTailBaseIdx its last mip,
  NeverStream, no cache name (`top_mip_bytes` reads a G8 shadow map's top mip too).
- [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py): `lighting_boxes` finds each texture's box over every record of
  the copy that reads it (the textures one lightmap record reads share one box; a texture whose records can't move
  exactly is cloned whole); `clone_assembly` makes the cropped textures and rewrites the copy's lightmap records and
  ShadowMap2D coordinates. Pieces from other maps are cropped the same way (the plan said blank: a crop is no larger
  and keeps the home map's bake where the relight writes nothing). A made piece's LOD 0 textures are no longer
  cloned at all where nothing else reads them.
- [frac_walls.py](../tools/bake/frac_walls.py): a made wall's, floor's or ground's lightmap is textures of its own
  of its rectangle's size with its ring (`own_light`), the rectangle one texel in; its shadow map of the dominant
  light a blank texture of that size (`own_shadow_size`), in place of a clone of a 1,024 field. Its density is its
  donor's, as before, no larger than 1,022 texels a side.
- [relight.py](../tools/bake/relight.py) and [shadowmaps.py](../tools/bake/shadowmaps.py): a copy relit from its
  source takes the source's texels in the copy's own layout; the layout check is
  [lightmap_texels.py](../tools/bake/lightmap_texels.py) `moved_rect` (the same rectangle, moved by whole texels).
- [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py): a relight that writes no texture cache, or one no texture names, is "its
  lightmaps inside the map, none moved" (`lightingInside` with 0 textures); `lightingInside.held` and a log line say
  what the map holds of lightmaps ([lighting_size.py](../tools/bake/lighting_size.py) `inside`), with a warning
  from 100 MB (decision D4: the game loads them with the map and keeps them in memory for the battle).
- [lighting_size.py](../tools/bake/lighting_size.py), new: a map's lighting textures, who reads each, its box and
  what it would weigh at that size (`--list`, `--json`).
- [research/evidence/lighting-texture-survey.py](../research/evidence/lighting-texture-survey.py), new, with its
  result: the game's 18,906 lightmaps and shadow maps in 138 maps, the small ones' properties and mip chains.
- The folders (KB-16): [folder_scrub.py](../tools/viewer/folder_scrub.py), new, holds the scrubber the pack export
  used (moved from manager.py) and a guard for folders it was not told of: a drive's or share's path becomes
  `<folder>`, the name after Users or home `<user>`, and the export's answer says so
  ([manager.py](../tools/viewer/manager.py)). The build folder's own `manifest.json` now names folders by
  placeholders too (`<builds>`, `<projects>`, `<install>`, `<cache>`, `<temp>`, `<home>`); the record with the real
  folders is the work folder's `build-log.json` and what the Build returns (decision D5).
  [profile_build.py](../tools/bake/profile_build.py) reads `<builds>` as the package's own builds folder.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md): rows for the sized lighting textures and the folder scrubber.
- [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md): KB-15 out; KB-16 in until a release carries the folder fix (a 0.6.0 pack's
  `packages\<map>\manifest.json` names the maker's folders: delete it from the zip, nothing reads it).
- Release notes: a map built before keeps its size until it is built again, and a pack until it is exported again.

Checked: the bake suite (896 tests; `test_lighting_size` new: the mip chains read off the game's, the box rule,
every record of URB_Bar and of the intro map's non-square atlases moved exactly, sized textures read back by the
audit reader, the writer editing one in place with no cache; `test_native_copy`'s copy with its own lighting reads
its source's texels over its rectangle and ring; `test_frac_walls` on the new layout), the editor's `test_build`
(nothing to move, the size warning, the scrubbed manifest), the viewer's `test_pack_export` (the guard). The reported
project built on main and on this branch: 340.8 MB against 55.8 MB, its lightmaps inside 306 MB against 23.6 MB;
every one of its 166 copies' lightmap rectangles with their ring (332 textures, 1.9 million texels) and shadow maps
(140, 0.9 million texels) the same texel for texel, the map's 137 own lighting textures byte for byte. URB_Bar with
five copies the same way (796,800 and 303,252 texels, 234 textures). build_outputs.py: every package file of its 11
inputs byte for byte as before; the manifests differ by their placeholders, the new tool's hash and, where the
stand-in relight writes no cache, "inside, none moved".

Known gaps: a copy's lower mips are made from its own texels, not the atlas's. Compressed storage was left out
(decision D3).

### Diagonal cover kept under a change and carried by copied corners: the Build writes whole tiles

Stages D2 and D3 of the diagonal cover plan. A slanted corner's diagonal cover now survives an edit on its own tile,
and a copied or moved slanted wall brings it along.

- [diagonal_keep.py](../tools/bake/diagonal_keep.py) has three new parts:
  - `plan_whole` works a tile out whole as the game's full build would: passes 1 and 2, the link step and the
    ladders' links (tile_build, tile_rule, tile_links), with the tiles round it as the battle will have them.
  - `find_new` finds the new corners.
  - `refit` makes any rebuild volume that would reach a new corner as several that do not, in its place in the
    level's list.

  `write` takes the tiles under a change (`whole`) and the candidates for new corners beside the tiles next to one,
  and its record gains `whole` (with `newCorner`: `carried` or `found`) and `refitted`. It writes nothing, and the
  manifest has no `diagonalCover`, when there is nothing to write.
- [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py):
  - `rebuild_spares` keeps every seeded tile in a changed box out of the rebuild, and names the ones a change stands
    on in the volume's `diagonalWhole`.
  - `diagonal_candidates` says where a new piece may make a corner. A copy of one of the map's own pieces carries the
    map's marks: a tile it stands on whose place on the original had diagonal cover gets it where a diagonal still
    gives cover. A made piece or a cover block ([cover_blocks.py](../tools/bake/cover_blocks.py)) gets the corners
    the finder takes.
  - The Build's log names the new corners.
- The editor:
  - The compiler's `diagonal-cover-taken` warning is now the note `diagonal-cover-rewritten`
    ([floor_edits.py](../tools/editor/floor_edits.py)).
  - View options' Diagonal cover draws a corner under a change blue instead of red
    ([view_layout.js](../tools/viewer/web/view_layout.js), [cutaway.js](../tools/viewer/web/cutaway.js)), and
    its tooltip and the guide's paragraph ([guide.html](../tools/release/guide/guide.html)) say what the Build does.
- [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md): KB-14 ("An edit on a slanted corner takes its diagonal cover") is taken out
  with this fix.
- [findings-register.md](../research/findings-register.md): F-155, and F-149 and F-153 updated. ARCHITECTURE.md's
  tile build row names the new parts.

Checked:

### A build keeps a map's diagonal cover away from its edits, and reads a rebuild volume's reach as the game does

A built map lost the cover a unit gets in the corner of a slanted wall (the UFO maps, the Chryssalid hive): the
battle's tile rebuild clears a tile's diagonal cover for good (F-149), and a build's rebuild volumes reached every
tile of a map with a larger grid and, on many maps, tens of tiles round any edit. The second half was not known: the
Build took a volume's reach to be its box's diagonal, where the game takes its brush's sphere times its largest scale
(F-150, found when the first version of this fix failed in the game).

  `fit`, the cubes that take a box of tiles and none of a set of forbidden ones (`pose`: a cube's centre and radius).

  - `volume_sphere` reads a volume's sphere as the game does (`brush_sphere` times the largest scale), so
    `rebuild_order` and `ladder_order` read the battle's real work; `box_reach` is the radius of a template's clone
    over a box, `reach_box` the box that gives a wanted radius.
  - `diagonal_tiles` (the map's baked tiles with COVER_Diagonal) and `rebuild_spares` (what a volume must leave
    alone: every diagonal tile its own box does not hold, with the two tiles over it).
  - `add_rebuild_volume` makes a volume that would reach one of those as several fitted ones, the first its
    `export`; `add_to_level` lists the others after it. The record gains `fitted` (the volumes, the tiles spared),
    and `diagonalRebuilt` for diagonal tiles inside the box, which are rebuilt; the Build's log says both

  - `tile_volume` (a ladder copy's top tile) is placed by its sphere: radius 24 whatever the template's shape,
    where a flat template gave it 119 and three tiles by three.
  - A volume that reaches no diagonal tile is made as before, so a build of a map without diagonal cover, or of an
    edit far from it, is unchanged but for a ladder's tile volume.

### A built map's lost diagonal cover: the cause found and recorded (F-149, KB-14)

A user reported that maps saved in the editor lose diagonal cover (a unit in the corner of a slanted wall, on the UFO
maps). The cause: the game writes that cover flag only in a map's full build, from its cover seed actors, and the tile
rebuild a battle runs for each rebuild volume clears a tile and never reads the seeds; a build's rebuild volumes reach
every tile of a grown map and a few tiles round every other edit. Nothing in the tools changes here: the fix is not
built.

- [findings-register.md](../research/findings-register.md): F-149, with where the game has diagonal cover, which
  edits take it, what the game showed and a fix to try.
- [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md): KB-14.
- [diagonal-cover.py](../research/evidence/diagonal-cover.py): a read-only script. `maps` lists a map's cover
  seeds, its baked diagonal tiles and the rebuild volumes that reach them; `save` sets a tactical save's static and
  cover flags beside the map's bake.
  [diagonal-cover-2026-11-22.json](../research/evidence/diagonal-cover-2026-11-22.json) is its reading of the 26
  maps of the install that hold a cover seed.
- [cover-build.md](../research/native/cover-build.md) and
  [cover-and-sight.md](../research/native/cover-and-sight.md): a rebuilt diagonal tile got no cover in the game,
  where the reading expected straight cover.

Checked: the script run over the 26 maps, two builds of CSmallScout_Farm and two saves; a hidden game run of a grown
CSmallScout_Farm (LWR), whose save at turn 1 has none of the map's 8 diagonal tiles with any cover, and a soldier
put on two of them (teleported, then walked there) read no cover. The `repo` suite.

Known gaps: why the rebuild's straight cover test finds nothing on those tiles is not read; plain Enemy Within was
not played (the code read is the exe both share).

The editor's install and Play in game steps, the lab installer and the deploy tool refused whenever any `XComEW.exe`
ran, so with the user playing one copy nothing could be staged into another (the lab copy) for a hidden run (T-52).
They now ask whether the game of the install they change is running, told by the folder of its exe; a game whose
exe's path can't be read still counts as running.

  exe lies in that folder.

  [play.py](../tools/viewer/play.py) (the watch for the game a play started) and

  say so.

## 21 November 2026

### A made ramp's mapped slope takes its texture in its own plane

A made ground ramp's sloped top was mapped as if projected from above, so a repeat of 64 drew about 67.5 long up a
slope rising 100 over 300 (1 / cos of its angle), and the Texture mapping fold's handles worked on that projection. The
slope is now mapped in its own plane, in the generator and on the page alike:

- The rule ([uv_mapping.py](../tools/bake/uv_mapping.py) `along_slope`, `slope_extent`, written in its docstring):
  a point of the slope is at a = x0 plus its distance up the slope from the low edge, b = y; the slope's extent runs
  from x0 to x0 plus its length. Its low edge keeps a = x0, where a flat top beside it has it too.
- Aligned to the world: the frame's place is added as on any top (a + its x, b + its y), so the pattern lines up with
  the world's, and with a flat top's aligned to it, along the low edge, and runs up the slope by its true length from
  there; at the high edge it no longer meets a flat top's (the slope is longer than its run).
- [ground.py](../tools/bake/ground.py) `faces_of` maps a free ramp's slope by it when its mapping lists the top.
  The look's own texture (no mapping) stays projected from above, as the donor's top is; a rock's faces stay projected
  too; a ramp steeper than 60 degrees has its slope among its sides, as before.
- The page's twin ([made_mapping.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_mapping.js)): `surfacePlane` gives the ramp's top a
  unit axis up the slope (its origin where a = 0), `surfaceExtent` the slope's run up it, and `surfaceAt` now reads a
  point's place from the plane itself (its signature is `(plane, p)`;
  [made_mapping_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_mapping_wiring.js)'s drags and test hooks hand it the plane),
  so the blue dot, ring and white dot sit and drag on the slope, a unit of the surface a unit up it.
- Shared cases: [slope_mapping_cases.json](../tools/bake/tests/slope_mapping_cases.json) (four ramps and mappings:
  a repeat's size, a fit, a turned and flipped count, one aligned to the world from x0 96 at z0 -20), read by
  [test_texture_mapping.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_texture_mapping.py) (the places, the extent, the rule, and the
  built slope's corners) and [shared_cases_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/shared_cases_test.mjs).
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)'s texture mapping row names the case file.

Checked: test_texture_mapping.py (the ramp's slope under a 30-degree fit over the slope's extent, a repeat of 50 up
the slope, the shared cases; free numbers without a mapping still byte for byte with their digests) and the bake
suite; made_mapping_test.mjs (the slope's plane, normal, extent, its low and high edges, a point and back) and the
shared cases; the `texture-mapping` browser check's new ramp part (the blue dot on the slope, 100 of the surface 100
up it, the slope's extent its length, the pattern slid along it), `rock-corner`, `free-handles`, `api-names`; against
`04b9ee4`, the commit the branch started from, with this work order's three changes in: the quick and baked Builds of
build_outputs.py's 11 inputs the same (none maps a ramp), and every compile of the editor suite (compile_record.py)
the same but the three of the new atlas-note test.

Known gaps: a ramp with no mapping still draws its look's texture projected from above, stretched up a steep slope (the
donor's own top is mapped that way, and the look is the donor's); a slope steeper than 60 degrees is mapped as a side
(b up the height, stretched by 1 / sin of its angle). Rocks keep their projection.

### The Texture mapping fold says a pattern's real size where the material's own tiling is known

A repeat is one unit of a mesh's texture coordinates, and a material may multiply them itself: a building material's
TileXY of 1.25 draws its texture 1.25 times in each, so a repeat of 192 shows the pattern every 153.6. The map's
export records that multiplier in a material's `render.uv.scale` where it reads one (a texture coordinate node's
tiling, or a building material's TileXY: [materials.py](../tools/viewer/materials.py) `profile`), and the page
already draws by it; it doesn't say where it found nothing to read. The fold now uses what the export has, without a
new export:

- [made_mapping.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_mapping.js) `materialTiling`: a material's multiplier and whether it
  is known (a scale other than 1, or a family whose tiling scalar the export reads, BLDG_Enterable, at 1 too; not a
  material whose coordinates go through a node the export can't follow, nor one it read nothing of, whose 1 is only
  the default). `surfaceSlots`: the slots a surface draws in, from its look's catalogue entry (a wall's picked side's);
  every drawn material of the piece where its look is in no catalogue. `patternSize`: on a mapped surface whose
  materials are all known and scale alike, the note "Its material repeats its texture 2 times in each repeat: the
  pattern shows every 96" (in counts: "3.75 by 2.5 times over the surface"; one axis each way: "every 48 along U and 3
  times along V").
- [made_mapping_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_mapping_wiring.js): the note under the modes; where a material
  of the surface isn't known, the Repeat row's tooltip (`texRepeat` in [index.html](../tools/viewer/web/index.html))
  says its material may scale its texture itself, which the export doesn't record, so the pattern may repeat more
  often than a repeat.
- One rule on both sides through [material_tiling_cases.json](../tools/viewer/tests/material_tiling_cases.json):
  `materials.profile` gives each case's uv ([test_materials_and_floors.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_materials_and_floors.py)),
  `materialTiling` reads it known or not ([shared_cases_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/shared_cases_test.mjs)).

What it finds (the 2,408 materials of the 35 cached exports): the export read a multiplier for the building materials
alone (97 with TileXY: 86 at 1, 10 at 1.25, 1 at 1.2); no texture coordinate node's tiling was read anywhere (cooked
materials keep few expressions). Of the walls' catalogue, 114 looks' faces draw in a material at 1.25 or 1.2 (their
pattern's size is said) and 101 at a known 1; slabs (BLDG_Floors) and nearly all ground materials are not known.

Checked: [made_mapping_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/made_mapping_test.mjs) (the words in each mode, nothing for
an unscaled, unmapped or mixed surface, not known when any material isn't, the slots); the shared cases both sides;
the `texture-mapping` browser check (a wall's materials recorded at twice say the pattern is 96, at an unread 1 the
Repeat row says it may scale), `api-names`; web_names clean.

Known gaps: an export change would add what this can't show: whether a material's multiplier was read at all (a
`known` beside `render.uv`, so a read 1 and the default 1 differ for every family), and the tiling scalars other
families carry and the export doesn't apply (RoadAndSidewalk_Material's and Basic_Material's TileU, TileV and TileUV,
PROP_Objects_Tile's TileX and TileY, HQ_Props' Tile U and Tile V, ENV_Terrain's Tile, ENV_ForestGround's Rock_Tile,
M_Alien_Machinery's Tiling), each needing its shader's use of them confirmed, and materials that project by the world
(none recognised). It would raise `EXPORT_VERSION`, which this change does not.

### Looks that draw a part of a larger texture: said in the Texture mapping fold and noted by the compiler

Some looks draw a window of a larger texture (an atlas): the subway car roof's top is the top half of its texture and
its underside the bottom half, a supply ship crate's walls a small corner of theirs. Size, Fit and Count map the whole
texture, so on such a surface they show its other parts. Each catalogued look now says, per surface a mapping takes
(a wall's faces side by side, a slab's top and underside, a ground look's top and sides), whether its texture tiles,
worked out where the catalogue is served from the recipe's planar maps over the donor face's extent; no catalogue was
rewritten and no map read again.

- The rule ([looks.py](../tools/bake/looks.py) `tiling`, `surfaces`, in each row of `listing` as `surfaces`): along
  each axis the texture tiles where the face's coordinates run over a whole repeat or across a repeat's edge; where
  they stay inside one repeat, it tiles when the surface's two repeats are square (within a tenth: a texture laid by
  the world on a face narrower than its repeat) and is a part of a larger one when they are not (an unwrap fitted to a
  window) or when the coordinate doesn't change. On the checked-in catalogues: 22 wall faces of 17 looks, 8 slab
  surfaces of 6 looks and the tops of 32 of the 193 ground looks. Named atlases it finds: the subway car and engine
  roofs (top and underside), the subway engine's inner wall, the supply crate's walls, the UFO's outer walls (side B),
  the EXALT holo-globe wall, the HQ assault walls, the vault wall's strip, the flat roof corner trims, a cemetery roof's
  constant underside. Named tiling textures it keeps tiling, which the span alone would have called windows: the
  construction kit's core floors (88 across a 192 tile), its facades (168 of 192 up), its joint strips (52 up), the
  low stone walls, the truck stop's skylight walls, the police station's walls, the fishing shack's roof.
- A wall look's side with no face (its outline all trims, which a mapping doesn't take) is `None`: 71 faces of 50
  looks, both sides on 21. The faces' slots per side are listed, for a face of several materials up the wall.
- The fold ([made_mapping.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_mapping.js) `lookSurface`, `textureNotes`;
  [made_mapping_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_mapping_wiring.js); `texNotes` in
  [index.html](../tools/viewer/web/index.html)): once a surface is mapped, "This look draws a part of a larger
  texture (an atlas) on its top: mapped, the whole texture repeats there, its other parts with it" (a wall's: on this
  face, its other face or both); before any mode, a wall look's side with no face ("the mapping takes this side
  alone", or no faces at all); once mapped, a wall's faces in several materials up it (plan item 5.3: a picture across
  the wall needs a look with one face material). Nothing is disabled.
- Size's first repeat for a catalogued wall look is now its faces' measured repeat (side A's, else side B's;
  `lookRepeat`), as it was for slabs; 192 for a look no catalogue holds, as before.
- The compiler notes a mapped surface its look draws from an atlas (`mapped-atlas`, a note: nothing goes wrong in the
  game; [made_edits.py](../tools/editor/made_edits.py) through `looks.mapped_windows`).
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)'s texture mapping row and [UI-GUIDELINES.md](../UI-GUIDELINES.md)'s
  texture paragraph say so.

Checked: [test_looks.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_looks.py) (the rule along each axis, a wall's side with no face
and each slot over its band, the catalogues' named atlases and tiling textures, the mapped windows);
[test_compiler_free.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_compiler_free.py) (the subway roof's mapped top noted, the core
floor's not, nothing warned); [made_mapping_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/made_mapping_test.mjs) (the notes on a
stubbed catalogue, the walls' first repeat); the `texture-mapping` browser check (a roof in the subway look says so
once mapped and not in Original, a wall in the UFO doorway's look says it has no faces), `looks`, `walls` and
`api-names` on a test server; web_names clean.

Known gaps: the rule reads geometry, not the texture's pixels, so it can be wrong both ways: the Road House's walls (7
faces, a texture painted for the wall's height, non-square) are called windows along their height, which is right for

and turn gizmo stayed, over the texture handles. Now every other control steps aside while the fold is open on the
piece handled: the gizmo is held aside (in move and turn mode alike), and a rock's picked corner is let go with its
arrows. They come back once the fold is shut or another piece is picked.

### The generators apply a made piece's texture mapping to its main faces

A free-form wall, slab or ground shape whose numbers carry a texture `mapping` (the custom geometry improvements plan,
section 5, decision D8: the main faces first) now draws those faces with it; until now the generators took the mapping
and built as without it.

- **Which faces.** A wall's two faces (`faces`: its outline's strips that are faces, on both sides), a slab's `top` and
  `underside`, a ground shape's `top` (a ramp's slope and a rock's faces turned more up than aside, projected straight
  down as the look's own texture is) and `sides`. Trims, caps, ends, gaps' sides, a slab's edges and the faces inside
  keep their look's texture. A look whose outline has no face strip (the UFOs' walls, one unwrap of the whole outline)
  has nothing to map on that side.
- **Where on the pattern.** Each corner at its place on the surface's axes in the whole logical piece's frame (a
  wall: along it and up it; a slab or a ground top: x and y; a ground side: x or y along it and up), over the whole
  surface's extent: a split wall's or slab's piece reads both from its `whole` (`frac_wall.whole_origin` and the new
  `face_extent`, `slab_cells.origin` and the new `slab_cells.extent`), so a fit or a count goes on across the cuts and
  the stacked pieces or bands; a ground shape's is its box.
- **World alignment.** `mappingOrigin` beside `mapping`: {role: [a0, b0] on the role's axes or [x, y, z] on the
  frame's} (a ground side takes [x, y, z] only), read for a surface with `world`; absent, (0, 0). A split piece carries
  its whole's.
- **The image the right way round.** The mesh's v runs down the image, so the faces write the rule's (U, -V); a wall's
  side B, a slab's underside and the ground sides whose axis runs left seen from outside write -U: the mirror through
  the piece, as the game's donors' own textures are, so an unturned mapping reads the image as the look does and one
  offset keeps both faces of a wall in place.
- **Before the tangents, after the lightmap.** The coordinates go into UV channel 0 before the tangents are worked out
  from them (a turned mapping turns them), then through `free_form.held` (whole repeats taken off, the phase kept; a
  face spanning too many repeats is refused with 'half-floats'). The lightmap's channel, the vertex paint, the slots
  and the geometry are as without a mapping.
- **The rule turns before it scales.** uv_mapping.uv scaled a point to repeats and then turned it, which sheared a
  turned pattern whose u and v differ (a 96 by 48 repeat turned 30 degrees drew as an 87 by 64 parallelogram). It now
  turns the point, scales it along the turned axes (a count or a fit over the run of the surface's corners along each,
  so a quarter turn fits the turned image exactly), mirrors and slides it. Unturned results are the same.
- **Checked numbers.** `free_form.mapping` checks the mapping's shape (`uv_mapping.check`) and `mappingOrigin`
  (`uv_mapping.check_origin`) for every generator, code 'mapping'.

### Free-form made walls and slabs cut into pieces at any size

The splitter cuts made walls and slabs whose numbers hold `free: 1` (the custom geometry improvements plan, stage 2)
into pieces the game takes, at any size; numbers of the old form are cut as before.

- **Along.** At tile edges counted from the frame's origin, at most 16 tiles apart, each as far along as it goes
  outside every opening or hole; the last piece whatever is left, fractions and all. A tail under 48 units (one its own
  end or its fracture would eat) shares the cut before it, which moves back a tile.
- **Up (walls).** By the wall's `tall`: 'repeat' stacks its look's height while a storey of the look or more would be
  left over one more, the top piece the rest (lengthened or shortened, no sliver); 'stretch' is one piece up to twice
  its look's height, else bands of equal height no taller than the look, each a `band` [lo, hi] of the one stretched
  outline (the wall generator builds the window). The look's own height and storeys are asked of the look alone.
- **Every piece** keeps the whole's seed, its free numbers (`free`, `y0`, `y1`, `z0`, `z1`, `look`, `mapping`, ...),
  its openings or holes cut to it and moved into it, and `whole`: a wall's [its place along, the whole's length, its
  place up, the whole's height, the whole's x0], a slab's [its place along x, along y, the whole's width, depth, the
  whole's x0, y0], so a generator reads where the piece stands in the whole's frame (its lattice and its texture go on
  across the cuts). A piece an opening takes whole is no piece; a slab's piece is kept where the slab generator finds
  some of it left (`slab_cells.FreeSlab`, its holes snapped), or by the holes' own edges where its look is a donor not
  resolved here (`free_left`, which `slab_left` uses for free numbers).

### Made walls build from free numbers: any size, thickness and height, leaning ends

The wall generator builds a wall whose numbers hold `free: 1` (the custom geometry improvements plan, stage 2, its
request's free form) at any size, by the general path whatever its look; numbers of the old form build byte for byte
as before.

- **Extents.** `x0 < x1` any finite values; `y0 < y1` its faces: each side of the look's outline moves with its face,
  so a trim stands as proud of it as it did, and the collision across moves with them; `z0 < z1` its bottom and top:
  the outline is raised to `z0`, then the height it lacks goes into (or what it has too much comes out of) its longest
  stretch upright on both sides at once, the bands under and over it keeping their sizes, else every height is scaled.
  `storey_cut` and `lowered` learnt to put height in. The Bar look is written as a measured look (`as_measured`), so
  every free wall takes the one path. A raised wall's faces keep their pattern on them (`uvShiftZ`).
- **Bands.** `band: [lo, hi]` makes the window lo..hi of the stretched outline: no bottom trims when lo is over the
  bottom, no top trims when hi is under the top, each cut strip's texture going on as on the whole.
- **Cells.** One seed in each lattice cell of the look's cell size counted from the frame's origin (the whole wall's,
  for a piece: `whole` [dx, length, dz, height, the whole's x0]), placed in it by a hash of the seed and the cell's
  place: dragging an end changes only the cells near it.
- **Ends.** Each end a style measured from the wall's own x0 or x1 ('free', 'line', 'through': half the faces'
  distance) or `{inset, lean}`: the end's plane stands `inset` in and leans `lean` along the wall for each unit
  across (the end at y across at its place plus lean times y, y from the frame's line; clamped at a 30-degree
  corner's lean). A leaning end's cells are a column of bands, so nothing but the end lies within its reach; its
  corners then move along the wall, the faces' texture read at the moved place, the charts grown to hold them, and its
  collision box becomes a hull. A gap within a leaning end's reach is refused unless cut through to the end.
- **Gaps** anywhere inside, reaching an end or not; `mapping` taken and not used yet (stage 4); each face's texture
  coordinates held near 0 in whole repeats (`free_form.held`).
- **Checks.** `check_free` refuses with a `free_form.NumbersError` and its code: 'free', 'number', 'extent', 'mapping',
  'tall', 'band', 'whole', 'opening', 'ends', 'thickness' (faces that would leave the look's outline crossing itself),
  'lean'. A size is never changed to fit. `solid_box` gives the box a free wall's solid stands in, its leaning ends'
  reach included.

`free_shape`), [frac_wall.py](../tools/bake/frac_wall.py) (the block "the free form": `check_free`,
`free_shaped`, `free_ends`, `free_seeds`, `lean_ends`, `solid_box`; `solids` makes the hulls; 1,568 lines, a little
past the guideline: the next change lists it in ARCHITECTURE.md).

### Made floors, roofs and ground build from free numbers

The slab and ground generators take the free form of the custom geometry improvements plan (stage 2, section 10.2):
numbers holding `free: 1` give a piece's box in finite game units in its own frame, any size, with no whole tiles and
no tile minimum. Old numbers never hold `free` and build byte for byte as before. Nothing calls the free form yet: the
request versions, the splitter, the compiler and the page come in their own changes.

- **Slabs** ([frac_slab.py](../tools/bake/frac_slab.py), [slab_cells.py](../tools/bake/slab_cells.py), new):
  - Footprint and plate: any `x0 < x1`, `y0 < y1` (a slab under a tile included, off the tile edges), and the plate
    between `z0` (underside) and `z1` (top).
  - Holes: rectangles anywhere inside the footprint, overlapping or not.
  - Fragments: the look's tile lattice is counted from the frame's origin (a split piece reads it from its `whole`
    place, with the whole's corner as two more numbers where it is not the origin). Each cell is cut by the footprint
    and the holes into convex rectangles; each connected group is one fragment. A whole cell's pattern (tile, diagonal
    halves or a two-cell piece) comes from a hash of (seed, i, j), with pairs at fixed lattice places. A size change
    therefore re-rolls only the cells near the cut, and the old slabs' fragments a tile for the same look stay within
    a few per cent. A cut piece thinner than 8 units joins its neighbour. Every polygon has a corner at each other
    polygon's corner on its sides.
  - Collision: boxes over exactly the solid area, kept at the look's distances from the plate's bottom and top (a
    roof thickened keeps its collision's top 2 under its drawn top, with the bottom on the underside), or the whole
    plate where that leaves none.
  - Texture and paint are read in the whole slab's frame as before. Each face's coordinates are held near 0 in whole
    repeats.
  - One piece is at most 17 of its look's tiles each way (`CHUNK`, the splitter's chunk and a tail).
  - `check_free` checks free numbers, and `local_box` gives their box.
- **Ground** ([ground.py](../tools/bake/ground.py)): any `x0 < x1`, `y0 < y1`, `z0 < z1` (a patch's plate, a block's
  bottom and top, a ramp rising from `z0` at `x0` to `z1` at `x1`, a rock's bottom and top, its points within that
  box). There is no 64-tile or 384-unit cap. Each face's texture coordinates are held near 0 in whole repeats. A face
  that would still reach 1,024 repeats from 0 is refused, since a half float keeps no place within a repeat past that.
  For a look of 320 units a repeat (the default) that means up to about 655,000 units a side or high. For the
  catalogue's smallest repeat (24.6 units) it is about 50,000 units. `check_free` and `local_box` work as for slabs.
- **Shared** ([free_form.py](../tools/bake/free_form.py), new): what is free, extents checked without changing them,
  the texture-coordinate hold, and `NumbersError`. That is a ValueError with a code (`extent`, `hole`, `left`,
  `chunk`, `half-floats` and others) beside its reason. `mapping` and `plain` are accepted and not read (stage 4 and
  the editor).
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) section 2 gains the free form's row.

### Tilted or turned made floors, roofs and ground build as drawn, with what is not made for them said

A made floor, roof or ground shape pitched or rolled builds as drawn (the custom geometry improvements plan, decision
D6, its default) and the Build warns once per piece of what is not made for it: a floor's or roof's cursor floor is the
box round it, so the cursor may not land on it where it slopes; past about 10 degrees a unit on it gets no cover (F-81),
past 45 it is no floor to stand on. A floor or roof turned about the vertical off the quarter turns is warned that its
cursor floor is the box round it, so at its corners the cursor may land beside it. A free-form piece no longer gets its
template's off-grid warning: it is drawn to stand anywhere at any angle, and the Build seeds and rebuilds the tiles
over its box and makes its fracture columns where it stands.

- [made_edits.py](../tools/editor/made_edits.py) `made_tilted`, run by [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py)
  after the cursor floors; `add` leaves a free-form piece out of `single_grid_rule`.

Checked: [test_compiler_free.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_compiler_free.py) (a pitched slab, a slab turned off
the quarter turns, one on a quarter turn, a rolled block; no off-grid warning for free-form pieces) and the editor suite.

Known gaps: a turned slab's own turned cursor volume (the plan's first try, 4.6) needs a game run; until then its cursor
floor is its box, as the warning says.

### Free-form walls meet at any angle: mitred corners, stems that lean

Where two free-form made walls meet, their ends are now worked out at any angle (the custom geometry improvements plan,
4.7, decisions D7 and D10 on their defaults): two ends within a unit of each other are each cut on the one upright
plane through the corner, from where the inner faces cross to where the outer faces cross, right angles too; two ends
in line meet end to end; an end on another wall's line between its ends stops against that wall's near face, leaning
along it, as ends do against a pair in line. Under 30 degrees, or three or more ends at a point with no two in line,
ends meet square. An end goes to the Build as `{inset, lean}`: how far in from the wall's own end its solid stops, and
how far its plane leans along the wall for each unit across. A free-form wall meeting a wall of an older version keeps
today's rule. The angle is the rounded rotator's on both sides.

- [made_edits.py](../tools/editor/made_edits.py): `free_wall_joins`, `made_wall_joins` (the free-form walls among
  themselves, every other end by `wall_joins`), `join_made_walls` putting leaning ends into the request and the box.
- [walls.js](../tools/viewer/web/walls.js): the twins `freeWallJoins`, `madeWallJoins`; `joinWords` says "a
  mitred corner"; [made_handles.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_handles.js) `refreshJoins` uses `madeWallJoins`.
- [free_join_cases.json](../tools/editor/tests/free_join_cases.json) (new): 17 cases both sides pass (right angles,

  pair with a stem, three ends, under 30 degrees, a storey apart, a fractional corner off the axes, a start off the
  origin).

Checked: [test_compiler_free.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_compiler_free.py) (the cases, a mitre worked by hand,
an older wall's rule kept, mitred walls' ends in the Build request) and

### Align to grid, level and game pose in place of Level snap and the recipe snap

Two snaps that were not steps of the snap setting are now commands, and a piece can be brought onto the grid without
typing (the custom geometry improvements plan, section 3, decisions D4, D5, D11 and D12, their defaults):

- **Align to grid** (L, or the piece panel's Align section): the selection's pivot moves to the nearest multiple of
  the snap setting's steps from the tile grid's corner and lowest level, and turns to whole angular steps; with snap
  off, to the nearest tile corner, level and quarter turn. One undo step. `gizmo.js` `alignToGrid`.
- **Align to level** replaces Level snap (the rail's L button and its key): a floor piece was kept to whole levels
  when placed and moved; it is now placed and moved as any piece, and Level (shown for a floor piece) moves it to its
  height in its map moved by whole levels, the nearest; a copy goes by its original's height. `align.js`
  `alignToLevel`, [floors.js](../tools/viewer/web/floors.js) `nearestLevel`,
  [level_snap.js](../tools/viewer/web/level_snap.js) `floorBaseOf`.
- **Align to game pose** replaces the recipe snap: under tile snap a ladder, door, car, van or fracturing piece was
  pulled onto its pose rule; it now steps as any piece does (so one on its rule stays on it), and Game pose (shown for
  such a piece) puts it at the nearest pose its rule allows. The snap button's R and the Recipe snap chip go; the Off
  the grid chip says to use Game pose. A prefab with such a piece is placed under the snap setting, and only a prefab
  with a building still goes by whole tiles. `gizmo.js` `alignToGamePose`,
  [selection.js](../tools/viewer/web/selection.js), [prefab_place.js](../tools/viewer/web/prefab_place.js),
  [clipboard.js](../tools/viewer/web/clipboard.js).
- The **Align section** shows for one piece too, with its Align to row (Grid, Level, Game pose); with two or more it
  keeps its target, axes and Align button. [align.js](../tools/viewer/web/align.js),
  [index.html](../tools/viewer/web/index.html), [style.css](../tools/viewer/web/style.css).
- A **typed pose** with snap on is taken as a move or turn from where the piece stands in the snap setting's steps,
  said in the hint line while it is typed; with snap off, as typed. [snap_steps.js](../tools/viewer/web/snap_steps.js)
  `typedStep`, [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js).
- The prefab builder's Align to grid is renamed **Align prefab to grid** (D11).
- The help panel's keys, the test hooks (`alignToGrid`, `alignToLevel`, `alignToGamePose` in place of `levelSnap`,
  `setLevelSnap`) and ARCHITECTURE.md's rows say the same.

Checked: node tests (snap_steps_test, floor_rules_test), `web_names`, the viewer and repo suites, and the browser checks
`api-names`, `typed-pose`, `pivot`, `recipe` (rewritten: off the grid, Game pose, tile snap's typed steps), `adding`,
`groups`, `copy-drag`, `clear-map`, `align`, `cover` (tile snap's levels of 64), `floor-placing` (rewritten: placed as
any piece, then Level) on the Bar, and `walls`, `made-openings`, `rock-corner`, `room-buttons` on the police station,

the L button; it is brought level, pictures too, in the plan's guide pass. The Build gains no note for a floor piece
off its levels: no run has shown what the game does with one, so it would be a guess.

### Snap steps count from where a drag started, and snap off is smooth everywhere

The snap setting now means one thing on each of these paths: snap off moves without rounding, to fractions of a unit;
fine moves in steps of 24 and tile by whole tiles across and levels of 64 up, each counted on the distance moved, so a
piece, a face or a gap off the grid keeps its offset (the custom geometry improvements plan, section 3).

- The gizmo's fine snap stepped by rounding the pivot to multiples of 24 from the world's middle, pulling a piece off
  the grid onto it; it now steps from where the drag started, as tile snap did. With the piece's own axes shown
  (local space) a move steps along them. A building's box still moves by whole tiles and levels.
  [gizmo.js](../tools/viewer/web/gizmo.js)
- A gap's handles moved by whole units with snap off and in steps of 24 up under tile snap; they now move smoothly with
  snap off and in levels of 64 under tile snap, and a side or top steps the distance it is dragged rather than landing
  on multiples of the step. Alt stays steps of 8. [walls.js](../tools/viewer/web/walls.js) `movedOpening`,
  [made_handles.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_handles.js).
- A cover block's or invisible floor's faces moved by whole units with snap off, sized to multiples of the step under
  fine and tile, and stepped heights by 96 from the type's first top under tile snap. They now move smoothly with snap
  off, step the distance dragged under fine and tile, and step heights in levels of 64 under tile snap.
  [cover.js](../tools/viewer/web/cover.js) `resizedCover`, [cover_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/cover_wiring.js).
- A piece placed or pasted under fine snap was rounded to multiples of 24 from the world's middle; it now moves from
  where the piece stands in the map in steps of 24, as tile snap moves it in whole tiles.
  [clipboard.js](../tools/viewer/web/clipboard.js), [snap_steps.js](../tools/viewer/web/snap_steps.js)
  `droppedAcross`.
- The handles' hints name the steps from the one table (`moveWords`, `stepWords`).

Checked: node tests [snap_steps_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/snap_steps_test.mjs),
[walls_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/walls_test.mjs) and [cover_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/cover_test.mjs)
(new cases for snap off and for stepped distances, which failed before), `web_names`. The browser checks follow with
the align commands.

### Landing zones move as the snap setting says

A landing zone's gizmo moved it only by whole tiles across and storeys up, and a zone placed from the Add panel
stood on a tile, whatever the snap setting. At the user's word they now follow it, as the editor's other moves do:
smoothly with snap off, in steps of 24 units with fine snap, by whole tiles across and storeys up with tile snap.
Turning stays quarter turns whatever the snap: a zone faces north, east, south or west, the only ways Long War's lines
and the game's landing take, and the gizmo's hint says so.

  snap; where clicked with snap off). `draggedHeight` no longer pulls a zone moved under the grid back onto it (the
  compiler warns of a zone outside the grid); only a zone saved under the grid still comes onto it with its first

  the step.

([browser_smoke.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_smoke.py)) drags the zone under tile snap (whole tiles, height

### A landing zone dragged keeps its own height

The landing zone gizmo's first move put a zone's ground onto a level of the map's tile grid, counted from the grid's
box. That assumed every map's floors and LWR's lines stand on a level's start. On the police station they do not:
its floors, its own landing and LWR's lines there stand at 0, 48 over the grid's first level (-48). So moving the
police station's landing zone sideways lifted it 16, and with it the drop zone frame and the Skyranger carried along,
which would stand 16 over the asphalt in a Build. The `clear-map` browser check stopped there on the police station.

- [spawns.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawns.js) `draggedHeight`: a zone dragged keeps its own height, moved by
  whole storeys; only a zone saved under the grid (an old project's tutorial zone, 16 under it, which the rule was
  made for) comes onto the grid's nearest level. [zones_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/zones_wiring.js)' gizmo
  uses it.

Checked: node cases in [clear_map_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/clear_map_test.mjs) (the police station's
height kept, storeys up and down, under the grid onto its first level, the tutorial's old zone). On a test server
the browser check `clear-map` passes on the police station (it stopped at the drag before), the Bar and TempleShip;
`spawns`, `reset-all`, `effects` and `grid-panel` pass on the Bar. `web_names` clean, node and repo suites pass.

Known gap: the zone gizmo still moves by whole tiles and storeys whatever the Snap setting.

### A map's own landing stays where the map has it while its zone does (KB-13 fixed)

The editor and the Build took a map's own landing as moved, with nothing changed, on most maps: 89 of the install's
141 landings with a frame, on 71 maps. Both compared the landing's six soldier points with where LWR's landing-zone
mutator lays them out for the zone, and on those maps the points stand elsewhere: on the police station on raised
ground, on many maps a third of a tile off, on some in a layout of their own. In the view the landing's Skyranger,
frame, dust and sound were hidden as moved (seen on the police station as it opened). A Build of a project that
changes its landing zones moved such a landing's soldier points, evac volume, player start and PointInSpace onto the
layout, up to 384 units across or down from raised ground.

- [spawns.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawns.js) `landingUnmoved` and [native_spawns.py](../tools/bake/native_spawns.py)
  `unmoved` now compare the zone's layout with the layout of the landing's own zone, the one its frame gives: the same
  direction, and the frame and the six soldier points within 4 units. The map's own soldier points are not compared,
  so an unmoved landing keeps them; a zone moved, turned or of another kind still moves the landing.
- [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md): KB-13 taken out. [T-51](../research/findings-register.md) says what was
  found and fixed.

Checked: new cases in [clear_map_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/clear_map_test.mjs) and
[test_native_spawns.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_native_spawns.py) failed before the fix (soldier points off the

with its own entries. Five items wait for later and two were dropped; the rest were built, a few in part.

  DefaultMaps record read three ways (KB-11), a prefab's Test in game on a long builds folder (KB-12). One found and
  left: the police station's own landing read as moved (KB-13, its own entry).

  no longer the donor's clone beside it (seen in the game: EXP-89, F-144). A made-ground Build's map is 12.9 MB
  smaller for it.

The final checks, at the branch's tip:

  (every module about 1.5 times its time at the follow-ups' first merge point, 325 s).

  and dates. Against the start: the Bar's map byte for byte the same; the made-ground map 12.9 MB smaller (the cloned
  shadow maps gone). The made-ground Build took 40 s (43 s at the start).

### A guidance page for the editor's interface

[UI-GUIDELINES.md](../UI-GUIDELINES.md) is new, beside ARCHITECTURE.md: what a change to the editor's interface
should be like. Its sections:

- editing in the 3D view (handles, gizmos and views of their own for what has a place or a size, a value drawn where
  it is, and the view kept readable: handles only on what is picked, markers in their own views, one meaning to a
  colour);
- one interface (one way to do a thing, each kind of control in its place, the stylesheet's parts, the same name, icon
  and key everywhere);
- panels, messages and buttons (a panel holds what is needed to act and no more, explanation behind the info button
  and in tooltips, a button has a border and a fill, with the main action in the accent colour; the bare-text `.link`
  style is not used for a new control);
- mock designs before a larger change (a new window, dialog, panel or view, or one laid out anew): two to four
  designs shown, one chosen, then built; the mock designs stay in `private/`;
- a checklist.

[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) has a bullet that points to it, and the [README](../README.md) a line.

### The page asks the server through api.js only

Editor follow-ups, stage P3, item 3.28: eighteen requests the page's modules made with the browser's `fetch` beside
[api.js](../tools/viewer/web/api.js) now go through it, so a refusal is read one way everywhere. Each place does on a
failure what it did before.

- **[api.js](../tools/viewer/web/api.js)** gets two helpers beside `call` (which throws the server's words on a
  refusal): `ask(url)`, a GET whose failure gives null (refused, not answered or not JSON), and
  `sendPng(method, url, blob)`, a PNG sent, giving the response as `fetch` does. (The plan named it `putPng`; one of
  the PNG requests, the map picture's preview, is a POST, so the method is given as `call`'s is.)
- **`ask`, for the reads a failure leaves as none:** the map's families as it opens and the map list
  ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js): a failed list still stops the opening with its own words), the map list
  brought up to date ([map_menu.js](../tools/viewer/web/map_menu.js)), the map's collision for invisible floors
  ([cover_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/cover_wiring.js)), its spawn rules
  ([spawns_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawns_wiring.js)) and the look picker's kept pictures
  ([look_picker.js](../tools/viewer/web/look_picker.js)).
- **`call`, for the requests whose failure is said or stops something:** the prefab builder's families (app.js), the
  install's landing lines ([clear_map.js](../tools/viewer/web/clear_map.js), with its own words for a refusal
  without any), a rock's corners ([made_handles.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_handles.js), the same), another map's
  piece and effect and many effects at once ([library_templates.js](../tools/viewer/web/library_templates.js)),
  the looks' catalogues ([looks.js](../tools/viewer/web/looks.js), whose `loadLooks` no longer takes a fetcher:
  its node test stands in for the browser's fetch), Prepare's export and its progress
  ([prepare.js](../tools/viewer/web/prepare.js)) and the map picture's removal
  ([map_picture.js](../tools/viewer/web/map_picture.js)).
- **`sendPng`:** the library's thumbnails ([library.js](../tools/viewer/web/library.js)), the look picker's
  samples, a prefab's picture ([prefabs.js](../tools/viewer/web/prefabs.js)), the map picture and its preview.
- **What stays a plain `fetch`**, named in [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) ("The page", Modules) and in the
  new node test: a picture read as a blob (map_picture.js twice, prefabs.js once), the wave's range probe
  ([effects_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_wiring.js)) and the scene's layout read with its progress
  ([loading.js](../tools/viewer/web/loading.js)).
- **[one_home_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/one_home_test.mjs)** (new) reads every page module as code (comments
  and strings left out, a template's `${...}` kept; a module that does not read whole fails) and counts the
  browser's `fetch` in each against that list with its reasons. It failed on the stage's start commit (14 modules:
  the eighteen requests and looks.js's default fetcher) and passes now.

Where the two can differ, only on answers this server never gives: a Prepare progress answer refused (it stops with
the server's words, where it asked again forever; the server refuses it only for a map not listed), the prefab
builder's families refused (its opening stops, where the refusal was read as the families' table), an answer of 200
that is not JSON (read as `{}` by `call`, so the looks' catalogue would be kept empty and Prepare would ask again), and
the map list's or the spawn rules' read not answered at all (the map's opening says its own words rather than the
browser's; the Spawns panel is drawn with no rules, as for a refused read).

Checked: the node suite (36 files) and `web_names` (98 files, clean); the twenty-edit recording the same as on the
stage's start commit, all 52 steps; browser checks `library`, `library-all`, `library-effects`, `cover`, `clear-map`,

([pack_scripts.py](../tools/viewer/pack_scripts.py), run by the pack's Install.cmd and Uninstall.cmd) found a
DefaultMaps.ini record's `Name` and `DisplayName` only when written `Name="..."`, so a pack installed in Replace mode
left a base map's record written by hand as `Name = "URB_Bar"` in use beside the pack's map (the game reads such a
record, and the editor's own install switches it off since KB-11's fix). The script's patterns now allow blanks around
`=`, as [mapsini.py](../tools/viewer/mapsini.py) reads a field: the base map's records it switches off or puts
its own after, the pack's own records it checks for, and the DisplayName a pack's map switches off by.
