Install.cmd on a game whose Bar record is written with blanks around both fields (failed before: the record stayed
in use): the record is commented out, Bar's records the pack's maps have none for stay in use, and Uninstall.cmd
puts the file back byte for byte; the viewer's pack script, manager and pack export tests pass (XCOM was not running:
none skipped).

### A build's step no longer shows the last tool's label while a tool without one runs

When a baked Build's light stage failed on copies it had not been tried on and the Build tried again without them, the
build window went on showing "Copying and relighting…" while the transplant ran again: the server kept the last
tool's label until the next stage ended. The Build's empty `running:` line before such a tool (the shell, the
transplant, the intro and stream copies) now clears the label in [builds.py](../tools/viewer/builds.py), so the
step shows its own words, as it does for those tools in every other build.

Checked: the new test in [test_builds.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_builds.py) (failed before: the label stayed)
reads a labelled line, a progress line, an empty line and another label; the viewer's builds and build queue tests
pass.

### The Build says what runs before each tool, and the server reads that line

The build window's line under a running step ("Patch and cook…", "Copying and relighting…", "Making the edit in the
map…", "Relighting…") was worked out by the server from the command line the Build echoes before a tool
([builds.py](../tools/viewer/builds.py) looked for the tool's file name and `--bake` in it), and its test fed a
hand-written echo, so a change to the echo would have dropped the label unseen (follow-ups item 6.4).
[build.py](../tools/editor/build.py) now starts every tool through `Build.tool`, which first prints
`running: <label>` (`running:` alone for the shell, the transplant and the intro and stream copies, whose steps say
enough in their own words), and the server reads that line. The fake Build of the viewer tests
([viewer_fixtures.py](../tools/viewer/tests/viewer_fixtures.py)) prints the line too.

  one):

### The browser checks' rough edges: names of their own each run, the server's 500s with their address, skipped parts that fail nothing, and --all's own Play install

The refactor's follow-ups (item 4.9) listed rough edges of the browser checks; all but the page load's time-out under
load (the computer's) are dealt with in [browser_smoke.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_smoke.py):

- **Run again against the same folder.** `projects`, `prefabs` (its project), `prefab-effects`, `library-effects` and
  `effect-values`, and `library-all` and `library-flares` the same way, name what they save after the run (`RUN`, a
  stamp of the run: "Smoke test project 123456"), so a second run no longer meets the first's project of the same name
  and times out. `projects` compares the files of the two projects it saved, not the whole folder's, so it also runs
  after other checks' projects. `prefab-effects` deletes the prefabs it made on every way out, as `prefabs` does, so a
  failed run leaves the prefab library check no prefab to trip on.
- **The server's 500s with their address.** Every page a check opens through the run's browser (in any check module:
  `browser.new_page` is wrapped) records the answers of status 500 and above with their method, address and the check
  that met them. The report lists them (`serverErrors`), a failed run prints them, and `--all` prints them under a
  failed run's line. (A console error said only "the server responded with a status of 500".)
- **`adding` picks its own piece** (typed-pose's, one function `own_piece` for both), so `--only adding` runs alone.
- **The effect edits put the snap back on every way out.** `check_effects_editing` turned the snap off and its skip on a
  map with no effect to move returned without putting it back, so later checks on such a map inherited snap off; the
  setting is now put back in a `finally`.
- **`library-effects` waits for the list to settle.** The likeness pane hides on its row's mouseleave, and the All maps
  list is drawn again whenever its size changes, which the busy row under it does while the pictures in view are read.
  The one time the wait for the pane to hide timed out (1 of 76 hovers, five pages at once), the list had been drawn
  again during that hover; the pointer now goes on a row once every picture in view is drawn and none is being read.
- **Under `--only`, a part that skips fails nothing.** A check asked for that did nothing (skipped whole, or its server
  or map can't have it) still fails the run, and so does a run in which everything skipped; a skipped part is listed
  in the report and printed. (`--only streams` on the Bar, and `streams,spawns` on the police station, exited 1 on a
  part that skipped.)
- **`--all` makes the Play check's scratch install itself.** Without `--play-install`, it copies the files the Play
  check needs (the config's `Default*.ini`, `XComGame.upk`, the played map, the `XCom*.int` words, an empty
  `Binaries`) from the game install the settings name, which is only read, into its scratch folder, when they come to
  less than 300 MB (32 MB for LWR); else Play is skipped as before, saying why. The module's docstring and
  `--play-install`'s help say so. The scratch folder is made whole first: the servers run from the repository, so a
  relative `--scratch` named folders of their own there.

Checked: before and after with the start commit's script on one test server: `--only adding` failed before and passes;
`--only streams` on the Bar and `--only streams,spawns` on the police station exited 1 before and pass, their skipped
parts listed. The changed checks (`typed-pose`, `adding`, `effects`, `projects`, `prefabs`, `prefab-effects`,
`library-all`, `library-effects`, `effect-values`, `library-flares`) passed five times in a row on one test server
against one projects folder. `browser_smoke.py --all` twice: 9 of its 10 runs passed each time (77 checks); the Play
run made its scratch install itself (36 files) and was then refused because XCOM was running (a game not started by
the checks), so Play is still to be run with the game closed.

### A Build no longer fails when another program holds its map a moment

The Build put two maps in place with a bare `os.replace`: the map with the project's picture written into it, and
the map with its lightmaps put inside it ([build.py](../tools/editor/build.py), `picture` and `lighting_inside`).
On Windows a replace is refused for a moment while another program holds the file (a virus scanner, a search
indexer), so a Build could stop with a `PermissionError` at its last steps, after a finished bake. Both now go through
[atomic_files.py](../tools/viewer/atomic_files.py)'s `replace`, which tries again through that moment (about a
second, as the server's writers do since KB-10's fix) and raises the last refusal.

Checked: a new Build test in [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py) refuses each of the two replaces
twice and sees the Build finish with the picture and the lightmaps in the map and the manifest's hash the map's (it
failed before with the `PermissionError`); the editor suite passes (379 tests).

### A prefab test's records are written through atomic_files too (KB-10's last writer in the server)

KB-10's fix (one writer for a file replaced whole, [atomic_files.py](../tools/viewer/atomic_files.py)) left one
writer of `tools/viewer` replacing once: `write()` in [prefab_tests.py](../tools/viewer/prefab_tests.py), which
writes a prefab test's `test.json`, its snapshot, its project and its compile report, then the Build track's file. It
now writes through `atomic_files.write_text`, keeping its temporary file's name (`<stem>.tmp` beside the record) and
its bytes, so a Test in game whose record another program holds a moment (a virus scanner, an indexer) waits for it
instead of failing, and a write that fails leaves no temporary file.

Checked: [test_atomic_files.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_atomic_files.py) runs the prefab test's writer among
the writers whose every replace is refused twice (it failed before with a `PermissionError`), and its scan no longer
allows `prefab_tests.py` (the scan failed until the entry went); the atomic files and prefab test tests pass (22).

### One reader of a DefaultMaps.ini record's fields: the map list and the mission kinds read through mapsini

A record's fields were read in three places, written three times: [maplist.py](../tools/viewer/maplist.py)'s
`field` and `unquoted`, [missions.py](../tools/viewer/missions.py)'s `_unquoted` and `_quoted`, and

family), and the export, the output names and the install that used `maplist.field`
([export.py](../tools/viewer/export.py), [outputnames.py](../tools/viewer/outputnames.py),

record also with blanks put around every `=`) through the map list's, the mission kinds' and the streams' readers, a

the same before and after. The viewer's map list, play, manager, output names, install and mapsini tests pass (the

### A Replace build takes out a map record written by hand with spaces around "=" (KB-11)

A record of `DefaultMaps.ini` written by hand as `Name = "URB_Bar"` (the game reads it so) was found by the map list
and the export, which allow blanks around `=`, but not by the install, whose reader did not: installing a Build that
replaces the map added the editor's records and left that one live, so the game could still load the original.

[mapsini.py](../tools/viewer/mapsini.py), the install's reader and writer of a record's fields, now reads a field
as the game and the map list do (decision D5 of the follow-ups plan: the tolerant way everywhere): `field`,
`unquoted` and `set_field` allow blanks around `=`, and an unquoted value may hold digits as well as letters and
underscores (the installs' landed and crashed UFO records write `ShipType=10`; the map list read those already).
`set_field` writes the field it sets without blanks, as the game's records are. Everything that reads a record
through mapsini reads such a record now:

- the install ([installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py)): a map's records (`base_records`), the records a Replace
  comments out (`replaced_records`), a record's rotation and mission;
- the Build ([build.py](../tools/editor/build.py)), which since the commit before writes its records through
  mapsini: it finds the same records of the base map as the install in the same order (so a Build's records stand
  for the install's: `config.recordMissions`), and writes its own copy of a hand-written one, where it left it out
  before;
- the library's donor maps ([library.py](../tools/viewer/library.py)), whose record names now come from
  `mapsini.field` in place of a pattern of their own.

What a user sees: such a record is commented out by a Replace install like the map's other records, and put back as
it was when the install is taken out; a Build of the map has a record for its mission. Records written as the game's
are read as before (the three installs hold none with blanks around `=`), and no Build's output changes.

Checked, each test failing before the change: [test_manager.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_manager.py) installs a
Build in Replace mode on an install whose Bar terror record is written `Name = "URB_Bar"` and
`MissionType = eMission_TerrorSite`: the three records of Bar are commented out (two before), the variant has a
record for each mission, and a reset leaves the files byte for byte; [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py)
has the Build and the install find the same records, a hand-written one among them, and the Build write its copy;
the new [test_mapsini.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_mapsini.py) reads and sets fields with blanks around `=` and
`ShipType=10`, and reads and writes a line of text as its bytes (that second test passes on the commit before too).
The editor suite (378 tests), the viewer's install, play, manager, pack, map list, output names, library and squad
tests (170; the 10 game-script tests skipped while a lab copy of XCOM ran) and the bake suite's deploy tests pass.
KB-11 leaves [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md).

Left as it was: the stream names in a record (`MapName="..."`) are still read without blanks around `=`, everywhere
the same way (mapsini's `slot_streams` and the readers that follow it).

### The Build writes its DefaultMaps.ini records through mapsini, the installer's writer (one writer of a record)

[build.py](../tools/editor/build.py) held a text copy of [mapsini.py](../tools/viewer/mapsini.py)'s record
writer (`field_re`, `set_field`, `add_stream`, follow-ups item 3.27). The three are gone: `config_lines` and the
records' helpers read and write a record through `mapsini.field`, `unquoted`, `set_field`, `add_stream` and
`slot_streams`, which now take a line of text as well as one of bytes and give a line back in the kind they were
given (a line of bytes is read as Latin-1, a character a byte, so it goes back byte for byte; the patterns match a
line of text as they match its bytes). The base map's records are found by `installs.same_map` on the record's Name
as `mapsini.field` reads it, as the install finds them, in place of a regular expression of the Build's own; the
intro a record streams is read by `slot_streams`; the template record's council test, the display names and the
`|n` ending read through `field` and `unquoted`. [missions.py](../tools/viewer/missions.py)'s `added_record`
streams the bomb's stream with `mapsini.add_stream` itself, so the Build no longer passes its copy in.

What a Build writes is the same. Two things differ where no Build goes: `mapsini.add_stream` refuses a patch name that
is not a package name and a stream the record has already (the Build's copy did neither; a Build's patch is
`patch_<map>`, and an added bomb record streams the bomb's stream only where its template has none), and a refusal of
the writers (a base record without a Name or DisplayName to set) stops the Build with "a DefaultMaps.ini record can't
be written: record has no DisplayName" (`record_edits`) where it said "the record has no DisplayName".

Checked: the editor suite (377 tests, its config-line tests now writing their records with `mapsini`), and the
viewer's install, play, map list, output names and pack tests and the bake suite's deploy tests, which use mapsini's
writers on bytes; [build_outputs.py](../tools/editor/tests/build_outputs.py)'s records on the commit before and on
this one are the same (11 inputs, quick and baked Builds, the config lines among them).

### The relight probe kept as a research tool: where a relight's time goes inside its workers

The editor refactor's stage B5 timed the relight's parts inside every pool worker with a scratch probe and replayed
the pool's clock with what-ifs; that is how the made pieces' second shadow maps (follow-up 2.2) and the workers'
start were found. The probe is now [relight_probe.py](../tools/bake/relight_probe.py) (follow-up 1.5), with three
commands, its usage in its docstring (`--help` prints it; `tools/bake` has no README):

- `run --log <folder> -- <relight.py's arguments>` runs [relight.py](../tools/bake/relight.py) as it is, with timers
  round its parts in the main process and in every spawned worker (each imports the probe as its main module and finds
  the folder in the environment the probe sets), one JSON line per timed call per process. A part the relight no longer
  has is named at the start and left;
- `report <folder>` (B5's `analyse.py`): the workers' start, the jobs by kind, each piece's preparation and its parts,
  the band computations' parts, and each shadow map's job with its component, its shadow map (the job's record now
  names it), its rectangle and seconds;
- `replay <folder> [--relight-json <record>]` (B5's `simulate.py`): the pool's clock from the measured jobs, as
  `run_jobs` hands them out, with what-ifs: a fresh piece's shadow maps of one light but the last it lists left out,
  the distance fields' window search four times faster, a band's preparation paid once a piece.

Folders come from the arguments, the tool folders through [paths.py](../tools/paths.py)'s `use()`, and nothing heavy
is imported for `--help`, `report` or `replay`. It is listed as a research tool that does not ship
([structure.json](../tools/repo/structure.json)'s `not shipped`).

Checked: [test_relight_probe.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_relight_probe.py) (new, in the bake suite) runs `--help`
and the report and replay on made-up records (4 tests, 1 s). A real run on the made-ground Build's relight (the
follow-ups' baseline, 16 workers) wrote 17 processes' records: 269 jobs, 48 of them shadow maps (56.7 s summed, 44.3 s
of it the made pieces' second maps), the replayed clock 17.4 s as run and 14.6 s without the second maps; its relight
took 37 s with the timers on (31 s in the Build without; the computer was loaded by other work).

### A save no longer fails while another program holds the file a moment: one writer for every file the server replaces whole (KB-10)

A new module, [atomic_files.py](../tools/viewer/atomic_files.py), is the one writer of a file the editor replaces
whole. `write_bytes` and `write_text` write a temporary file beside the file and put it in its place with `replace`,
which tries `os.replace` again while Windows refuses it with a `PermissionError` (another program holding the file a
moment: a virus scanner, a backup or search indexer), 50 tries 0.02 s apart as the install's records always did, and
then raises the last refusal. A write that fails removes its temporary file and leaves the file as it was.

Every writer of `tools/viewer` goes through it now, each keeping its own lock, flush to the disk, read-back,
temporary file's name where something looks for it, and error words: a project and its drafts and its revision before
([projects.py](../tools/viewer/projects.py)), a prefab's picture and a deleted prefab moved aside
([prefabs.py](../tools/viewer/prefabs.py)), a map picture and the one before it
([pictures.py](../tools/viewer/pictures.py)), a build's snapshot, its writer record and a report's zip
([builds.py](../tools/viewer/builds.py)), the publication journal
([publication.py](../tools/viewer/publication.py)), the build queue, its last good copy and a queue set aside
([buildqueue.py](../tools/viewer/buildqueue.py)), the package digests
([catalogue.py](../tools/viewer/catalogue.py)), the library's index, its pieces', effects' and area lights'
records, the favourites and the thumbnails ([library.py](../tools/viewer/library.py)), the test squad and its
backup ([squads.py](../tools/viewer/squads.py)), a play's saves put back and moved
([playsaves.py](../tools/viewer/playsaves.py)), a pack's record and zip ([packs.py](../tools/viewer/packs.py),
[manager.py](../tools/viewer/manager.py)), the settings ([settings.py](../tools/viewer/settings.py)), and the
install's ledgers, config files, package files and their roll-backs ([installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py),
[mapsini.py](../tools/viewer/mapsini.py), whose retries were the model and are now the module's).
`installs.replace_bytes` and `installs._put_bytes`, the same function twice, are one (the temporary file named for the
prefab test, or for the change under way).

What a user sees: a save, a picture, a build's record or an install that met a file held a moment now waits up to
about a second for it instead of stopping with "could not be written". A writer that left its temporary file behind
when it failed (a build's snapshot, the publication journal, a build's writer record, the install's ledger) now
removes it. Every file is written with the same bytes and names as before.

Left as they were: the folder moves of the export's publish ([export.py](../tools/viewer/export.py)) and of a
package's swap ([publication.py](../tools/viewer/publication.py)), which rely on `Path.rename` refusing a folder
that is there; and `write()` in [prefab_tests.py](../tools/viewer/prefab_tests.py) (a prefab test's records), the
Build track's file, which still replaces once. The scan lists the three with their reasons.

Checked: the new [test_atomic_files.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_atomic_files.py) tries `replace` through two
refusals, through the last (raised, the file moved left where it was) and with another error (raised at once), and
`write_bytes` and `write_text` failing (no temporary file left); runs 18 writers (a project saved twice, a picture
saved twice, a build's snapshot, a prefab saved, pictured and deleted, a publication, the build queue, the package
digests, the library's index, area lights, favourites and a thumbnail, the settings, the squad saved twice, a pack, a
play's saves, the install's ledger, an install's change, its config files) with every replace refused twice, each
written in full with no temporary file left; and scans `tools/viewer/*.py` for `os.replace`, `os.rename` and a path's
`replace` or `rename`. Before the writers moved, 17 of the 18 writers failed (only the install's ledger tried again)
and the scan named 14 modules. [test_playsaves.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_playsaves.py) counts the moves at
`os.replace` itself, as `playsaves` no longer imports `os`. The viewer (662 tests; the 10 game-script tests skipped
while a lab copy of XCOM ran), editor (377), lab (49), release (17) and repo (44) suites pass, and the browser checks
of projects and prefabs pass on a test server with a scratch cache (whose library scan wrote its index through the
new writer). [build_outputs.py](../tools/editor/tests/build_outputs.py)'s records before and after are the same (11
inputs, quick and baked Builds). KB-10 leaves [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md).

### The near-black made blocks' 29/255 measured in light: a preview's scale, no stored texel

Editor follow-ups, stage R1 (item 2.4, decision D2). The refactor's final checks found two made ground blocks of the
made-ground real baked Build whose relit images moved up to 29/255 with the DXT1 reading of the original bakes. The
findings register's [T-50](../research/findings-register.md) has the measurement; in short:

- The two blocks are made pieces lit from nothing (`--fresh-copy`), whose written lightmaps don't read the original
  bake: built with the reading of today and with the Pillow reading before it, they are byte for byte the same (the
  largest difference 0, against URB_Bar's median lit level of 0.443). The images that moved are the relight's
  previews, which divide by the original's 99th percentile: the donor's cloned near-black bake, read 31% higher by
  the exact decoder.
- Decision D2's rule (a difference under a 255th of the median lit level changes no code) leaves
  [relight.py](../tools/bake/relight.py)' `apply_change` as it is; the guessed cause (its weight near a zero
  original) does not touch these pieces.
- Where the reading does move the light (pieces of the map relit as a change, at most 0.022 before the encoding and
  as much as each Build's own DXT1 error once stored) is the move the DXT1 reading was accepted with.

Checked: the ground Build run with the Pillow reading in a scratch copy of the tools reproduces the final checks'
moves exactly (181 of 214 previews, largest 29/255, 274 texels over 6/255); each relit component's lightmap decoded
from the two variant maps; an absolute relight of the two blocks in the built map (scratch scripts, not checked in).
No code changed.

### Two identical baked Builds keep the same piece cache bytes

Editor follow-ups, stage R1 (item 3.10). A relit piece's report carries the scene's counts, and its
`albedoSources` (how many materials got their albedo from a diffuse texture, a constant colour, the fallback, ...) was
built over a set of those words, whose order changes with each process's string hashing. The piece cache keeps the
report as JSON text in each piece's `.npz`, so two runs of the same Build kept files with the same arrays and the same
parsed report but different bytes, and "two runs identical" could not be a byte comparison.

- [relight.py](../tools/bake/relight.py)' `Scene` builds `albedoSources` over the sorted words.
- No image, scale or record changes. relight.py is in the piece cache's key (`TOOL_FILES`), so a project's kept
  pieces are relit once by the next baked Build.

Checked:

- New test `SceneCounts` ([test_relight.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_relight.py)), on a Scene built from
  stand-ins (no install, no Embree): eight kinds of albedo note given in three orders come out in sorted order with the
  same JSON text. It failed before the change (the words came out in the set's order).
- The two real baked Builds of the follow-ups' baseline (the Bar with a moved floor, and EXP-77's made ground), each
  run twice into an empty piece cache: run 1 and run 2 byte for byte the same in every package, texture cache, relit
  image and piece cache file (184 and 322 `.npz` files), where the baseline's two runs differed in the report text of
  every `.npz`; only the records' times and the logs differ. Against the baseline run: the packages, texture caches
  and the 214 and 321 relit images byte for byte the same; the piece cache files are under new keys, and held by
  their reports' components, all 183 and 321 have the same arrays and the same parsed report.
- `python -B tools/run_tests.py bake -k SceneCounts`.

### A texture's or lightmap's compressed bulk payload is read by the one chunk-header reader

[texture.py](../tools/viewer/texture.py)' `decompress_payload` (every texture the exporter reads, and the bake's
lightmap, shadow-map and albedo modules) read a compressed bulk payload's header and block table its own way, beside
[decomp.py](../tools/upk/decomp.py)' `read_chunk`, which says it is the one reader of a chunk header. It now takes
the header and the block table from `read_chunk` (the tag, the block size, the table's two sums checked against the
header's before anything is decoded) and keeps what is its own: zlib or LZO by the flags, LZX refused, at most 512 MB
(`BULK_LIMIT`), the payload ending where its blocks end, each block decoded to its table's size. `read_chunk`'s
`ValueError` becomes the reader's `FormatError`, as its own refusals were. [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)'s
rule for readers of package bytes now names the readers V1 put the package's header, an export's native data and a
chunk header through (`upkinfo`, `Package.native`, `decomp.read_chunk`).

Checked: new tests in [test_damaged_packages.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_damaged_packages.py): an LZO and a zlib
payload decode; a block table whose packed or unpacked sizes do not add up, another tag, a block size of 0, a header,
a table or the blocks cut short, bytes after the blocks, a total past the limit and LZX are each a `FormatError`; a
block that decodes to another size than its entry is lzo1x's `ValueError`, as before. Every case gave the same kind of
answer before the change (only the words differ): it changes no answer. The three maps' exports (their textures go
through it) are byte for byte the same as before V1; the bake suite passes.

### The made pieces read a component's LOD 0 through the one reader

Editor follow-ups, stage B2 (item 3.11). [frac_walls.py](../tools/bake/frac_walls.py) read LOD 0 of a mesh
component's native data three times on raw bytes, with no bounds: `_lod_colours` (where the painted colours lie, which
a made piece's colours replace), `lightmap_offsets` (where the lightmap's textures, scale and bias lie, which
`set_light` writes over) and `add_shadow_ref` (a made piece's own shadow map added to the list). A count that ran past
the record read on into the next bytes, or stopped with a `struct.error`, and `add_shadow_ref` wrote a list cut short
without a word.

- **`frac_walls.lod0`** reads the record with [native_fields.py](../tools/upk/native_fields.py)' `mesh_lods`, the
  one reader of it ([ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md), section 3, "The compiler and the Build"): every count
  held to the bytes, every reference to the package's objects, each value with its place. The three readers take
  their places from it, and `add_shadow_ref` also checks the shadow map it adds is an object of the package.
- **The map being grown:** a made piece's component bytes are in the numbering of the map the Build is growing, with
  the objects it added. `GrownObjects` gives the reader that numbering (the grower's imports and exports, its licensee),
  so a reference to a clone made earlier in the Build reads as one.
- **native_fields' `lod_record`** gives the painted colours' places too: `overrideVertexColorsOffset` (the flag's) and
  `overrideVertexColorsEnd` (where they end).
- **What changed for a caller:** what does not read as the layout is a `ValueError` (the reader's `FormatError`) from
  each of the three. `lightmap_offsets` of a component with no LOD record is now that error, where it gave None: its
  one caller in a Build, `component_data`, stopped on the same component a line later with the same words.
- ARCHITECTURE.md's rule of the one reader says the grown map's bytes are read by it too.

Checked:

- A scratch script held the start commit's three functions (from `git show`) against the new ones over every mesh
  component of URB_Bar and URB_PoliceStation (2,543: 2,141 with a LOD record, 402 without): the same places and the
  same bytes from `add_shadow_ref` for all 2,141, on each component's bytes and on the whole package's; the 402
  without a record raised as before in `_lod_colours` and `add_shadow_ref`, and give the error in place of None in
  `lightmap_offsets`.
- New test `LodReaders` ([test_frac_walls.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_frac_walls.py)), on a made-up component
  that needs no install: the places are the record's, and a component with no LOD record, a LOD count past its end and
  a shadow map count past its end are a `ValueError` from each of the three. Before, 7 of its 9 cases failed (a
  `struct.error`, bytes read on, a list cut short, or None); the two that passed were the no-record refusals the old
  `_lod_colours` and `add_shadow_ref` already had. [test_native_fields.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_native_fields.py)
  checks the two new places in both licensee branches.
- The upk suite (181 tests, 7 skips for their usual reasons); test_frac_walls (53 tests);
  `tools/editor/tests/build_outputs.py`: the eleven inputs' quick and baked Builds the same as at the start commit.

Known gap: native_fields.py is in the relight's piece cache key (relight.py `TOOL_FILES`), so a project's kept pieces
relight once on its next baked Build, as after stage B1's change to decomp.py.

### A map pack's GUID check reads the package summary through the one reader

[packs.py](../tools/viewer/packs.py)' `package_guid`, which the map pack export uses to warn of a map file with an

### The level's actor list, a volume's corners, a material's textures and a mesh's bounds are read inside their export

Four readers of an export's native data read the package's bytes with `struct.unpack_from`, bounded only by the end of
the file, so a damaged count or a short export was read on into the next export's bytes. They now read through the
package's bounded reader (`Package.native`, which refuses a read past the export's end with a `FormatError`):

- [scene_metadata.py](../tools/viewer/scene_metadata.py)' `level_list` (the persistent level's actor list) and
  `plain_box` (a floor volume's brush corners; a vertex count is checked as a count);
- [export.py](../tools/viewer/export.py)' `compiled_textures` (a cooked material's texture list; it kept its final
  check, which already kept it from answering with another export's references);
- [library.py](../tools/viewer/library.py)' `describe` (a mesh's bounds, which give a piece's size and box).

Each keeps its answer when its export can't be read (the actor list's `None`, the volume's `None`, the material's
`[]`; a piece is refused as before by the scan's catch, a `FormatError` being a `ValueError`).

Checked: new tests in [test_damaged_packages.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_damaged_packages.py) on made-up packages
([upk_fixtures.py](../tools/upk/tests/upk_fixtures.py) takes the names a body's properties use): an actor list whose
count runs past the level, a mesh with four of its seven bound numbers. Both failed before (the list read two more
actors from the next export; the bounds took three numbers from it). The exports of URB_Bar, URB_PoliceStation and
TempleShip from the LWR install are byte for byte the same as before the change (1,891 files), in the same time
(68.0 s before, 69.6 s after, noisy); a library scan of the three maps gives the same 746 entries. The viewer tests of
the exporter, the library, the effects and the spawn records pass.

### A Build whose files would pass Windows' path limit stops before it starts, saying by how much

Where Windows' long paths are off (the usual), a Build whose files would pass its 260 characters stopped part-way with
a `FileNotFoundError`: a prefab test's at the grown map's temporary file (KB-12), a project's at its package's intro
copy or a preview of the relight under a builds folder of about 130 to 150 characters. Now the Build works out the
deepest files it writes and, past 259 characters (247 for a folder), stops with the error code `path-too-long`, saying
which file, by how many characters, and that the builds folder should be on a path at least that much shorter
(Setup, or the output setting) ([build.py](../tools/editor/build.py), `check_paths`; decision D4 of the follow-ups
plan). For a project's Build and a prefab test alike:

- **Before the snapshot stage,** once the project's names are read: the compile report, the edited map's temporary
  file (`<map>.upk.grow-tmp`), the staged map's, in a baked Build the relight's previews (`<variant>-<actor>-shadow.png`,
  the actor's name taken at 32 characters, the game's longest being 28), and the package's maps (the variant and the
  copies of the intros its base map's records stream, read from the install) in the work folder and in place.
- **Again in preflight,** with every name the compile adds (a patch, the copies of the streams the edit changes),
  before the costly stages.
- **Not where long paths are on** (`long_paths`: Windows' own answer for this Python, which the Build's tools run on):
  there is no limit to keep to, so nothing is refused.
- **The decoded maps the Build keeps in its work folder** (`<work>/unpacked/<64 characters>.unpacked`, the deepest of
  all) are not counted: one whose name is too long is not kept, and each tool decodes the map again, which is slower
  and stops nothing (decomp.py). The snapshot stage says so in a note instead. Counting them, as the plan's list did,
  would have refused projects' quick Builds that build today, under builds folders of about 110 to 160 characters.

Checked:
- New tests in [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py), each failing before: a prefab test under a
  builds folder of 160 characters stops with `path-too-long` before the snapshot stage, nothing run or made, its words
  naming the file and the 9 characters; one of 145 builds, with the note; with long paths on the same Build is not
  refused; a project's Build whose stream copy would pass the limit stops in preflight, after its compile (before,
  it stopped at the package with `FileNotFoundError`).
- Seen in the build window on a test server (8793) with a builds folder of 170 characters: "EXP-88 wall groups didn't
  build", the log's `build failed code: path-too-long` and the refusal's words (21 characters too long).
- The editor suite (375 tests).

### The growing writer's check decodes only the blocks a write made

Editor follow-ups, stage B1 (items 1.1, 1.3 and 1.2). [package_grow.py](../tools/upk/package_grow.py)'s
`Grower.write` read back every map it wrote through the pure-Python LZO decoder, whole: 147 of the bake suite's 269
package decodes, and over half of a test build. It still reads the written file back from disk and makes every
comparison it made (the logical bytes, the tables, each export's place, no item across a chunk boundary). What changed
is how the file's decoded bytes are had:

- **[decomp.py](../tools/upk/decomp.py)'s `decompress_written`**, beside `decompress_pkg`, takes the source's
  compressed bytes, summary and decoded image (the Grower holds all three). A block of the written file whose packed
  bytes are those of the source's block at the same logical offset, of the same size, is taken from the source's image
  (the decode of the same bytes); every other block (the blocks an edit re-encoded, the new chunks) is decoded. Each
  chunk is read by `read_chunk` and held against the chunk table as `_decode` reads it (`decode_written`). The image
  is kept in the memo and the work folder under the written file's hash, as the whole decode was, so the next reader
  of the file (the copy tool's own checks, the relight in its own process) decodes nothing.
- **Blocks, not chunks:** the plan named chunks. A chunk that holds an edit keeps its other blocks' packed bytes, so the
  same rule taken block by block decodes 14 blocks of a bar build's 237 instead of whole chunks of eight.
- **`decomp.STATS`** counts these reads as `written` (the relight's timing record shows the key); `decoded` counts
  whole decodes only.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md): the rule that a writer reads back what it wrote says a read-back may take
  the blocks kept from the source from the source's decode.

Numbers (on this computer with four other stages at work, one of them running the bake suite: clock times are noisy,
CPU times are the measure):

| | before (0012083) | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the bake suite, clock (not alone: see above) | 388 s | 305 s |
| whole package decodes in the bake suite, all processes (decoding seconds summed) | 298, 177.8 s | 167, 110.4 s |
| of them in the test process | 269 | 126 (3 of them the new test's own) |
| of them in `Grower.write`'s read-back | 149, 83.7 s CPU | none; 153 reads from the source, 1.9 s CPU (28,079 blocks taken, 1,770 decoded) |
| `Grower.write` in the bake suite (157 calls before, 158 after) | 97.5 s CPU, 0.62 s a call | 15.3 s CPU, 0.10 s a call |
| one test build of the bar (a car's assembly moved, a lamp copied), three runs | 1.12 to 1.19 s CPU | 0.50 to 0.52 s CPU |
| the same build's read-back | 0.67 s | 0.03 s (reading and hashing the file) |

- **1.3, `edit_columns`' scan, is not done:** it costs 0.10 to 0.12 s CPU a build (the bar build above, three runs;
  61 calls in the bake suite, 6.8 s CPU summed), under the plan's 0.25 s a build.
- **1.2, the memo's size:** with this in, a bake run decodes 142 maps whole at `MEMO_SIZE` 8 against 167 at 4 (the
  test process 101 against 126): 12.6 s CPU of decoding saved. A decoded map holds 28.5 MB (the median of the suite's
  decodes; 36 MB the largest), so 4 hold up to about 145 MB and 8 about 290 MB. Under the plan's 15 s, so the default
  stays 4 and the bake fixtures do not change it.
- **The relight's kept pieces:** its piece cache's key takes the hash of `decomp.py` (`relight.TOOL_FILES`), so a
  project's next baked Build after this change relights its kept pieces once.

Tests: [test_package_grow.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_package_grow.py): with made-up chunks (no game file), only
the blocks a write made or moved are decoded and the image is the whole decode's, and a chunk whose size disagrees
with its table is refused; on URB_Bar, URB_PoliceStation and DLC2_3_Furies (stored uncompressed), the read-back is the
whole decode; a byte changed on disk in a new chunk, a byte changed on disk in a block kept from the source, and a
writer that leaves an edited block as the source had it each fail the check; the written map is decoded zero times
(one `written` read) and kept for the next reader and another process.
[test_native_copy.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_native_copy.py): the three maps the NativeCopy class writes read back
as a whole decode reads them; a build decodes the bar once (twice before).

Checked: the bake suite (703 tests, 1 skip for the ring of base maps) and the upk suite with the install's maps (181
tests, 3 skips: no private copy of the reference writer in a worktree) pass; over a whole bake run every growing
write's read-back (151; the rest were the same file again, from the memo) was held against a whole decode of the file:
all equal; `build_outputs.py` recorded on 0012083 and on this change: the same, the ten inputs' quick and baked
Builds; the two real baked Builds (moved bar floor, EXP-77's made ground) against the follow-ups' baseline: every game
file (the grown and lit maps, the package's map and texture cache) byte for byte the same; the manifests and readmes
differ by the build's time, stamp and folders only.

Known gaps: `package_edit.write_edited`'s own check (with `verify`, as the relight's writes call it) still decodes the
written file whole: 12 decodes of the bake suite, 7.3 s CPU. It is not in this stage's files.

### An undo or a redo takes the delete's hint away

After a delete, the hint "Deleted 402 pieces · Ctrl+Z brings them back" stayed up for its two and a half seconds even
when Ctrl+Z had brought the pieces back meanwhile. Now an undo or a redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, the header's buttons), once
its step is done, puts the resting hint back in place of the notice: none, or how to place the piece being placed, or
box select's line ([delete_reset.js](../tools/viewer/web/delete_reset.js) `undoStep`, given the hints' `restingHint`
by [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)). For a large step under the busy mark, that is after the step has run.

What the exploratory test also saw, looked at on a test server: `viewer.changes()` reading 0 moved pieces for a moment
right after the first Ctrl+Z of a large delete is the large step's wait under the busy mark, not a stale count. The
undo of a step of 60 pieces or more runs one frame after its mark is drawn; until then the count is the one before
the undo, in which the moved pieces deleted count as deleted only (432 deleted read once, then the right count from
the next sample on). No change made for it. The second Ctrl+Z once lost in that wait is the busy mark holding the
view's keys while a mark put up at once shows (so that a second step does not queue behind the first); it was not
reproduced, and nothing is changed for it.

Checked: the `small-defects` browser check ([browser_editing.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_editing.py)) deletes
402 pieces (432 with their linked pieces), then one, and after each Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Z the hint is gone. It
failed before the change (the hint still read "Deleted 432 pieces · Ctrl+Z brings them back" after the undo).
`--only small-defects` passes.

open and nothing changed. It did not show: the edit chip was hidden, as it is before any edit. But a hidden chip kept
its last words, "not saved", and the test read the chip's text with Playwright's `inner_text`, which gives a hidden
element's text too. Now the chip holds no words, and no title, while it is hidden
([piece_status.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_status.js)), so the page's text says only what is shown. What a user
sees is unchanged.

Checked: the `reset-all` browser check ([browser_editing.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_editing.py)) asserts that
after a Reset all that leaves nothing changed, with no project open, the chip is hidden with no words and no title. It
failed before the change (hidden, with "not saved"). Tried on a test server, and the chip never showed with nothing
changed: a group alone, a move, a clear and a landing zone copy, each reset with no project open (the group and the
move undone and redone after), and a project closed with changes. `--only reset-all,typed-pose` pass.

### A damaged package is refused, not read on: a damaged map-picture package no longer stops the Project manager's list (KB-9)

The package header reader, [upkinfo.py](../tools/upk/upkinfo.py), now refuses a damaged or cut-short package with a
`ValueError` that says what it met and where, instead of a `struct.error` at the buffer's end, an `IndexError`, a
recursion that never ends or a name made up as `?N`:

- a string whose length runs past the bytes left (`R.fstr`);
- a count of names, imports, exports, generations, chunks or additional packages that the bytes left can't hold,
  refused before the loop that reads them; a field cut short inside a table names the table and the entry
  ("cut short in export 3 of 3: a field at byte ...");
- a name index out of range in the tables (an import's or export's name);
- an object or class reference out of range, its own or one of its outer chain's, and an outer chain that loops
  (`objname`, now a loop rather than a recursion, and `clsname`);
- a file under eight bytes (`load`).

The two other readers of a name index refuse one out of range too: [kismet_links.py](../tools/upk/kismet_links.py)'s
`P.name` (it made up `?N`) and [schema.py](../tools/upk/schema.py)'s closing-None check, where a negative index
wrapped round to a real name. A sweep of the LWR install's 8,183 packages (and the lab copy's 8,233) found no name
index out of range in the tables and none in the 40,290 name values of the 562 packages with Kismet that
`kismet_links` reads, so none is kept; the schema built from either install's script packages is the same as before.

[pictures.py](../tools/viewer/pictures.py)' `_base_index` then skips a damaged map-picture package through the
catch it has (now `OSError` and `ValueError`, what the readers raise), so the other packages' pictures are listed, a
project's picture state is worked out and the Project manager lists its projects. Before, the `struct.error` or
`IndexError` went through that catch and the listing failed. KB-9 leaves [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md).

Checked: new tests in [test_bad_input.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_bad_input.py) (a made-up package from
[upk_fixtures.py](../tools/upk/tests/upk_fixtures.py) cut at every byte of its header and tables, wild counts, bad
string lengths, names, outers and classes out of range, looping outer chains, the Kismet and schema readers) and in the
new [test_damaged_packages.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_damaged_packages.py) (six damaged forms of
`UILibrary_MapImages_SF.upk` beside a good DLC package: the picture index, `base_library`, `pictures.status` and the
Project manager's listing). Eight of the nine new upk tests and both viewer tests failed before the change (each of the
six damaged forms stopped the picture index with a `struct.error` or an `IndexError`). The sweep's hash of every
package's summary and tables is the same before and after; the tables' time is unchanged and a map's paths and classes
take about 1 ms more (some 27,000 names; times noisy, other work ran on the computer). The upk and viewer suites pass.

### A prefab's Test in game builds under a long builds folder (KB-12 fixed)

**Test in game** in the prefab builder stopped in its Build with a `FileNotFoundError` naming a file that ends in
`.upk.grow-tmp` when the builds folder sat deep in folders, while a project's own Build from the same folder worked
(KB-12). A test's Build made its files under
`<builds>/.prefab-tests/<test id, 36 characters>/artifacts/.work/<pt_ and 26 characters>-<date>-<attempt>/`, which
added about 120 characters before the files the Build writes, so the grown map's temporary file came to 169 characters
past the builds folder and passed Windows' 260 with a builds folder of about 90. Now:

- **The Build takes its work folder from a new field,** `BuildInputs.work` (`--work` on the command line); without
  it, a prefab test's Build works in `w` beside the test's project file, in the test's own folder, and any other
  build in `<output>/.work/<Variant>-<stamp>` as before ([build.py](../tools/editor/build.py), `work_folder`).
  The manifest's `work` names it. A prefab test's folders are pruned whole as before, and what looks for a running
  test's tools (its folder in their command lines) finds them there too.
- **A new test's folder and map are named by the first 12 hexadecimal characters of its id**
  ([prefab_tests.py](../tools/viewer/prefab_tests.py) `short_name`,
  [prefab_stage.py](../tools/editor/prefab_stage.py) `package_code`: `pt_<12>` and `pp_<12>`, where they were the
  whole id in base 32, 26 characters). The id itself stays a UUID: the install's journal of a test's files names it
  and is refused for anything else ([installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py) `recover_test_install`). A test made
  before, its folder named by its whole id, is still recovered, read, played from and pruned.

So a test's deepest file is now about 90 characters past the builds folder (the package's map in place; the decoded
maps the Build keeps while it runs, `w/unpacked/<64 characters>.unpacked`, about 112).

Checked:
- KB-12 reproduced first with a scratch script (a prefab of three pieces of another map prepared on the blank map and
  built quick as the server starts a test, on a scratch cache): with a builds folder of 100 characters the old layout
  stops in `native_copy.py` on `lit\pt_<26>.upk.grow-tmp` (169 characters past the builds folder), with one of 120
  already at the compile report; with the change the same test builds under 120, its deepest file 89 characters past.
- New tests, each failing before: [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py) builds a prefab test with
  stand-in tools under a builds folder of 140 characters, where the old layout's deepest file would be 280 (it stopped
  with `FileNotFoundError` before), and checks its work folder and that its deepest file is 108 characters past the
  builds folder; a given work folder is the build's; `--work` reaches the Build.
  [test_prefab_tests.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_prefab_tests.py): a new test's folder and map are named short,
  a test of before (its folder named by its whole id) is recovered and read, a folder whose record names another test
  is left alone.
- The editor suite (373 tests); the viewer suite's prefab test and builds tests.

KB-12 leaves [KNOWN-BUGS.md](../KNOWN-BUGS.md).

### The builder check's held draft: its answer waited for, not 1.1 s

Editor refactor, stage P10. In [browser_builder.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_builder.py), the recovery-edges
part holds a draft's write (PUT) 300 ms, saves meanwhile, and checks that no draft is left: a draft written after the
save would show. It waited 1.1 s after the save for that write; it now waits for the held write's answer (Playwright's
`expect_response`), which is already in when the save waited for it, as it should, and comes after the save if a
change ever lets the save go first. The 300 ms hold itself stays: it is the slow server the check makes, not a wait.

Checked on a test server: `--only builder` five times in a row, all passing; `browser_smoke.py --all` twice (its
`builder` run).

filter typed into the Add panel went: the panel draws its list again in the box's input listener (pieces.js `render`),
which Playwright's `fill` runs, so the list is read at once. Kept, with why written beside them: the two 300 ms after
the camera is put over a spot (a frame drawn from there before `screenOf`, which reads the camera's matrices a render
updates, gives the points to drag between).

--all` twice (its `police` run).

### The Map picture check's fixed waits: the wheel's turns counted and the server's answer drawn

Editor refactor, stage P10. In [browser_map_picture.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_map_picture.py), its four
fixed waits went:

- **The wheel:** each run of turns now waits until the frame canvas has had every turn (a counting listener the check
  adds after the dialog's own), instead of 300 ms after the frame first came under 800 pixels; the frame's own waits
  (1,600 wide, 32 wide, under 800) stay.
- **The result as the game shows it** (three waits of 900 ms): the dialog draws the crop at once on each change of the

`map-picture` run).

### browser_editing's fixed waits: the dialogs' focus and the slow mesh's request waited for

Editor refactor, stage P10. In [browser_editing.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_editing.py), four of its six
fixed waits went (no assertion dropped):

- `modals`: a dialog's own focus, which comes a moment after it shows, is waited for (the focus inside the dialog;
  in Missions with no row ticked, on the first row that can be ticked), and so is the focus back on the header's Map
  button after Escape, each for up to 5 s before the assertion that says what was found (150, 150 and 50 ms before).
- `look-undo`: the test's own slow fetch counts the made-mesh requests, and the check waits for the new look's mesh to
  be asked for (the look change under way, its answer held back) before deleting the other piece, where it waited
  200 ms.

### browser_smoke's fixed waits: each one that is not a camera wait replaced by a wait for what the check reads

Editor refactor, stage P10. Of [browser_smoke.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_smoke.py)'s 42 fixed waits
(`wait_for_timeout` and `time.sleep`, on 40 lines), 20 went (no assertion dropped, no time-out made longer):

- **Waits for a state the check reads:** the floor-placing preview under the pointer before a click
  (`viewer.placing().ghost.visible`, as library-all already waited); the floor tile tip saying the piece's name, then
  "deleted since" (`#floorTip`, written by the draw loop); the Map lighting mode with the lights as edited
  (`viewer.lighting.counts`); the likeness drawn, switched off (none and no particles), back on, deleted and undone
  (`viewer.likenessState()`); output-names' held answer: the test's own slow fetch records the name asked for, and
  the check waits for the name typed to be asked before reading the dialog meanwhile.
- **Read at once where the page acts in the event's own listener**, which Playwright's mouse and key calls wait for
  (measured on the Bar: 150 of 150 moves, presses, releases, wheel turns and keys were seen by the page's listeners when
  the call returned): the Map grid's and a no-spawn volume's handle drags (the press takes the handle under its own
  point, the release sets the size), and the hunts for a gizmo's handle along a line (the gizmo takes its hovered axis
  in its pointermove listener; copy-drag's hunt always read it so).
- **A negative check made exact:** copy-drag's Escape during a Shift drag now waits for the release to be handled and
  checks that no paste began (`viewer.copySerial()`: a paste numbers its copies before anything it waits for), where
  a 200 ms grace looked for a copy turning up; library-effects' sound row checks that the hover took no tip into the
  likeness pane (what a row the pane is to show does at once), where 600 ms looked for the pane.

Kept, with why written beside each: the key holds (arrow-pan's and turn's 300 ms, the text field's 200 ms: how long a
key is held, then 100 ms for the last camera step); `settled`'s camera polls; frames drawn after the camera was put
somewhere before screen points are read (floor-placing's drag, the Spawns view's pod and volume handles, the zone
gizmo's ring after R) and before pictures (map-lights, floors-cut, previews, the run's screenshot, likeness's framed
effect); likeness's 1.5 s of likenesses drawn before the frame time it reports, and its picture polls; polls of a
server or page state at 250 ms (`wait_recovery`, `wait_opened`) and the server start and stop polls (Playwright's
`wait_for_function` does not wait for an async predicate's answer, so a poll that fetches stays a loop).

Checked on a test server: copy-drag, clear-map, library-effects, floor-placing, floor-tiles, lights, output-names,
likeness, spawns and header five times in a row with `--only`, all passing (60 to 66 s a run, 77 s at the base
without header; other agents' runs make the times noisy); `browser_smoke.py --all` twice with `--play-install`.

### startScene split into the scene's parts, each in the module that owns it

Editor refactor, stage P9, second part (the plan's P9 step 3, first half): app.js's `startScene`, which starts the
editor on a map's or a prefab's scene, no longer holds each area's start itself. Each run of it that belongs to an area
moved verbatim into a function of that area's module, and `startScene` calls them in the order it always ran them.
Nothing the editor does changes.

- **The parts and their homes**, each returned by its module's factory (or exported) and called from `startScene` in
  its place:
  - [scene_pieces.js](../tools/viewer/web/scene_pieces.js) `buildPieces(streamObjects, mapName)`: every mesh and
    material asked for up front, the pieces built in scene order with the loading overlay's count, and the refusal
    when none could be drawn (the factory is now given `loadingState`);
  - [clear_map.js](../tools/viewer/web/clear_map.js) `readLandingLines()`: the install's landing lines for the map
    read, the ground grid and the zones following when they come; `startMissionPicker()`: the header's Mission picker;
  - [lights_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/lights_wiring.js) `lightingModes()`: the Map lighting mode's buttons;
    `applyMapLighting()`: the view lit with the lights as edited, which `startScene` puts in app.js's `applyLighting`
    (a `let` that does nothing until a scene has started, as before; it was an arrow made there, now a function of the

    options' Hide patch helpers and the layout's patches and streams;

    checked as it opens (the factory is now given `projectsAvailable`);
  - [builder_session.js](../tools/viewer/web/builder_session.js) `builderPage()`: the page dressed as the prefab
    builder's (the factory is now given `showFileDialog`);
  - [scene_start.js](../tools/viewer/web/scene_start.js), new, plain exports for what is no one area's:

### The edit hub: each area registers what it keeps up after an edit (edit_hub.js)

Editor refactor, stage P9, first part (decision D5's default: registration only): `editChangedNow` no longer calls
every panel by name. Each area's module registers its refresh with the edit hub as it is made, and the hub calls them
in the order the page always called them. Nothing the editor does changes.

- **[edit_hub.js](../tools/viewer/web/edit_hub.js)** is new, a pure module (node imports it, so it is not in
  editor_state.js, which reads the page's address as it loads). Its `RUNS` lists each run's refreshes in their order,
  with whose each is: `edit` (after any edit, undo or selection) holds fifteen, from the Effects view's redraw asked
  through the selection following the gizmo, the Buildings view, the cutaway, the selection's marks, an invisible
  floor's note, the pose fields and edit status, the Flags group, Select all of a kind, the group and Align sections,
  the Room section, the gizmo's buttons and the project's title to the lights; `drag` holds what the edit status's
  refresh runs while a gizmo handle is held (the lights drawn following). `onHub(run, name, refresh)` registers one,
  and refuses a name the run doesn't list or one registered twice; `runHub(run, ...args)` calls those registered, in
  `RUNS`' order whatever order they were registered in, and a refresh that gives back `STOP` ends the run (as
  `return` ended `editChangedNow`). Its node test, [edit_hub_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/edit_hub_test.mjs),
  registers a run backwards and checks the order, `STOP`, the arguments and the refusals.
- **[app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)**: `editChangedNow` is `runHub('edit')`; app.js registers its own four
  parts of it (the selection following the gizmo, the selected piece's marks, the pose fields and edit status, the
  gizmo's buttons), moved verbatim, and no longer takes the refreshes it called by name from the factories that
  return them. While a handle is held, the edit status's refresh runs the `drag` run where it called `lightsChanged`.
  app.js: 2,788 lines to 2,783; its top-level functions (114) and `let` statements (13, 20 names) as they were.
- **The areas' modules** each register their part of `editChangedNow`, moved verbatim, inside their factory:
  [effects_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_wiring.js) (the redraw asked),
  [buildings_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/buildings_wiring.js) (the boxes followed, a box never turned),
  [cutaway.js](../tools/viewer/web/cutaway.js), [cover_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/cover_wiring.js) (an
  invisible floor's note), [flags_panel.js](../tools/viewer/web/flags_panel.js),
  [select_kind.js](../tools/viewer/web/select_kind.js), [groups.js](../tools/viewer/web/groups.js) and
  [align.js](../tools/viewer/web/align.js) (each its half of "a building's box is in no group and is not aligned"),
  [made_panel.js](../tools/viewer/web/made_panel.js) (the Room section),
  [document_session.js](../tools/viewer/web/document_session.js) (the project) and
  [lights_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/lights_wiring.js) (the lights after an edit and while a handle is held).
  What each gave app.js only for `editChangedNow` is no longer returned (`syncVolumes`, `floorNote`, `flagsPanel`,
  `groupPanel`, `targetHelper`, `roomPanel`, `lightsChanged`, `warnLights`).
- **What the cutaway last followed** (`cutKey`) is only the cutaway's now, so it moved out of
  [editor_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/editor_state.js) into `createCutaway`, its setter's call an assignment.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md): the rule that a panel registers its refresh with the edit hub and is not
  called by name from another area, how (a name in `RUNS`, `onHub` in the factory, `STOP`, a run of its own for a
  refresh called in the middle of another), its row in where new code goes, and the hub in how the page fits.

### Copy, paste and placing, and the templates of other maps' pieces, in modules of their own (clipboard.js, library_templates.js)

Editor refactor, stage P8, fourth part: the clipboard, paste and placing, and the library's templates leave app.js, in
two modules, since reading a piece or an effect of another map as a template is asked for by much more than placing
(a project or a prefab opened, the Effects view, the prefab builder) and shares no state with it. Nothing the editor
does changes.

- **[library_templates.js](../tools/viewer/web/library_templates.js)** is new. `createLibraryTemplates` is made
  once by app.js, with a piece's root built and its bounds, the Lights view's and the Effects view's sources, the cover
  blocks' collision meshes, the assemblies of other maps and the helpers. It holds, moved verbatim, the run of app.js
  that was the pieces of other maps: an asset's url (`assetUrl`), whether a target is another map's
  (`isForeignTarget`), a record's id (`recordId`), many records read in a few requests (`readLibraryRecords`,
  `readEffectRecords`), a piece's and an effect's template (`libraryTemplate`, `effectTemplate`), the templates a
  project's records name (`loadForeignTemplates`), and what such a piece costs and says (`foreignCount`, `kilobytes`,
  `foreignCost`, `foreignNote`, `bakeNote`). Its own state is the records and effects read ahead; it gives back the 11
  functions the clipboard, the scene and its textures, the document's state, the prefab builder, prefabs saved and
  placed, Build's panel, the selection, the Effects view and the made pieces call.
- **[clipboard.js](../tools/viewer/web/clipboard.js)** is new. `createClipboard` is made once by app.js, with the
  gizmo, the scene, the pieces' roots made and taken out, the Lights, Effects, Spawns, Landing zones and Buildings
  views' adding and placing, the cover blocks' ground, the templates of other maps' pieces, the floor boxes' outline,
  the busy mark and the hints. It holds, moved verbatim, the four runs of app.js that were these: a clip of the
  selection (`snapshot`) and a floor box's matrix in it (`boxMatrix`, `matrixBox`); a clip pasted (`pasteSnapshot`,
  `linkOf`, `groupTree`, `mapChain`), Copy and Cut (`copySelection`) and Paste (`paste`); placing (`startPlacing`,
  `stopPlacing`, `moveGhost`, `placeAt`, `dropTarget`, `moveTo`, `keepRecipe`, `placeMove`, the preview's two
  materials); the Add panel shown and its tab (`showPieces`, `setLibraryScope`) and an entry of it chosen and placed
  (`chooseEntry`, `entryParts`, `chooseLibraryEntry`, `chooseLibraryEffect`); and a copy dragged off with Shift
  (`copyDragBegin`, `copyDragEnd`). Its own state is the preview's materials; it gives back the 25 functions and
  constants the gizmo, the keys, the pointer handlers, the draw loop, the event wiring, the test hooks and the other
  areas call.
- **[editor_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/editor_state.js)** owns, each with its setter, what of these other areas
  read or set: the preview's redraw asked (`ghostDirty`, `setGhostDirty`: the pointer handlers, keys and Level snap set
  it, the draw loop reads it), the Add panel's tab (`libraryScope`, `setLibraryScopeValue`, beside the clipboard's
  `setLibraryScope`, which also shows the tab: app.js gives it the remembered tab as the page loads), Level snap
  (`levelSnap`, `setLevelSnapValue`, beside app.js's `setLevelSnap`; its value from the browser's storage is given by
  the setter's call where the `let` was, so it is read at the same point), and the url the open map's export is served
  under (`cachePrefix`, `setCachePrefix`: app.js's opening sets it). The components of other maps' pieces read as
  templates (`foreignTemplates`), which app.js's recipes, templates and listings read, are there as a collection.
  The comments of what is placed and of the records of other maps read name the modules.
- **[app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)** makes the templates' module where its run was, given the Lights view's
  and the Effects view's sources and the cover blocks' collision meshes (made further down) as functions that call
  them; the modules made after it (the document's state, the prefab builder, prefabs saved and placed, Build and Play,
  the Effects view) get its functions directly. The clipboard reads values that are not functions and that factories
  made further down return: the cover blocks' floor clearance (`FLOOR_CLEARANCE`) and the Buildings view's layer of the
  map's own buildings (`ownVolumeLayer`). So its module is made after the cover blocks', before the made pieces', and
  given the drawing's `stopWallDrawing` as a function that calls it; the modules made before it that read its
  functions as the page loads are given functions that call them (the prefab builder `snapshot`; prefabs saved and
  placed `snapshot`, `boxMatrix`, `matrixBox`, `groupTree`, `linkOf`, `mapChain`, `startPlacing`, `stopPlacing`; the
  Buildings view `copySelection`; Align `keepRecipe`). The floor boxes' outline geometry and material that a clip's
  preview draws (`ghostEdges`, `ghostLine`) stay in app.js where they were made, with a comment saying why: prefabs
  saved and placed, made before the clipboard, draw them too, and both are given them. What the clipboard's runs made
  as the page loaded now happens later: the preview's two materials, see-through, which three.js sorts by render
  order and depth (it consults the order materials were made only for opaque objects; the preview's meshes are made
  when placing starts, as before), a unit box and the tabs' table. No other code sets a handler between. Each
  assignment to a moved name is its setter's call, with the same value (13 writes). app.js: 4,853 lines to 4,271; its
  `let` statements 34 to 31 (48 names to 44); its top-level functions 262 to 224. [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) names the two
  modules, their rows in where new code goes, the state added to editor_state.js, and the object two modules share.

  and the hints. It holds, moved verbatim, the run of app.js that was the groups': a group's pieces on the map now

### Cover blocks and invisible floors in a module of their own (cover_wiring.js)

Editor refactor, stage P8, first part: the cover blocks' and invisible floors' wiring leaves app.js for one module.
Nothing the editor does changes.

- **[cover_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/cover_wiring.js)** is new. `createCoverWiring` is made once by app.js,
  with what it needs of app.js in one argument object: the gizmo, the camera, the renderer and the scene, the pieces'
  parts and the meshes' caches, the handles' helpers (`projector`, `HANDLE_PICK`, `alongLine`), the Buildings view's
  hint, the selection and the hints. It holds, moved verbatim, the two runs of app.js that were the cover pieces':
  - a cover piece as a piece of the scene: its recipe and the version a block is saved with (`coverRecipe`,
    `coverVersion`, `validCoverValues`), its mesh and material (`ensureCover`), its template (`coverSource`,
    `coverOf`) and the Add panel's Invisible kind (`coverEntries`);
  - the ground under an invisible floor as the game's floor trace finds it: the map's collision asked for once
    (`askLineCollision`, `collisionMesh`), the ground under a point (`groundAt`, `solidGround`, `outwardY`,
    `groundBox`), a floor's tiles' centres and how far its top stands over the ground there (`floorCentres`,
    `floorClearances`), and Fit to ground (`fitFloor`);
  - the piece panel's cover section (`coverPanel`, `floorNote`, `commitCover`) and a new record put on a piece
