### A shadow map's distance field searched once per pair: the same bytes in a twelfth of the time (editor refactor, stage B6)

Every dominant-light shadow map the relight traces (a fresh piece's whole field, the region an edit changes in a
moved piece's) turns its sub-samples' views of the light into a signed distance field in
[shadowmaps.py](../tools/bake/shadowmaps.py) `signed_distance`. Stage B5 measured that search as nearly all of a
fresh piece's shadow-map time: 100 of the bake suite's GroundShapes' 112 s of shadow CPU and 600 of 619 s in a Build
with made ground, at 35 to 57 ns per (sub-sample, window offset) pair, 16.6 s of it in the two 97 x 97 dilations
that find the sub-samples near the edge. It now gives the same arrays, bit for bit, in about a twelfth of the time,
and a baked Build with made ground takes about 47 s instead of 113:
- **The masks near the edge** are grown by `near`, a maximum filter, which grows the window's box along one axis and
  then the other: the same masks as the dilation by the whole box. `change` grows its region by it too.
- **The search** (`nearest_across`) meets each (lit, shadowed) pair within the window once, from the side with fewer
  sub-samples near the edge, and gives its distance to both ends. Only the pairs on the other side have a distance
  worked out, through one linear index into the padded grid, with the world's three axes as arrays of their own.
- **Equal distances** go as before. The old search took the window's offsets in raster order and kept a strictly
  shorter distance, so of equal distances the first offset in raster order set the step count (the half step taken
  off). The side searched from meets its offsets in that order and keeps a strictly shorter one; the other end of
  each pair meets the reverse offsets in reverse order and keeps one as short, so the last of equal ones, the first in
  raster order, wins. A distance is worked out as numpy's norm works one row out, `sqrt((x * x + y * y) + z * z)`, on
  the difference or its negation (which squares the same), so it is the same number from either end.

Checked:
- **B5's dumped inputs** (all 40 calls of GroundShapes' relight, kept by its probe): every answer the old one's, bit
  for bit; 90.3 s of CPU before, 7.6 s after (B5's benched form, the masks and the gather with each pair met from
  both ends, 20.7 s), one process on a loaded computer.
- **[test_shadowmaps.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_shadowmaps.py)** keeps the old function as the reference
  (`old_signed_distance`) and gains `SearchAsBefore`: 40 made-up grids (whole units, where many distances are equal;
  stretched texels with a second island beside the first; a bent, noisy surface; coarse steps in height; holes;
  `only` masks; light on uncovered sub-samples), a case of two equal distances with different step counts met from
  either side, and `near` against the dilation by the box. Broken on purpose in a scratch copy (the found end keeping
  only a strictly shorter distance, the searched end keeping an equal one, `only` not widened, the squares summed in
  another order), the search fails these tests.
- **The images:** three real baked Builds (URB_Bar with its east floor `XComLevelActor_302` moved a tile; EXP-77's
  made-ground project; TempleShip with the console `XComDestructibleActor_35` moved a tile) and the GroundShapes and
  BarScene classes, each run on the code before and after with an empty piece cache in a scratch cache: every map,
  texture cache, picture, piece cache array and relight array the same bytes (the piece cache's report strings differ
  in their `albedoSources` key order only, as two runs of the same code do: a known follow-up).
- **The piece cache's key** is unchanged: `TOOL_FILES` does not hold shadowmaps.py, since no piece's lightmap images
  depend on it and the shadow maps are traced in every baked Build, never kept. A project's kept pieces stay kept.
- **The suites:** bake (701 tests, 1 skipped: XCOM_TRANSPLANT_RING; 679 s on the loaded computer), upk (175, 7
  skipped: the install checks and the reference writer), repo; the ten Builds (`build_outputs.py`, which records the
  relight's command and does not run it) the same before and after. No image changes, so no game check.

**Times** (wall clock and the CPU of the whole process tree, two rounds each, the code before and after taking turns;
other agents were working on this 32-thread computer, its load read at 0 to 54% before and after the runs; a first
round, run beside the rewrite's benches, was slower for both and is left out):

| Run | Before: wall, CPU | After: wall, CPU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| URB_Bar, a floor moved a tile | 55.4 and 52.8 s, 652 and 622 s | 51.1 and 52.1 s, 602 and 615 s |
| EXP-77's made ground | 114.3 and 111.8 s, 910 and 881 s (the relight's pieces 87.2 and 85.4 s) | 46.6 and 46.5 s, 348 and 343 s (pieces 20.4 and 20.1 s) |
| TempleShip, a console moved a tile | 16.9 and 16.8 s, 133 and 129 s | 17.0 and 17.2 s, 132 and 133 s |
| GroundShapes (the class alone) | 49.6 and 50.1 s, 212 and 213 s (pieces 39.0 and 39.5 s) | 19.0 and 18.9 s, 130 and 130 s (pieces 8.5 and 8.3 s) |
| BarScene (the class alone) | 53.2 and 53.6 s, 54 and 55 s | 53.4 and 53.6 s, 55 and 55 s |

A moved piece's shadow map searches only the region its edit changes, so the moved floor and the console gain little
(B5 put the floor's search at about 0.6 s); BarScene traces no shadow map.

**Not built: preparing a large piece once** (the plan's section 9, step 3: one preparation shared by the band jobs
that each prepare the whole piece again). B5 measured what it would save: the repeated preparations are 35.6 s of a
moved floor's Build's CPU (5.6%), the k-d tree in each 0.01 to 0.03 s, worth about 2 s of a 54 s Build's wall time and
nothing elsewhere; the step is dropped.

**Left as it is:** a made piece on an outdoor donor carries two moon shadow maps, the donor's cloned one and its own,
and both are traced; which one the game draws is a game check and the user's decision (the refactor's follow-ups).
ARCHITECTURE.md does not describe the distance field, so it is unchanged.

### The Landing zones view in a module of its own (zones_wiring.js)

Editor refactor, stage P6, fourth view: the Landing zones view's wiring leaves app.js for one module. Nothing the
editor does changes.

- **[zones_wiring.js](../tools/viewer/web/zones_wiring.js)** is new. `createZonesWiring` is made once by app.js,
  with what it needs of app.js in one argument object (as `createSpawnsWiring` is): the camera, the renderer and the
  scene, the landing zones' layer and its storage key, the other views' switches, the header's mission and the Clear
  map window's zones. It holds, moved verbatim, the whole run of app.js from `ZONE_OWN` to `clearedChanged`, the
  zones' heading comment, and the view's switch, `setZonesShown`, its own `let` (whether the layer was hidden before
  the view) and the Add panel's Landing zones kind, `zoneEntries`, which P6's first part left beside the Lights view:
  - the zones drawn (`refreshLandingZones`, `zoneLabel`, `floorTop`, `zoneSoldiers`, `carried`) and the map's own
    landing pieces a moved zone takes along (`movedLandingActors`);
  - a zone picked (`pickZone`, `zoneHit`), its gizmo and its drag, its panel (`landingPanel`, `zoneNotes`) and the
    panel's handlers;
  - the zones changed, each change one undo step (`setZones`, `zonesChanged`, `explicitZones`, `changeZone`,
    `turnZone`, `copyZone`, `deleteZone`), a zone added with a click (`startZonePlacing`, `placeZone`,
    `stopZonePlacing`), and what follows a change of the cleared mark (`clearedChanged`).

  Its own state is inside it: whether the layer was hidden before the view, the gizmo's mode and drag, the drag's zone
  drawn in place, the floor tiles' tops. It gives app.js back the 25 functions and objects app.js, its hooks and the
  other views call, under the same names.
- **[editor_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/editor_state.js)** owns `zonePlacing`, whether the next click places a
  zone, with its setter: app.js's keys and pointer handlers read it.
- **[app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)** makes the module where the run of code ended. `gameToView`, which stood
  in the run, stays where it was (the Spawns view and the test hooks use it too), so the module is made after it; what
  the run does as the page loads (the gizmo made, added to the scene and given its listeners, the panel's handlers)
  happens at the same point, since only declarations stood between. The landing zones' layer and its storage key stay
  where they were made, before the Spawns view, which shows the zones too; both views are given them. The Lights view,
  the scene to and from a document, Build and Play, the Spawns view and the Effects view are made before it and given
  its functions, so they are given functions that call them (`setZonesShown`; `clearedChanged`; `setZones`;
  `pickZone`, `setZonesShown`, `zoneHit`, `zoneState`; `carried`, `setZonesShown`, `zoneState`); `headerMission` and
  `stopPickBox` are made further down, so the module is given functions that call them. Each assignment to
  `zonePlacing` is now its setter's call, with the same value (3 writes). app.js: 8,639 lines to 8,245; its `let`
  statements 63 to 58 (94 names to 88); its top-level functions 542 to 512. [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)
  names the module, its row in where new code goes, the state it added to editor_state.js, and what happens to a
  layer two views use and to a function an earlier stage left behind. The comments of editor_state.js and app.js that
  placed the view in app.js name the module.

Checked:
- **The move:** [moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py) against the commit before: the 30 moved functions are
  the same with the 2 substitutions of a write by its setter's call (without them, 3 differ). app.js against itself:
  its 512 functions are the same, and the 30 moved are only in the old file. The whole moved text, statements as well
  as functions (416 lines), is the old text line for line, the factory's indent aside, with those substitutions and
  the `let` statement whose name went to editor_state.js (now a comment naming it). No code that runs as the page
  loads, before the module is made, reaches what it returns, nor what the Spawns view's returns (a scan of app.js's
  top level).
- `web_names` is clean (60 files), and the node suite passes (31 files).
- **Browser checks** on a test server, on the stage's first commit and on this change: `api-names` (240 names on each
  of its three pages) and `clear-map` (which moves, turns and adds zones) pass; on this change also `streams`,

### One DXT1 decoder: the lightmaps' top mips are read by dxt1.py (editor refactor, stage B3)

[lightmap_textures](../tools/bake/lightmap_textures.py) decoded a lightmap's top mip, the original bake every relight
reads the light before the edit from, through Pillow's DDS decoder, while the relight's encoder and its tests use
[dxt1.py](../tools/bake/dxt1.py)'s (review finding 52: two decoders). `top_mip_rgb` and `top_mip_rect` now decode
with `dxt1.decode_image` and `dxt1.decode_region`. Pillow's decoder rounds a block's two in-between palette colours
down to whole 255ths; dxt1.py keeps them exact. Over every DXT1 lightmap of URB_Bar (180) and TempleShip (316), 15.4%
and 14.1% of the texel channels decode a third or two thirds of a 255th higher than before, the rest the same.

That changes what Builds make:
- **Baked Builds:** the relight's pieces start from the new decoding. Two real baked Builds with the code before and
  after: the Bar's pieces, 671 of its 673 relit pieces' lightmap images changed, 3,208,034 of 9,605,144 texels moved
  (3,127,280 by one 255th, 76,630 by two, 3,507 by three, 617 by four to six); the Bar's made pieces, 350 of 351
  changed, 1,816,217 of 5,327,672 texels moved (1,781,306 by one, 34,187 by two, 724 by three or four). The shadow
  maps (11 and 62 images) are the same. The variant map, its relit texture cache and the relight's record follow.
- **Quick Builds with made walls:** a made wall's even light (`frac_walls.even_light`, the texel of the nearest lit
  piece whose light is nearest that piece's median) is taken from the new decoding, so it is often another texel of
  the same piece, its light within 0.0065 (a box at every 25th actor of the Bar: 36 of 62 another texel, none another
  piece). Of the ten Builds (`build_outputs.py`), the four with made walls (the Bar's made pieces, its wall groups, its
  flags, the police station) make another map.
- **The relight's piece cache:** its key hashes the code of the files the images depend on (`TOOL_FILES`, which hold
  lightmap_textures.py and dxt1.py), so it is raised by this change: a project's next baked Build relights its kept
  pieces once.

A mesh component's LOD lighting records (each LOD's shadow maps, its lightmap and its texture slots, and Enemy
Within's two mesh-swap records and their meshes) were read three times, each reader with its own copy of the layout
and of the licensee branch (review finding 52): by `lighting_records` for the bakers, by `lightmap_fields` for the
places the relight writes, and by `native_fields` for the transplant's references and bulk records. Now
[native_fields.py](../tools/upk/native_fields.py) holds the one reader: `mesh_lods` (the licensee branch, once),
`lod_record`, `lightmap_record`, `object_refs` and `bulk_record`, each value with its place in the package.

- [lighting_records](../tools/upk/lighting_records.py) (which imports `native_fields` beside it, found as it was
  itself) gives its records from it in the same form and key order
  (`component_record`, `lod_record`, `lightmap`, `refs`, `bulk_meta`), and `component_lods` with the rule that a
  StaticMeshComponent ends after its records; `bulk_meta` keeps its refusal of a negative count or size, which the
  shared reader can't have: a texture's unused mips in a separate file say -1 (40 of the Bar's Texture2D records).
- [lightmap_fields.component_fields](../tools/bake/lightmap_fields.py) gives its places from it, through
  `component_lods` so that it refuses what `component_record` refuses, as it did by checking its own reading against
  `component_record`'s; that cross-check of one reader with itself is gone.
- `native_fields`' fields of a mesh component come from it, in the order they did; the check that an inline bulk
  record points to its payload stays its own.
- The relight's images now depend on `native_fields` (lighting_records imports it), so it is in the piece cache's key

  lightmap_fields.py changed too, a project's next baked Build relights its kept pieces once.
- The checks of the three readers are now each reader's: a vertex-colour flag other than 0 or 1, a colour array whose
  stride or count differs from its header, an unknown lightmap type, an object that is not one, and a vertex
  lightmap's bulk record with a negative count or size are refused wherever a component is read (the transplant's

### The copier's guess at object references against the typed walk: listed, and kept (editor refactor, stage B2)

The copy tool's `Walker.refs` ([native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py)) takes every array of 4-byte values
for object references unless its name is on a list (`NOT_REFERENCES`); the typed walk
([typed_props.py](../tools/upk/typed_props.py)) names a reference only where the game's property types say one is.
The stage would have switched the copier to the typed walk if every place where the two differ were a wrong guess and
no copy of the ten Builds changed. Over every export of URB_Bar, TempleShip, URB_PoliceStation and CB2_MP_Blank:

- the typed walk names no reference the guess lacks (30,810, 23,807, 31,671 and 2,990 references named by both);
- the guess names more: 19,439, 13,772, 20,292 and 4,914 places, in 72, 51, 47 and 35 arrays. Nearly all are the
  float tables of the particle modules' curves (`LookupTable`: 19,186 places on the Bar), then other arrays of floats
  (`SoundNodeRandom.Weights`, `ParticleSystem.LODDistances`, `AnimNodeBlendList.TargetWeight`,
  `SoundNodeMixer.InputVolume`) and arrays of whole numbers (`AnimSequence.CompressedTrackOffsets`,
  `PhysicsAsset.BoundsBodies`, `XComVisGroupData`'s `ChildGroups`, `XComBuildingVolume`'s floors'
  `ExternalMeshGroupIndices`): wrong guesses. A few of those numbers fall in the range of object indices, but none of
  their classes is cloned by a copy (an anim sequence, a physics asset, the world's vis group data), and a building's
  mesh group indices are 0 or 1;
- one array the guess has right: `VisGroupActor.DependentOn` (13 places on the Bar, 4 on TempleShip, 18 on the police
  station). Its class is UnrealEd's, an editor's, which no cooked script package holds, so the typed walk can't type
  it; every value of it names a VisGroupActor of the map;
- the dominant light's component, whose properties stand after its leading shadow map, is refused by the guess (it
  walks from where an export's properties usually start) and read by the typed walk.

So the switch stops: the typed walk alone would lose `DependentOn`'s references. Whether the copier should take the
typed walk where it types a property and its guess only where it can't is left as a decision. Nothing of the product
changed; [test_schema.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_schema.py)'s comparison of the two on the Bar now says so and
checks that every `DependentOn` value names a VisGroupActor and that the schema does not know the property.

Checked: the upk suite.

Review finding 51, refactor stage B4, after its seven cuts: `build`'s remaining lines copied the state's fields into
locals before each step and back after it, and kept its results at the end with `BuildState.keep`.

- [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py): `build`'s lines read the inputs and results from the state and
  write each result to its field where they make it (`st.made`, `st.hidden`, `st.effect_record`...), so the copying
  lines (26 statements) and the `keep` call at the end go: it kept every result under the field it already had.

  before they are joined; the manifest). `build` is now the light edits, the steps in their order (`clone_copies`,

  `wall_columns`, `edit_buildings`, `edits_in_place`, `floors_and_cursors`, `write_and_verify`) and the record.
- `BuildState.keep` goes; the fields it made by first use are named in `BuildState` with the step that fills them
  (`groups`, `children` and `hidden_buildings`, which `build` makes; `sections` and `copy_members`, which
  `manifest_parts` keeps for the relight command).

### Build and Play in game in a module of their own (build_play.js)

Editor refactor, stage P4: the Build window's and Play's wiring and state move out of app.js into one module, with
the test squad's line, the prefab builder's Test in game and the build queue's chip. Nothing the editor does
changes.

- **[build_play.js](../tools/viewer/web/build_play.js)** is new. `createBuildPlay` is made once by app.js, with
  what it needs of app.js in one argument object (as `createDocumentSession` is): the views and dialogs it opens
  (Prepare, the Save dialog, a spawn point's marker, the landing zones), the selection, the document session's
  `banner` and `saveProject`, and the prefab builder's document. It holds, moved verbatim:
  - the Build window: `canBuild`, `openBuild`, `buildProject`, `setLastBuild`, `followBuild`, `pollBuild`,
    `openBuildWindow`, `closeBuildWindow`, `renderBuild`, `pathLink`, `playFinished`, `playBuilt`, and the window's
    buttons and key listener;
  - Play in game: `savingFor`, `savingOption`, `playMissions`, `playMissionNote`, `followPlayedMission`,
    `builtAsShown`, `refreshInstalls`, `renderPlayItems`, `playInGame`, `playChosen`, `sendPlay`, `playedFor`,
    `playAgain`, `withZone`, `landHere`;
  - Build's panel, the test squad's dialog and `refreshSquadLine` (the Settings button's handler with them), the
    prefab test's window and `openPrefabTest`; the build queue's `renderQueueChip` and `followQueueForProject`.

  Build and Play are one module, not two: Play has its own button in the build window, a play waits for its build,
  and Play's dialog goes by the build's state, so two modules would share five more names through editor_state.js and
  call each other both ways. Its own state is inside it: the build its window follows and the window's clock, a play
  waiting for its build, and the next play's landing zone, mission and saving. It gives app.js back the twelve that
  app.js calls (`openBuild`, `playInGame`, `landHere`, `refreshInstalls`, `prefabTest` and the others), under the same
  names. The words stay where round two put them, in [build_window.js](../tools/viewer/web/build_window.js) and
  [play.js](../tools/viewer/web/play.js), whose node tests still load nothing of the page.
- **[editor_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/editor_state.js)** owns three more names other areas use, each with its
  setter: `playStatus` (the Missions panel reads its mission kinds), `pickedZone` (the Landing zones view picks it,
  Land here plays it) and `missionPickValue` (the header's Mission picker sets it).
- **[app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)** makes the module where the Build window's code was, after `mapLabel`,
  which it is given, so its handlers and dialogs are set up as the page loads, as before, and its key listener in
  the same place among the page's others. The document session is made before it and calls `followBuild`, `renderPlayItems` and `setLastBuild`, so the session is
  given functions that call them. Each assignment to a moved name is now its setter's call, with the same value.
  What stays in app.js, and why:
  - the Project menu (`renderProjectMenu`): the project's name, revision and recent projects, which are the
    document's; it reads the build status and calls `renderPlayItems`, as before;
  - `mapLabel`: the prepare dialog, the file dialog and the project manager use it too;
  - the prefab builder's Problems check (`checkPrefab`, `problemsPaint`, its chip): the builder resets and runs it,
    and the document session paints it (stage P5's);
  - `selectActors`: a selection that the builder's Problems list uses too;
  - the setup dialog, the file dialog and the build queue's controller: the controller is the project manager's as
    well, and is given the chip's two functions.

  app.js: 12,231 lines to 11,702; its `let` statements 98 to 93 (166 names to 157); its top-level functions 791 to
  760.

Checked:
- **The move:** [moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py) on the 31 moved functions against the commit before.
  With the 4 substitutions of a play status write by its setter's call (8 writes), all 31 are the same. Without
  them, the 7 that write it differ. app.js against itself, with its 4 substitutions (`pickedZone` and
  `missionPickValue` written through their setters): its 760 functions are the same, and the 31 moved are only in the
  old file; without them 6 differ. The whole moved text, the statements as well as the functions (536 lines), is the
  old text line for line, the factory's indent and those substitutions aside, and the one `let` that lost
  `playStatus`.
- `web_names` is clean (54 files). The node suite passes (31 files, with `build_window_test.mjs`, `play_test.mjs` and
  `build_queue_test.mjs` unchanged), and so does the repo suite.
- **Browser checks** on a test server with scratch projects, builds and squad: `api-names`, `streams`, `spawns`,
  `clear-map`, `project-menu`, `squad`, `output-names`, `prefab-test` and `documents` all ran and passed (2 min 25 s,
  with other work on the computer); `streams` skips its streamed piece's edit on the Bar, which draws none.
- **Build and Play from the page,** on a test server playing into a scratch game folder (`serve --install <scratch
  game> --dry-play`): one quick Build from the page (a project saved on the Bar with one piece moved, Ctrl+B, Build):
  the window followed it to "Built", its manifest came back, with its two files. Then `play` and `prepare` with
  `--play --play-project` that project: both pass (51 s). Before the move the same runs passed on the commit before
  (with the checks of the entry before). Land here, which no check presses: a zone picked on the project, Land here
  opens the play dialog for the project landing at that zone.
- **`browser_smoke.py --all`** on fresh test servers, with a scratch cache and `--play-install <scratch game>`: all ten

  two, the police station's light bar and Play run elsewhere; `streams`' edit and the patch previews have nothing on

  through `native_lights.set_property` and poses through `native_copy.set_pose`, both on `native_copy.Walker`, which
  walks with `props.tags`.
- **[map_frame.describe](../tools/bake/map_frame.py)** (a texture's properties and native data): every export the
  same, its bool's size still the one its tag saves. One refusal reads otherwise: the dominant light's component,
  whose properties stand after its leading shadow map (describe reads only textures and does not skip it), is refused
  at the same place as a `ValueError` ("bad property name") where it was the viewer's `FormatError` ("Invalid FName");
  `locate`, its one caller, catches `ValueError`.
- **[inline_lighting](../tools/bake/inline_lighting.py)** (`_tags`, a texture's tags with where each starts and
  ends, so that two can be taken out): every export the same; a refusal of `props.tags` is still an `InlineError`,
  in `props.tags`' words. Its name helper (`lighting_name`), used by nothing else, went with its loop. The dominant
  light's component is refused in other words ("bad property name at 4", where it named the bad index).
- **[light_factory](../tools/bake/light_factory.py)** (`used_guids`, the GUIDs of the light components a Build
  added): `_walk`, a copy of `props.tags` without its bounds checks, is gone; `used_guids` walks with `props.tags`.
  Every export the same; the dominant light's component refused in `props.tags`' words.
- **[lightmap_fields.property_offsets](../tools/bake/lightmap_fields.py)** (where each property's value lies, for
  the relight's writes): every export the same, refusals included (a refusal of `props.tags` is still the viewer's
  `FormatError`; the dominant light's component is refused by its class first, as before). Its now unused `Reader`
  import went.
- **[relight.lightmass_settings](../tools/bake/relight.py)** (a light's, a piece's or the world's Lightmass
  settings): its walk read a name without its number, did not skip a byte property's enum name, checked no bound
  and stopped without a word where the closing None was missing; with `props.tags` such a struct is refused. Every
  export of both maps reads the same (316 settings on the Bar, 1,446 on TempleShip: no member has a number or is a
  byte property, and every struct is closed), so no output changes.
- **[pack_card](../tools/upk/pack_card.py)** (`_properties`, a map pack card's properties): the walk is
  `props.tags`, each value still read and checked by the card's rules. A refusal of the walk is a `CardError` in its
  words, as one of an object whose size runs past the file's end. Its old walk read a byte property of a size other
  than 1 or 8 as one byte and went on from there, and took a name with a negative number; neither is in a card the
  writer makes. Cards read the same: the tests' cards, the install's 188 Maps lines and 453 LZArray lines each
  through a card, and the two cut cards refused alike; every export of both maps too (a card's reader refuses most of
  a map's properties, in the same words).
- **[script_enums](../tools/upk/script_enums.py)** (`_skip_properties`, the properties before an enum's names):
  `props.tags` finds where they end; a refusal is still an `EnumError`, in its words. The old walk took a property
  name's number as unsigned (an enum entry's still is: LWR's padded enums), took a bool's tag size on top of its one
  byte and did not check a struct's or an enum's name; a cooked enum holds no property but its None. The 282 enums
  of the install's XComGame.upk read the same (so `READER_VERSION` stays), and every export of both maps.
- **[typed_props](../tools/upk/typed_props.py)** (the typed walk: every name and object reference of an export, by
  the game's property types): its tagged walk is `props.tags`, which reads and checks the tag's names; the walk notes
  each as a field, the closing None's too, in the order it did. A refusal is still a `WalkError` with the property's
  path, in `props.tags`' words. The old walk read a bool's byte without a bound and measured a struct's or an enum
  property's value from its name, 8 bytes short of where it starts. Every export of both maps gives the same fields,
  starts, ends and untyped arrays.
- **[props.read_props](../tools/upk/props.py)** (a line for each property, read by the research tools and `props.py`'s
  own dump): its walk is `tags()` beside it. The old walk took a name outside the table as `?<index>` and went on,
  and ended without a word at the export's end; such properties are refused now (a `ValueError`). Every export of
  both maps gives the same lines and end; the dominant light's component, whose properties the old walk read as
  garbage until a `struct.error`, is refused at its first name. Its callers (`audit_clear`, `audit_install`,
  `audit_spawns`, `map_layout`) each catch any exception of it, as they did.
- **[Package.tagged](../tools/viewer/package.py)** (the viewer's, which every export, every Build and every reader
  of a map's properties goes through), last and on its own: its walk is `props.tags`, each value decoded as before;
  a refusal of the walk is still a `FormatError`, in `props.tags`' words. Every export of both maps reads the same
  properties, values and ends, and every array read as structs the same (1,872 on the Bar, 1,753 on TempleShip);
  arrays that are not structs are refused alike, in other words. The gate was the export: fresh exports of URB_Bar,
  TempleShip and URB_PierA (two mission streams and three patches read as layers) into scratch caches, three runs
  each with the code before and after, interleaved, gave the same `scene.json` byte for byte in every run, in the
  same time (seconds, before / after, each the mean of three: the Bar 23.7 / 23.1, TempleShip 17.1 / 17.2, the pier
  19.1 / 20.0, its best runs 18.7 / 18.3; other work ran on the computer meanwhile), so `Package.tagged` takes the
  walk itself and not only its bounds checks.
- `props.tags`' docstring names its walkers, and [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) says that tagged properties
  are walked by `props.tags` and by nothing else in what ships.

### The play and prepare browser checks follow the page as it is

Found by the editor refactor's stage P4 before it moved anything: the `play` check, and the `prepare` check's part
with a project (`--play --play-project <id>`), failed on the page as it was. Neither runs in `--all` without
`--play-install`, so neither had been run since the page changed under them. Only the checks change, not the page.

- **[browser_smoke.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_smoke.py) `check_play`:**
  - Play in game on a map alone always opens the play dialog (whether saving is on, and with several missions which
    one). The check waited for it only on a map with several missions, so on the Bar (one mission) it never pressed
    Play. It now answers the dialog whenever it opens. It also checks that the dialog never offers baking and shows
    Enable saving, and hides the mission row for a map of one mission.
  - After a project's build was played, the check read the Game menu's "In the game" row as soon as the menu opened.
    The menu asks the server again as it opens (`refreshInstalls`), so the row could still show the state before the
    play. It now waits for that row's answer, then makes the same assertion.
- **`check_prepare`,** with a project: the build status it stands in for a build that stopped for want of a newer
  export now carries `errorCode: 'export-missing'`, as builds.py's do since the page went by the code (review finding
  55). With only the message, the page rightly offered no Prepare the map.

Checked: on a test server with a scratch game folder (copies of an install's `Default*.ini` files, `XComGame.upk`,
its `XComGame.int` and `XComStrategyGame.int` (which the test squad reads), and `URB_Bar.upk`), run as
`serve --install <scratch game> --dry-play`, with a project saved and quick-built from the page: `play` and `prepare`
with `--play --play-project` pass twice in a row on the page before stage P4 (46 s each, with other work on the
computer). Before this change they failed at the three places above.

### A baked Build that relights nothing says "lighting unchanged" in the Build window, not "lighting not baked"

What a user saw: a baked Build of landing-zone lines alone, a spawn rule alone, the missions list or map picture alone,
or a mission's objects moved or taken out in its stream relights nothing and keeps the map's own lightmaps. The manifest said so
(`quick: false`, `lightingUnchanged: true`) and the project manager showed "baked (lighting unchanged)". The Build
window's light step said "lighting not baked", the quick Build's words, because the light stage was recorded as a quick
Build's (`baked: false`). A baked Build of cover blocks, flags or effects alone already showed "lighting unchanged: no
texel to relight".

- [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py): `Build.edit_unbaked` takes `unchanged`. `Build.light`'s first case (nothing
  in the map changes) calls it with `unchanged=True`, and the light stage is recorded with `baked: true` and
  `lightingUnchanged: true`, as a baked Build of cover blocks alone records it, with the same counts as before. The map,
  the manifest's other fields and the other stages are as they were. A quick Build's light stage is unchanged. A stream
  move still does not relight (the mission types plan, Part E).
- Only the Build window reads the light stage's `baked`
  ([build_window.js](../tools/viewer/web/build_window.js) `stepDetail`, unchanged): with `baked` true and
  `lightingUnchanged` it already gives the unchanged words.
- Checked:
  - [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py)
    `test_a_baked_build_that_changes_nothing_in_the_map_records_its_lighting_unchanged`: a baked Build of landing-zone
    lines alone, and one of a spawn rule alone, record the light stage as baked with the lighting unchanged and no

  - The editor suite (371 tests) and the viewer suite's `test_builds` (23) and `test_buildqueue` (24) pass.

Editor refactor, stage T4 (the bake suite's time). No code changes: what was measured, what was tried and dropped,
and [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)'s rule for tests naming `fixtures.ModuleBuilds`, the builds several
classes of one module share (stage T2).

- Recorded over a whole bake run in one process (each compressed package read through `decomp.decompress_pkg` with
  its content's hash, each package opened, the test running and the code that asked; 694 tests, 409 s): 269 decodes
  took 148 s. Reading a cooked map decodes it in pure Python (about 0.7 s for the Bar), and the package reader keeps
  the last four decoded (`decomp.MEMO_SIZE`).
  - Packages the run wrote: 161 decodes, 90 s, nearly all the Grower's writer checking each package it writes by

  the reader's last four for the next build, which then decoded it itself. A cache in the tests moves the decodes to

### The move check reads the functions inside a page factory

[moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py) counts the functions a page factory declares (`createX`, a module made
as a closure) as functions of its file, named `createX.f`, so a function moved from app.js into a factory is found by
its own name (`--names f`, or paired by name without names). The refactor's page stages move code into factories;
stage P3 had to copy each factory's body into a scratch file to check its move. [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)
says so beside the tool.

Checked: the repo suite (a function moved into a factory compares the same by name and when paired, and a changed one
differs); on stage P3's own move, `--names saveProject,loadProject,navigate` finds all three inside
`createDocumentSession` (`saveProject` differs by the setter substitutions P3 stated in its pairs).

### The guidance names the document session's modules and how a module is made from app.js's functions

Editor refactor, stage P3, its last step: [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) says what the stage made true.

- Section 1, the page: the open document's life (a project opened, saved and left, its drafts, the banner) is
  [document_session.js](../tools/viewer/web/document_session.js)'s, and the scene to and from a document's state is
  [document_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/document_state.js)'s, which a project's file, its drafts and the prefab
  builder's document all go through.
- Section 2 gets two rows: opening, saving or leaving a document, its drafts and the banner; and a new part of what a
  project keeps of the scene (`editStateNow` writes it, `applyState` puts it back, the session carries it between the
  file and those two). The row for an area of the page names `createDocumentSession` beside the two models.
- Section 3, "The page":
  - what [editor_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/editor_state.js) now holds, by what shares it, and that state one
    area alone uses lives inside its factory when it is made by one;
  - a counter taken one step at a time has a `next<Name>()` beside its setter (`nextCopySerial()`);
  - how a module made from many of app.js's functions is made: it destructures its argument object, so moved code
    calls them by the same names; app.js destructures what it returns under the same names; app.js makes it after
    what it is given and before the code that uses it as the page loads; a function made further down is given as a
    function that calls it; and a move into a factory is checked on the factory's body written to a file of its own,
    since `moved_code.py` reads top-level functions.
- Comments that placed the moved code in app.js now name its module: the project open in editor_state.js, the Save
  and Load dialogs' caller in [project_files.js](../tools/viewer/web/project_files.js).

Checked: the repo suite; `web_names` is clean (53 files). The stage's end check, `browser_smoke.py --all` on fresh
test servers with a scratch cache, on the page as this commit has it: its nine runs pass in 9 minutes 48 seconds,
with 70 checks run, as at the stages before. The Play run was left out, since no scratch game folder was given.

### The Build's imports inside functions stay, with why beside them

The compiler part of the editor refactor asks for no import inside a function in `tools/editor`, and moves one to its
module's top only where the order in which Python loads modules stays the same. [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py)
has fifteen in nine functions: `inline_map` (`inline_lighting`), `Build._seed` (`seed_map`, `seed_tiles`),
`Build.shell` (`shell`, `package`), `Build.named_base` (`lightmap_writer`, `package`), `Build._name_copy`
(`package_grow`), `Build._picture` (`map_frame`), `Build.own_landing_groups` (`scene_metadata`, `package`),
`Build.landing_moves` (`native_spawns`, `scene_metadata`, `package`) and `Build.stream_tile_boxes` (`stream_copy`).

None moves. `python -X importtime -c "import build"` shows none of the eleven modules loaded when build.py's top has
run, so each would load earlier, in every process that imports the Build (the tests, the record tools, the examples),
and the order changes. Each is the module of one stage, and most Builds never reach some of them: a quick Build has
no relight, a Build without a patch never seeds from a plan, without a map picture never writes one, without moved
landings or a mission's moved objects never reads them. Importing one after build.py adds, measured with other work
running on the computer, from one module (`map_frame`, 2 ms) to 43 (`shell`, about 110 ms; `stream_copy` 35, about
80 ms; `lightmap_writer` 27 and `inline_lighting` 26, about 25 ms each). The bake's modules also need `tools/bake`
on the path, which their functions put there with `paths.use('bake')` and build.py's top does not. None imports
build.py back, so no cycle keeps them where they are. The server no longer imports build.py at all (since
[game_files.py](../tools/editor/game_files.py)), so its load order is not in question.

A comment at build.py's imports now says so, for whoever wants to move one.

Checked: `moved_code.py` on build.py: every function the same (a comment only). Against the stage's start,
`import build` loads the repository's own modules in the same order, with `game_files` added; of the standard
library, `dataclasses` (the Build's inputs record) is new, and `ast` (the manifest's modules) loads at the top, where
the compiler's imports loaded it later before.

### The scene to and from a document in a module of its own (document_state.js)

Editor refactor, stage P3, second step: the two functions that turn the scene into a document's state and a state back
into the scene move out of app.js. Nothing the editor does changes.

- **[document_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/document_state.js)** is new. `createDocumentState` is made once by
  app.js, with what it needs of app.js in one argument object: the roots' makers and readers, the lights', effects'
  and spawn points' records, and the groups', buildings' and map grid's own parts. It holds, moved verbatim:
  - `editStateNow`: the edits on screen as a project records them, sorted (app.js's `editState` keeps its answer for
    one edit event, as before);
  - `applyState`: a project's state put on the map as exported, with the records naming what the export lacks given
    back to be kept. Its note of a map the install lacks, said once (`foreignNoted`), is inside the module.

  A project's file, its drafts and the prefab builder's document all go through these two.
- **[editor_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/editor_state.js)** owns, each with its setter, the four more names they
  share with other areas: `library` (the Add panel's All maps), `areaBindings` (the Lights view's glowing pieces),
  `loadErrorCount` and `mergedBuildings` (what `allBuildings` worked out).
- **[app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)** makes it just before the document session, which is handed its
  `applyState`. Four functions it is given are made further down, with the Spawns view, so it is given functions
  that call them. Each assignment to a moved name is now its setter's call, with the same value. app.js: 12,407 lines
  to 12,231; its `let` statements 100 to 98 (170 names to 166); its top-level functions 793 to 791.

### The Build takes its inputs as one record, and names its stages' state where it is made

[build.py](../tools/editor/build.py): `Build.__init__` took 21 parameters (22 with `self`: the project, four
folders, the options, the server's ids and five stand-ins a test gives for its tools). It takes one record now,
`BuildInputs`, a frozen dataclass whose fields are those parameters in the same order with the same defaults, so a
caller's arguments move into it unchanged (`build.Build(build.BuildInputs(project, cache, output, lwr, udk, quick=True))`).
`main` makes it from the command line; the server starts `build.py` as a process, so its command line and the server
are as they were. `__init__` reads the record once and keeps each value under the attribute it had (`self.quick`,
`self.lwr`...), so no stage's code changes: that is fewer changed lines than reading `self.inputs.x` in the stages,
which read those attributes in about ninety places, and the tests that set one (`b.enable = ...`) still do.

The state the stages fill (about fifty attributes, from the project's document to the finished manifest) is now named
in `__init__`, grouped by the stage that fills it, with a comment each. Eight reads that went through `getattr` or
`hasattr` with a default (`stage_kept`, `picture_png`, `moves_landings`, `_landing_moves`, `shelled`, `variant`,
`work`, `unpacked_work`) read the attribute: each starts at the value the default gave (`_landing_moves` at None, its
memo filled on the first ask). Nothing a Build does changes.

The callers make the record: `main`, the tests' helpers and their other Builds
([test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py), [test_export_choice.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_export_choice.py)),
[build_outputs.py](../tools/editor/tests/build_outputs.py) and the 39 example generators in

### The document session in a module of its own (document_session.js)

Editor refactor, stage P3, first step: opening, saving and leaving a project, its drafts kept for recovery and offered
back, and the banner under the header move out of app.js into one module. Nothing the editor does changes.

- **[document_session.js](../tools/viewer/web/document_session.js)** is new. `createDocumentSession` is made once
  by app.js, with what it needs of app.js in one argument object (as `createProjectDialog` and
  `createQueueController` are): the scene to and from a document (`applyState`, `editState`), the gizmo, the camera,
  the dialogs and panels it opens or paints, and the page session's id. It holds, moved verbatim:
  - `clearDocumentRecovery`, `dropAdopted`, `discardDraft`, `draftWords`, `recoveryProblem`, `discardAndGo`,
    `askLeave`;
  - `banner` with its timer, `navigate`, `goTo`, `openProject`, `offerProjectDraft`, `projectChanged`,
    `keepRecovery`, `keptDraft`, `saveProject`, `loadProject` and `ensureSavedFor`.

  Its own state is inside it: `navigating` and the banner's timer. It gives app.js back the twelve that app.js
  calls (`banner`, `goTo`, `saveProject`, `projectChanged` and the others), under the same names, so app.js's calls
  are as they were.
- **[editor_state.js](../tools/viewer/web/editor_state.js)** owns the state the session shares with other areas,
  each with its setter: `leaving`, `saving`, `recoveryTimer`, `recoveryKept`, `adoptedDraft` and `recoveryTrouble`
  (the prefab builder's saves use them too); `askedPick` (the mission picker); `lastBuild` and `buildTimer` (the
  Build window; `setLastBuildValue`, since app.js has a `setLastBuild` of its own); `copySerial`, with
  `nextCopySerial()` for the five places that took the next serial with `++`; and `looksReady` and `landingRead`,
  the reads a project waits for.
- **[app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)** makes the session after the functions it is given, and before the
  dialogs that are handed `loadProject` and `ensureSavedFor` as it loads. `openingProgress` is made further down, so
  the session is given a function that calls it. Each assignment to a moved name is now its setter's call, with the
  same value. app.js: 12,767 lines to 12,407; its `let` statements 105 to 100 (184 names to 170); its top-level
  functions 811 to 793.

Checked:
- **The move:** [moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py) on the 18 moved functions against the commit
  before. The factory's body was written to a scratch file first, since the tool reads a file's top-level functions.
  With the 14 substitutions of a write by its setter's call, all 18 are the same. Without them, the 10 that write
  shared state differ. app.js against itself, with its own 19 substitutions: its 793 functions are the same, and the
  18 moved are only in the old file. The top-level statements that changed (the `let`s taken out, `looksReady`'s
  first read, the session made) were read in the diff.
- `web_names` is clean (52 files), and the node suite passes (31 files).
- **Browser checks** on a test server, before (on the commit before) and after: `api-names`, `project-menu`,
  `projects`, `prepare`, `modals`, `draw-errors`, `failed-reads` and `documents` all pass (2 min 30 s and
  2 min 36 s, with other work on the computer).
- **The saved file:** a project holding every kind of record (stage P2's scene on the Bar: copies, made pieces, a
  broken copy, cover blocks, lights, an effect, a sound and a lens flare) saved, reopened and saved again, on a server
  of the commit before and one of this change. Both revisions' files are the same byte for byte, the server's
  `savedAt` and `created` aside.

Left: the scene to and from a document (`editStateNow`, `applyState`) is the next step.

### The editor's imports inside functions: the one that can move goes to its module's top, the rest are listed

The compiler part of the editor refactor (plan section 2) asks for no import inside a function in `tools/editor`.
Moving an import to a module's top changes when the imported module loads, so one moves only where the imported
module is already loaded by the time the importing module's top runs; the others stay where they are, each listed here
with why. Nothing the editor does changes.

- **Moved:** [made_edits.py](../tools/editor/made_edits.py) `wall_look_storeys` imported `frac_wall`; the import is
  now at the module's top, after `import made_split`. `frac_wall` is loaded there already: the module's
  `import ground as ground_shapes` loads it (through `frac_slab`). Checked: the order in which Python loads modules
  (`python -X importtime -c "import <module>"`) is the same before and after for `compiler`, `made_edits`,
  `compiler_tables`, `light_edits`, `mission_edits`, `piece_lookup`, `prefab_stage` and `build` (an `import frac_wall`
  planted at `compiler_tables`' top shows as a different order); `moved_code.py` finds `wall_look_storeys` the same
  but for the import line.
- **Left, in what the release ships** (each would load a module that is not loaded yet when the importing module's
  top runs, so every process that imports the compiler or the Build would load it, earlier or for the first time):
  - [compiler_tables.py](../tools/editor/compiler_tables.py) `donor_shape` and `made_wall_along`: `frac_wall`. The
    tables module loads first, before every family; `frac_wall` loads later, with the made pieces' family.
    `made_wall_along` also catches an `ImportError` of it.
  - [light_edits.py](../tools/editor/light_edits.py) `submitted_light`: `storable_cone` from the viewer's
    `lights`, which no compile loads otherwise (only a light with a cone out of range reaches it).
  - [mission_edits.py](../tools/editor/mission_edits.py) `spawn_rules_notes`: `spawnrules`, which the compiler does
    not load (a Build loads it in `build.py`, after the compiler); only a compile with the library of an install
    reaches it.
  - [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `find_export`: the viewer's `catalogue`, which only finding an
    export needs.
  - [piece_lookup.py](../tools/editor/piece_lookup.py) `Library.record`, `Library.load` and `Library.effect`: the
    viewer's `library` and `projects`. The compiler does not load them, and `library` imports the compiler back
    inside its own functions.
  - [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py): fifteen imports in nine functions (`inline_lighting`, `seed_map`,
    `seed_tiles`, `shell`, `package`, `lightmap_writer`, `package_grow`, `map_frame`, `scene_metadata`,
    `native_spawns`, `stream_copy`), each the module one stage of a Build needs; none is loaded when `build.py`'s top
    runs. (`build.py` is the next stage's, C11.)
- **Left, in what does not ship:** the tests' 47 (in `build_outputs.py`, `compile_record.py`, `test_build.py`,
  `test_compiler.py`, `test_compiler_generated.py`, `test_patchtool_record.py` and `test_spawn_edit_fixtures.py`) and
  one example generator's (`exp51_project.py`). A test loads a module for the one test that needs it, or after setting
  up what the module reads when it loads (the record tools import `compiler` and `build` once their scratch settings
  and wrappers are in place); the rule is read as being about the product's code.

Checked: the compile recorder (`compile_record.py`): the same 1,091 calls of 369 tests as at the start of stage C8;
the ten Builds (`build_outputs.py`), quick and baked, the same; the editor suite (369 tests) and the release suite
(15).

  it never imports the compiler. The names of both modules are checked against `test_names.py` (no two tracked

### The compiler's floors in a module of their own

Review finding 23, the editor refactor's stage C9: the floor a project leaves and the floors its pieces are checked
against moved out of the `Compiler` class, the last of the families of the plan's table. A move: nothing the compiler
does changes.

- **[floor_edits.py](../tools/editor/floor_edits.py)** is new. `FloorEdits` holds the family's fifteen methods,
  moved from [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) with their names and bodies unchanged but for where they
  read the compiler (`self.c.`): the cursor's floors (`cursor_storeys`, `with_made_slabs`, `grown_storeys`), the floor
  the project's flat pieces give (`added_floors`, `floor_headroom`), ladders' climbs (`ladder_ends`, `ladder_climbs`,
  `flag_ladders`), the building floor a copy stands in (`floor_at`, `floor_boxes_now`, `floor_note`), and the map's
  low scenery made walkable and its floor tiles still there (`scenery_floor`, `floor_kept_off`, `floor_now`,
  `floor_records_now`). It owns `ladder_jobs` (the moved and copied ladders whose climb is still to be checked, which
  the compiler's `override` and `add` fill through it), made in its `__init__`. It takes what it shares with the
  compiler from [compiler_tables.py](../tools/editor/compiler_tables.py) and never imports the compiler.
- **The memo:** `floor_boxes_now` made its result the first time it was asked for, read through
  `getattr(self, '_floor_boxes_now', None)` (plan 2.5). The family's `__init__` now sets `_floor_boxes_now` to `None`
  and the method reads it plainly; that is the only change `moved_code.py` finds in it. It was the last memo of the
  compiler read through `getattr`.

  through the compiler. `made_cursors`, which only `with_made_slabs` uses, is now imported by the family, not the
  compiler. What the compiler's `index_export` reads (the map's floor tiles, `floors`, and its building floors' boxes,
  `floor_boxes`) stays the compiler's: the family and the buildings' family read it there.

  which the ten Builds run) and `Compiler.floor_kept_off` (test_compiler_flags.py).
- **Where the plan's list differs from the code:** it does not; "the floor memos" are now one, `_floor_boxes_now`
  (the others went with the buildings' and missions' families). `hide_helpers`, which sits among the ladders' methods

- **The guidance:** [structure.json](../tools/repo/structure.json) lists `floor_edits.py` under

### The guidance names piece_records.js as the one writer and reader of a piece's record

Editor refactor, stage P2, its last step: [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) says what the stage made true.

  app.js's counts (exit 0). The rules it still holds are unchanged: no page module imports app.js, no import cycle
  among the page's modules, what ships imports no lab, research or test module, no shipped function changes

### A paste makes its copies through optionsOf

placing, drawn wall, floor or ground piece, look change and placed prefab goes through, makes `addedObject`'s options
for each copied piece with [piece_records.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_records.js)'s `optionsOf`. Its record-like
input is the copy's new names, its pose and its links named anew, and its state is the clip entry's own. Nothing a
paste makes changes.

links. `addedObject` takes its options by name, so the order is not seen anywhere. A paste's lights and effects are

after. [moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py) over app.js: 810 of its 811 functions are the same, and
`pasteSnapshot` differs. `web_names` is clean.

### A prefab placed reads its records through optionsOf

Editor refactor, stage P2: `prefabClip` in [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js), which reads a saved prefab into the
clip a placing pastes, reads each piece's record through
[piece_records.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_records.js)'s `optionsOf`. Nothing a placed prefab makes changes.

- A copy of a piece: its clip entries take their pose, `unit` (its actor), `link` (its link tag), `partner` and state
  from `optionsOf(record, 'piece', stateOf(record))`.

- A recipe light: its recipe, values and pose for the recipe light come from `optionsOf(record, 'light')`.
- An effect, a sound or a lens flare: its original, pose and values from `optionsOf(record, 'effect')`. Its values
  are still placed only where their family builds, and never for a lens flare.

[app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js), which the prefab builder's opening uses too) makes each added thing from its
record through [piece_records.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_records.js)'s `optionsOf`. Nothing the editor makes of a
record changes.

- A copy of a piece: `addedObject`'s options are `optionsOf(record)`, made for each of its parts as before.
- A cover block: `optionsOf(record, 'cover')`, which takes no link, tint, flags or blasts from its record, as before.
- A light (`addedLightOf`): its names, pose, recipe or original and values come from `optionsOf(record, 'light')`. The
  page finds its source (the recipe made, or the map's light it copies) as before.
- An effect, a sound or a lens flare (`addedEffectOf`): from `optionsOf(record, 'effect')`, whose values are the
  page's (`keptValues`). They are now worked out before the page looks for the original, where they were after; the
  conversion has no other effect.

Checked: the browser recording of every kind of piece (the first of these entries says what it holds) gives the same
arguments to `addedObject`, `addedLight` and `addedEffect` as on the commit before, the same options in the same order
included, with the same roots and records. [moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py) over app.js: 808 of its 811
functions are the same, and `applyState`, `addedLightOf` and `addedEffectOf` differ. `web_names` is clean.

### A prefab's records written through recordOf

Editor refactor, stage P2: the page's writer of a prefab saved from a selection (`prefabRecords` in
[app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)) writes each piece's record through
[piece_records.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_records.js)'s `recordOf`, on its `'prefab'` path: a copy of a piece
(with its library recipe when it is of another map), a cover block, an effect, a sound or a lens flare, and a light,
which a prefab keeps as a recipe light whatever it copied. Nothing the editor writes changes.

How the prefab's records differ from a project's, each kept as it was:
- they have no `id`, so a prefab's units have none;
- a recipe light's `light` comes before its pose (`'prefab'` path);
- a copy of a map's light is saved as a recipe light, with every value and its cone in the Build's ranges, and a point
  light's rotation zeroed (worked out in `prefabRecords`, as before);
- a lens flare's values are never written (`prefabRecords` gives a flare none, as before); a project writes those a
  flare copy holds;
- `from` is a new record of the three names, where a project's piece copy keeps its root's own;
- the partner is named by its name in the prefab, after every piece is named (as before).

Checked: the browser recording of every kind of piece (the entry before this one says what it holds) gives the same
records from all three writers, field for field and in the same order, and the same arguments to the readers, as on
the commit before. [moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py) over app.js: 810 of its 811 functions are the same,
and `prefabRecords` differs. `web_names` is clean.

### A piece's whole record written and read in piece_records.js (recordOf, optionsOf)

Editor refactor, stage P2, first step: the page gets one writer and one reader of an added thing's whole record, beside
the conversion of a piece's state that review finding 6 put in the same module. Nothing uses them yet: the writers
and readers of app.js move onto them one by one in the commits after this. Nothing the editor does changes.

- **[piece_records.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_records.js)**:
  - `recordOf(unit, path)`: what the page knows of one added thing (a unit) as its record, by the unit's form: a copy
    of a piece (its names, source, components sorted, pose, link tag, partner, state and library recipe), a cover
    block, a recipe light or a copy of a map's light, an effect, a sound or a lens flare. The fields and their order
    are the ones a project, a prefab and the builder's document have always written. The unit's `id` is written only
    when it has one, as a prefab's records have none. `path` is `'project'` (a project and the builder's document)
    or `'prefab'` (a prefab saved from a selection): a prefab has always put a recipe light's values before its pose.
  - `optionsOf(record, form, state)`: a record as what makes its root again. For a piece it gives `addedObject`'s
    options, its state the record's or the one a paste's clip entry carries. A cover block's options take no link,
    tint, flags or blasts from its record. For a light and an effect it gives what `addedLight` and `addedEffect`
    are made from, the page finding the template.
  - It imports `keptValues` from [effects_rules.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_rules.js), itself pure: no
    three.js and no page.
- **[piece_records_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/piece_records_test.mjs)** checks each form's fields and their
  order on both paths, the components sorted in a copy, and each form read back.

Checked: the node test; `web_names` is clean (51 files).

### The copy tool's tests share builds: NativeCopy makes nine edits in three packages, not nine

Editor refactor, stage T1 (the bake suite's time). No product code changes. `NativeCopy` built and wrote the bar
once per edit, though most of its tests' edits touch different pieces. A build costs a second or more whatever its
edit, much of it the writer's check that decodes the written map again, so building once what the tests built one by
one is where the time is.

- [fixtures.py](../tools/bake/tests/fixtures.py): `SharedBuild`, one package made from several tests' edits,
  each test reading back its own part in a subtest named for its edit, so every failure names the edit it checks.
  When the shared build fails, each edit is built alone: those that fail fail their own tests, and the others are
  built together again, so one edit's failure is never read as its neighbours'. `native_build` joins the edits'
  arguments for `native_copy.build` (refusing two edits that name one piece, hidden piece or assembly), and
  `NativePart` gives an edit its records of the manifest: its copies' sections, hidden pieces, assemblies, ladders,
  vans, floor listings, and the pieces whose columns list its copies.
- [test_native_copy.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_native_copy.py), `NativeCopy`: two shared `native_copy` builds,
  one of the ladder moved without its climb, the police car turned, door 6 moved with door 7 deleted, and a corpse
  copied with another deleted; the other of the van copied and the floor strip moved up (the van's copy seeds tiles
  the car's seeds too, as the strip's do the ladder's, so they are in different builds). One shared Grower clones the
  two pieces at a full rotation and the car turned about a tile corner. Nine packages became three.
- Tests that keep a build of their own: those that count the whole map (the level's actors, its rebuild volumes, its
  list's end, its net indices, every wall's columns), those whose edits meet another's (the wall copy and the hidden
  wall: door 6, door 7 and wall 16 are in the door move), another source map (the grown bar), the relight's, and one
  build that makes each kind of edit alone: a copy (the strip at its own height; the car and lamp), a move (the ladder
  with its climb), a delete (the van's 14 parts), break-group links.
- Checked:
  - The same 45 tests by name pass before and after (the runner's logs compared), the count unchanged.
  - Each of the nine shared edits, built alone, gives the same records as its part of the shared build, the new
    exports' indices and names aside (a scratch comparison: no difference).
  - Three test-only breaks of `native_copy.py`, made and taken back, never committed, each fail their own edit's
    test and no other: a copy (the floor strip's copy made a unit higher: `test_a_storey_floor_copy_moved_up...`
    fails, in its shared part and its own build), a move (door 6 moved a tile off its wall:
    `test_a_door_copy_joins_its_walls_columns...` fails), a delete (KAsset_1 left in the level:
    `test_a_physics_prop_is_cloned...` fails). A fourth, the corpse's copy raising, fails that test alone as an edit
    that did not apply; the other three edits of its build are built again together and pass.
  - Times, before and after back to back, while other agents' suites loaded the computer (so noisy):
    - `NativeCopy` alone through the runner, four rounds: 29.7 s before and 23.6 s after, 29.9 and 23.3 s in the two
      quiet rounds; 59.8 and 52.7 s, 64.6 and 44.8 s in the two loaded ones. Its set-up, which makes the three shared
      packages, takes 3.5 to 5 s of that.
    - The whole file through the runner, three rounds: 45, 80 and 44 s before; 68, 41 and 37 s after.
    - The class wrote 23 packages and now writes 17. The baseline at the stage's start, the whole bake suite run
      alone: `NativeCopy` 38.4 s (a whole-suite run reads about twice a file run's seconds for each test).
- Not in this change: `RebuildTemplate`'s two builds of the police station (a door, a car) touch different pieces and
  could share one build. Every package's write decodes the written map again in pure Python to check it (about
  0.6 s a build); that is the writer's, not the tests'.

[ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)'s rules for tests state the shared-build pattern.

### The compiler's pieces' flags in a module of their own

Review finding 23, the editor refactor's stage C4: the pieces' flags family moved out of the `Compiler` class, as
the spawn, effects and lights families were. A move: nothing the compiler does changes.

- **[flag_edits.py](../tools/editor/flag_edits.py)** is new. `FlagEdits` holds the family's four methods, moved
  from [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) with their names and bodies unchanged but for where they read
  the compiler (`self.c.`): `flags_valid`, `flag_plan`, `stationary_flags` and `copy_flags`. It owns the family's
  state, made in its `__init__`: the map's own pieces whose flags change where they stand, the spec's `pieceFlags`
  (`edits`, which was the compiler's `flag_edits`), the actors whose floor such an edit takes away or gives
  (`floor_off`, `floor_on`) and the report's counts (`counts`, was `flag_counts`). Its tables, `FLAGS_EXPORT` and
  `FLAGS_WALL`, moved with it; nothing read them through the compiler. It takes what it shares with the compiler
  from [compiler_tables.py](../tools/editor/compiler_tables.py) and never imports the compiler.
- **The compiler** makes one `FlagEdits` for each `Compiler` (`self.flag_edits`, so the name now holds the family,
  not the list) and checks and builds each record's flags through it from `overrides`, `override`, `added` and
  `add`. Everything else of the compiler that reads the family's state reads it through it: the ladders near a flag
  change (`flag_ladders`, `ladder_climbs`), the floors (`added_floors`, `floor_kept_off`, `floor_records_now`), `spec`
  and the report. Two of those read the state through `getattr` with a default (`getattr(self, 'floor_off', set())`
  in `floor_records_now`, `getattr(self, 'floor_on', {})` in `added_floors`); the compiler's `__init__` always made
  both, so the default was never taken, and they now read `self.flag_edits.floor_off` and `.floor_on`. No method was
  left behind as a forwarder: nothing outside the compiler calls one by name.
- **The guidance:** [structure.json](../tools/repo/structure.json) lists `flag_edits.py` under
  `compiler families`. `compiler.py` went from 4,442 to 4,321 lines, within a twentieth of its ceiling, so the
  ceiling stands. [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) lists the family.

Checked, against the start commit of stage C2 (the compile record and the ten Builds recorded in a scratch worktree
of it) and against stage C3's head (the moved code):
- the compile recorder (`compile_record.py`): the same 1,091 calls (822 compiles, 269 native splits) of 369 tests;
- the ten Builds (`build_outputs.py`), quick and baked, the same;
- `moved_code.py`: the four methods the same (substitutions `self.` to `self.c.`, the four state names, and
  `flag_plan`'s calls back to `self.`); of the 133 functions left in `compiler.py`, 132 the same once the call
  sites' substitutions are made (the two `getattr` reads among them), and `Compiler.__init__`, which makes the
  family in place of its state;
- the moved tables' values, read by import, the same;
- `import flag_edits` alone in a fresh process, and `compiler.py --help`;
- the editor suite (369 tests), the release suite (15; its module list finds `flag_edits.py` by import) and the
  repo suite (40).

### The move checks: substitution pairs from a file, and a write to an imported name

Two gaps the refactor's first page stage met in its checks, closed for the stages after it:
- [moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py) takes `--subst-file <json>`, a list of `[OLD, NEW]` pairs applied
  after the `--subst` ones. `--subst OLD=NEW` ends OLD at its first `=`, so it could not state a write moved to its
  owner's setter (`selected = hit` to `setSelected(hit)`), which every page stage needs.
- [web_names.py](../tools/viewer/tests/web_names.py) turns on ESLint's `no-import-assign`
  ([web_names.config.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/web_names.config.mjs)): an assignment to an imported name (which
  throws only when its line runs) is reported, so a write left behind by a move to `editor_state.js` needs no grep.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)'s list of the move tools says both.

Checked: the repo suite (a `--subst-file` pair holding `=` makes a changed function the same, a malformed file exits
2); `web_names` is clean on the page's 51 modules and reports a planted write to an imported `data` as
`no-import-assign`.

Editor refactor, stage P1: the state several of the page's areas use gets one owner module, so that the later stages

    `projectMissions`, `projectPicture` and `projectSpawnRules`;

  functions 812 to 811.

### The compiler's shared tables in a module of their own, and the spawn family no longer imports the compiler

Review finding 23, its next step: a home for what the compiler and its edit families share, so that a family in a
module of its own needs nothing from `compiler.py`. A move: nothing the compiler does changes.

- **[compiler_tables.py](../tools/editor/compiler_tables.py)** is new. It holds each table and helper of
  [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) that more than one reader takes: the compiler and a family, or two
  families (the effects, lights, flags, made pieces, buildings, missions, groups and floors families, whose methods
  are still the `Compiler`'s, counted as families). 34 names, its `__all__`:
  - tables: `FAMILIES`, `CLASS_FAMILY`, `ASSEMBLY_FAMILIES`, `EPS_LOCATION`, `TILE`, `STOREY`, `QUARTER`,
    `POSE_SLACK`, `IDENTITY`, `FLOOR_THICK`, `HEADROOM`, `EFFECT_KINDS`, `STAGE_MAPS`, `MADE_KINDS`,
    `FRAC_WALL_END_INSET`, `FRAC_WALL_BOTTOM`, `FRAC_WALL_TOPS`, `FRAC_SLAB_LOOKS` and `GROUND_LOOKS` (with the
    private `_ground_looks` that reads it);
  - helpers: `short`, `tidy`, `game_round`, `tile_corner`, `keyable`, `target_key`, `world_box`, `union`,
    `turned`, `original_key`, `map_building_id`, `donor_shape`, `wall_heights` and `made_wall_along`;
  - the `LibraryError` exception, which the effects family and the compiler both raise or catch.

  A table or helper only the compiler reads stayed in `compiler.py`; one only a family reads stayed too, for that
  family's own stage. The module puts `tools/viewer` and `tools/bake` on the path through `paths.use()` (for
  `export_math` and the Build's `looks`), so it imports on its own.
- **The compiler** takes them with `from compiler_tables import *`, so `compiler.FAMILIES` and every other moved name
  is the same object as before for whatever reads it through the compiler (`build.py`, `prefab_stage.py`, the
  viewer's modules, the tests, which change `compiler.FAMILIES['spawn']` in place). It imports
  [spawn_edits.py](../tools/editor/spawn_edits.py) at the top (`SpawnEdits`, and `SPAWN_COPY_KINDS`, the one spawn
  table it reads); the import inside `Compiler.__init__` is gone.
- **The spawn family's tables** (`SPAWN_EDIT_KINDS`, `SPAWN_VALUE_KEYS`, `SPAWN_WORDS`, `SPAWN_COPY_KINDS`,
  `SPAWN_BOOLS`) moved into `spawn_edits.py`, which now imports `compiler_tables` and not the compiler. Nothing read
  the four others through the compiler, so the compiler names only `SPAWN_COPY_KINDS` again.
- **The guidance:** [structure.json](../tools/repo/structure.json) lists `spawn_edits.py` under `compiler families`,
  so the structure test holds that it does not import the compiler (planted: the start commit's `spawn_edits.py`
  fails it, at its import line). [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) says where a shared table goes (a new row),
  how a family takes what it shares with the compiler, and that `spawn_edits.py` is listed. `compiler.py` went from
  5,622 to 5,376 lines, under a twentieth, so its ceiling stands.

Checked, against the start commit recorded in a scratch worktree of it:
- the compile recorder (`compile_record.py`): the same 1,091 calls (822 compiles, 269 native splits) of 369 tests;
- the ten Builds (`build_outputs.py`), quick and baked, the same, both records reading the same exports (2 minutes
  each);
- `moved_code.py`: the 16 moved functions and methods the same; every function left in `compiler.py` the same but
  `Compiler.__init__`, which lost the import; `spawn_edits.py`'s 11 methods the same;
- the moved tables, which `moved_code.py` does not compare: each assignment's syntax tree the base's, and each value
  read by import (the base's `compiler` against `compiler_tables`, `spawn_edits` and the new `compiler`) the same;
  the compiler module's names are the base's less the four spawn tables and `_ground_looks`, which nothing read
  through it;
- `compiler.py --help`, `import spawn_edits` and `import compiler_tables` each alone in a fresh process;

Left as it was: the Build's manifest hashes `compiler.py` among its tools but neither `spawn_edits.py` nor
