### Two record tools for the editor refactor: the ten Builds byte for byte, and every compile of the editor suite

The editor refactor's checks (its plan's stage 0, items 0.1 and 0.2): a step that touches the compiler, the Build,
the copy tool, the package tools or the relight must leave their output as it was, and these two tools record that
output on the code before and after so that the two can be compared. They are tools, not tests: the test runner does
not run them, and their records are not checked in. No product code changed.

- **[build_outputs.py](../tools/editor/tests/build_outputs.py)**, the ten Builds.
  - `record --out <folder> [--only NAME ...]`: ten project inputs, each a quick Build and a baked Build into scratch
    folders under `<folder>`, with the Build's `run` hook a recorder. Every tool runs as in a real Build except the
    relight (relight.py, or native_copy.py `--bake`): its command line and the SHA-256 of each file it names are
    recorded, and in its place native_copy.py makes the edit without `--bake` and a stand-in relight record lets the
    Build go on. `outputs.json` holds, for each input and Build, the SHA-256 of every file of the package (the
    variant map, the intro and stream copies, the readme), the manifest and compile report (times, attempt ids,
    the tools' own hashes and folders masked; the Build's clock is fixed), the relight's command (folders masked)
    and the native edit the Build wrote; and for each input its project document, the compile's whole spec, report
    and native edit, and the export it read.
  - The ten inputs are made by the generators in [tools/editor/examples](../tools/editor/examples), each run in a
    process of its own on scratch settings with its compile recorded and its own Build refused. Seven of them merge
    the documents of two or three generators on one map (refused where two documents disagree on a piece or an
    override); two add a field or a piece in code (a spawn rule; an invisible floor). Together they hold every lane
    of the native edit: the Bar's copies, moves and deletions with cars and lights; effects, sounds and flares; spawn
    points moved, given values, copied and deleted, with a spawn rule; made walls with openings, flags and a break
    group, made floors, roofs and ground, map pieces broken; cover blocks that break with their group and an
    invisible floor; a building of the project and the map's own edited; Clear map on a larger grid with landing
    zones; a car, a door and a ladder of other maps; pieces' flags; cars and made walls on the police station; and its
    data recovery's capture point moved in its mission stream. `--list` prints each input with its lanes, and
    `record` fails when a lane (read from `native_split`'s and native_copy.py's code too) is in none of them.
  - `compare <before> <after>` lists what differs by input (files, manifest keys, compile keys, the relight's
    command, the export read) and exits 1.
  - The install and the cache come from the settings or `--game`/`--cache` (exit 2 without them). The cache is only
    read: the exports' scene.json and the library index are copied into a scratch cache, where the library makes
    pieces of other maps afresh from the install. A whole record takes about two minutes.
- **[compile_record.py](../tools/editor/tests/compile_record.py)**, every compile of the editor suite.
  `record --out <file>` runs the editor suite's test files in one process with `compiler.compile_project` and
  `compiler.native_split` wrapped before any test file is imported (so the files that import the names themselves
  reach the wrappers), and writes each call in order: the test, a hash of its inputs (document, scene, families on
  and off, the kind of library) and its outputs whole (a compile's spec, report and the native split of its spec; a
  native split's patch spec and native edit). `compare <before> <after>` gives each test's first differing call with
  the differing keys, and exits 1. Masked, in the inputs only: the light GUIDs test_compiler makes from Python's
  string hash and the savedAt of test_prefab_stage's project, which are new each run; nothing else differs between
  two runs.
- **[test_record_tools.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_record_tools.py)** (editor suite, no install): the two
  tools' compares say a difference for its input or test alone and compare every part of a record; the masks, the
  lanes, the merge and its refusals, and the planted byte.

**How a stage uses them** (a tool checks the code of the checkout it runs in): make a scratch worktree of the
stage's base commit and record there (`build_outputs.py record --out <base folder>`,
`compile_record.py record --out <base file>`), record again on the stage's head, and compare the two records of each
tool. Both build records must read the same exports: if the cache gets a newer export of an input's map between
them, `compare` says so.

Checked: two records of one commit compare equal (build_outputs: ten inputs, quick and baked, about two minutes a
record; compile_record: 1091 calls, 822 of them compiles, of 369 tests, about ten seconds); a record with one byte
planted in one copy's pose (bar-pieces, the destructible copy's x) differs from the first for that input alone, in
its document, compile, both maps, manifests, compile reports, native edits and relight command; a record with no
install or no cache exits 2; the editor suite (369 tests) and the repo suite.

Known gaps: no input makes an edit that only a patch or a larger grid makes, so the Build's relight-alone path
(relight.py on a named copy of the map) is not among the ten; the baked Build's map is the quick one's, since the
relight is not run (a step in tools/bake or tools/upk runs real baked Builds as well, by the plan's ground rules);
compiles in a subprocess of a test are not recorded.

### The look measurers ship in the release

A Build measures a made piece's donor afresh when the looks' catalogue lacks its look at the look's measurer version
([looks.py](../tools/bake/looks.py) `resolve`). It reached the measurer through `importlib` by its name, which the
release's list of modules ([make_release.py](../tools/release/make_release.py) `modules`, read from the imports)
cannot see: `wall_measure`, `slab_measure` and `ground_measure` were not in the zip, so in a release that case
stopped the Build on a missing module instead of measuring the donor. `looks.measurer` now imports each by name, so
all three ship. [wall_measure.py](../tools/bake/wall_measure.py) no longer reaches the lab: its `install_package`
(used by the wall-look audit's research script) reads the settings' install, not the lab's path helper, and
`tools/lab` is off its path, so nothing shipped imports the lab.

Found by the refactor's stage 0 (the structure test's work over what ships); not met in a release build.
Checked: a new release test (`test_the_look_measurers_ship`) gives each measurer the looks name in the module list,
and failed before (none of the three was in it); the release and repo suites pass (the structure test included:
`wall_measure.py` stays at its ceiling); the bake suite's looks, measurers and catalogues tests pass;
`install_package('URB_Bar')` opens the settings' install's package.

  - the rules, each with its reason;

  - **File size:** a tracked Python file or page module over 1,500 lines is listed with a ceiling.

### A checker that a move of code changed nothing, and the test runner's logs carry each line's times

Two of the tools the editor refactor's checks need (stage 0, items 0.3 and 0.5). No product code changes.

- [moved_code.py](../tools/repo/moved_code.py): `moved_code.py <base commit> <old file> <new file> [--subst OLD=NEW
  ...] [--names a,b,c]`. The old file is read at the base commit through Git, the new one from the working tree.
  - Python: each function's or method's syntax tree, after the substitutions, is compared with the old one's.
    Whitespace, line breaks, comments and a docstring's wrapping make no difference. A method may change class:
    `--names effect_of` finds it in any class, `Compiler.effect_of` qualifies it, and `OLD=NEW` names each side
    (also a rename).
  - JavaScript: each top-level function (`function`, `async function`, `export function`, `const f = (...) =>`,
    `const f = function`) is compared by its tokens, so whitespace and a comment's wrapping make no difference.
  - Without `--names`, every function in both files is compared, by its qualified name, else by its own name when
    it is in one class only on each side. Those in only one file are listed.
  - It prints a diff of each function that differs, leaving out lines that differ only in whitespace. Exit status 1
    if any differs or a named one is missing, 2 if it could not compare.
  - Its readers (`python_functions`, `js_functions`, `js_inner_functions`, `js_top_level`) are also what the structure
    test measures with.
- [run_tests.py](../tools/run_tests.py): each line of a suite's log starts with two times in seconds since the suite
  started, `[begun ended] `: when the line's first character came and when its end did.
  - unittest writes a test's name when the test starts and its verdict when it ends, so a test's line gives its start
    and end. The gap before a class's first test is the class's set-up.
  - `--times` prints the twenty slowest tests and classes of each suite after a run. `--times --log <folder>` with
    logs already there reads them and runs nothing. For node, each test file counts as a test.
  - The screen shows no times. The failure blocks, the skips and the outcome are read the same from stamped or
    unstamped output.
- Checked:
  - [test_moved_code.py](../tools/repo/tests/test_moved_code.py) runs on made-up files:
    - Python: a method moved into another class with `self.` to `self.c.` is the same, though its docstring was
      rewrapped and a comment and a line break were added. A changed method differs and shows in the diff.
    - Python: names are qualified, renamed and missing, and a name found in two classes is refused.
    - JavaScript: regular expressions, template literals and strings that hold braces are read right. A re-indented
      function with a rewrapped comment is the same; a changed one differs.
    - The command line, against a Git tree of the old file: exit status 0, 1 and 2.
  - The tool on real history: `moved_code.py ee5ae99~1 tools/editor/compiler.py tools/editor/spawn_edits.py --subst
    self.=self.c.` pairs the nine spawn methods with their new class. Three are the same. Six differ, and the diff
    shows each difference: the round's own changes (`self.spawn_actors` to `self.actors`, calls within the family).
    `compiler.py` and `app.js` compared with themselves at HEAD are all the same: 182 functions and 812.
  - [test_run_tests.py](../tools/repo/tests/test_run_tests.py):
    - A made-up log parses the same with and without its times.
    - The slowest tests and classes come out right, with a class's set-up, a test with a docstring and a test that
      printed before its verdict.
    - Node's files are timed.
    - A real subprocess that pauses 0.4 s inside a line gives that line two times 0.4 s apart.
    - `--times --log` reads a folder without running.
  - `run_tests.py editor --times`: 359 tests, all 359 timed (10 s on a computer running other agents' work, so the
    times are noisy). The slowest five: `test_patchtool_record.ShipRecord.test_set_ship_config_on_copies_of_the_installs_files`
    1.20 s, `test_compiler.ForeignTests.test_the_installs_library_gives_a_piece_and_says_what_it_lacks` 0.84 s,
    `test_prefab_stage.StageTests.test_real_blank_map_compiles_building_only_and_light_only_and_checks_actual_bounds`
    0.80 s, `test_patchtool_record.ShipRecord.test_the_records_on_real_lines` 0.47 s,
    `test_spawn_edit_fixtures.SpawnEditFixtures.test_each_case_gives_what_was_recorded` 0.30 s. The slowest class is
    `test_build.Builds`: 4.8 s for 66 tests, 0.6 s of it set-up.
- Known gaps: the JavaScript reader is a tokenizer, not a parser. A `/` after a `}` is read as the start of a regular
  expression, and an arrow function's expression body ends at a line break that no operator carries on. Neither
  occurs in the page's top-level functions today.

### The page's names check: an undefined name or an unused import in the page's modules, found without running them

Editor refactor, stage 0 (item 0.4, decision D9). A function moved from one page module to another without its import
throws only when its line runs, and no browser check runs every line. This check finds such a name without running
any.

- [web_names.py](../tools/viewer/tests/web_names.py) runs ESLint over `tools/viewer/web/*.js` (not `vendor/`) as
  ES modules in the browser, with two rules only: `no-undef`, and an unused-import rule (an import binding nothing in
  its module reads; `export { name }` counts as a use). It prints each finding as `file:line: name` and exits 1 if
  there is any. It exits 2 if node, npm or npx is missing, or if ESLint can't be installed or run. Files given on the
  command line are checked instead of the page's modules.
- ESLint 10.14.0 and the `globals` package 17.14.0 are pinned in the script. npm installs them into a scratch folder
  (`.scratch/eslint`, ignored by Git, made on the first run; `--scratch` names another), and npx runs ESLint from
  there. The repository holds no `node_modules`.
- [web_names.config.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/web_names.config.mjs) holds the settings. The known globals are the
  browser's, less the window properties whose names read as a variable of the page's own: the
  confusing-browser-globals list (`name`, `status`, `open`, `parent`, `top`, ...) and `viewport`. app.js declares
  `open`, `moveTo` and `viewport` itself. A function moved out of app.js without its import would read the window's
  instead and not throw, so a bare use of one is reported. `location` and `history`, which app.js uses as the
  window's on purpose, are added back with their reasons. Inline ESLint comments in the page are not honoured: the
  exceptions live in the config, each with its reason.
- [requirements-dev.txt](../tools/requirements-dev.txt)'s notes give the versions and how to run it. `run_tests.py`
  does not run it.

### F-143: what a fix for the cover block that outlives its made wall has to get round

[F-143](../research/findings-register.md) (EXP-88: a cover block grouped with a made wall keeps its cover when
the wall goes) gains what the game's decompiled script says. An invincible block could succumb to the columns' clear
damage, but soldiers' projectiles, dying units, pushing pawns, the kinetic strike and destroyed props send the same
damage class, so the block could then go under ordinary fire while its wall stands. A fracturing wall cannot name the
block in `AffectedChildren` (only props carry it). The entry names a way round both (a collision-less hidden helper
prop listed in the wall's columns that names the block), not tried. No code changed.

Checked: the repo suite.

### The Build's state, record and relight command apart; the relight's main in stages

Review finding 51, its first step: the two long functions split along the seams they had, their bodies moved as
they were.

- [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py): a `BuildState` holds what the edit has taken out so far, and
  its `gone()` is the one answer the clear, the landings, the pieces' flags and the broken pieces read, in place of
  four sets built by hand with different members. The manifest's nativeCopies section (`manifest_parts`) and the
  relight's command line (`relight_command`, with the removed-casters and light-edits files it names) are plain
  functions of it, out of `build`.
- One change of behaviour comes with the one `gone()`: a project's landing moved in place now leaves alone a piece
  the edit's light deletes or its clear took out, as the clear, the flags and the broken pieces already did (before,
  it moved such a piece, which no longer stands in the level). No Build of the ten compared below has one.
- [relight.py](../tools/bake/relight.py): `main` reads its arguments and calls the stages in turn:
  `edit_arguments` (the edit the command line gives), `edit_scenes` (the scenes before and after),
  `edit_receivers` (where the edit reaches, and the receivers it adds), `select_components` (what goes to the
  relight), `kept_pieces` (the last build's pieces kept), `run_pieces` (the workers, the results in the map's
  order, the shadow maps) and `write_record` (the lighting written and the record). Each takes what it reads and
  returns what the next ones need. The relight's piece cache is keyed on relight.py, so a project's kept pieces are
  relit once more after this change.

Checked: quick and baked Build outputs of ten real project inputs (scratch builds, the relight's run recorded, not
run) are byte for byte those of the code before, their manifests and relight commands too; two real baked Builds of
URB_Bar projects (one copy; two copies, a hidden piece and light edits), each run twice so that the second takes its
pieces from the first, give the same variant map, texture cache, manifest and relight record (timings aside) as the
code before; the bake tests of the relight, faster bake, shadow maps, native copies, lights, spawns, made walls,
transplant, light factory, shadows and bounce, lightmap encoding, clear, building edits, effects and cover blocks.

Left: `build` keeps its clone loop, made walls, buildings and floor lists in line (the plan's further seams), and
its thirty parameters.

### The server's and the compiler's own notes say what the code does; a queue's stop told only once saved

Review finding 64, the docstrings and comments of the server and the editor's Python, and the build queue bug one of
them hid.

- **The build queue's stop** ([buildqueue.py](../tools/viewer/buildqueue.py)): its comment said the queue's build
  is told to stop "once the change is saved", but it was told before the save, so a stop that couldn't be saved left
  the queue put back as running while its build had been stopped. Now `_stopping` only notes the attempt, and the
  request (or Cancel in the build window) tells the builds runner after the save; one that can't be saved leaves the
  queue and its build running, as the queue then says. When the server closes, the build is stopped even if the
  queue can't be saved.

  longer says the move is untested in the game; a record the compiler can't build is left out and named while an

  and come from other maps too (it said they waited for their game check).
- **[projects.py](../tools/viewer/projects.py)**: schema versions 1 to 4 open and a save writes 4 (it said another
  version is refused and there is no migration).
- **[installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py)**: it names the two traces of the lab's deploy tools it knows (it
  said it knows nothing of the lab).
- **[viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py)**: the module says what it is (not "Local original-map viewer"); the
  export route's comment is above the export route, and the prefab test route has its own; a port in use says to

- Five modules' headers name their plans in `private/plans/done/` where they are now (gamedata, scene_metadata,

### One package writer, one chunk reader and one bounded property walk

Review finding 52, its first step. The package tools wrote, read and walked the same things several ways, and the
copies checked different things.

- **One writer.** [seed_tiles.py](../tools/upk/seed_tiles.py) `seed_package`,
  [world_links.py](../tools/upk/world_links.py) `write_package` and [bake_actor.py](../tools/upk/bake_actor.py)
  `rewrite` now build edit lists for [package_edit.py](../tools/upk/package_edit.py) `write_edited`, in place of
  their own block writers. They take a container or an edit in any chunk (later chunks move along, the chunk table
  follows), an uncompressed map such as DLC2_3_Furies, and blocks of any size; seed_tiles' second `lzo_literals`
  (which refused blocks under 19 bytes) and its `chunk_table_offset` are gone. On URB_Bar the seeded, link-moved and
  actor-baked packages are byte for byte those the old writers made.
- **One chunk reader.** [decomp.py](../tools/upk/decomp.py) `read_chunk` checks a chunk header's tag, block size,
  block table sums and length; the map decode, [upkinfo.py](../tools/upk/upkinfo.py) `load`'s packages compressed
  whole and package_edit's writers read through it (package_edit's `read_chunk` is that one). The map decode also
  refuses a chunk whose size is not the chunk table's. [audit_cross_map.py](../tools/upk/audit_cross_map.py)'s
  copy of the whole-file decode now calls `upkinfo.load`.
- **One bounded property walk.** [props.py](../tools/upk/props.py) `tags` (and `read_tags`) walks tagged
  properties with the viewer reader's checks: a name or kind outside the table, a negative size, a value past the
  end, and a list without its None are refused, never read through. It takes the names the bytes were written with,
  so a Build's grown bytes walk with the grower's (review finding 37). The Build's `Walker`
  ([native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py)), the Kismet reader `kismet_links.P.props` (every Build that
  makes an intro copy) and bake_actor walk with it.
- **One static tile store reader.** world_links `static_tiles` reads the static flags with `parse_store`'s checks
  (every chunk of the grid saved, as before). native_copy reads them through it once for each open package
  (`static_flags`, in place of a parse for each seeded copy), and seed_tiles' unchecked `parse_static_store` is gone.

Tests: [test_package_edit.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_package_edit.py) (the actor baker in blocks of 10 bytes;
on URB_Bar, seeds land on the empty tiles and nowhere else, an uncompressed bar seeds as the compressed one, a link
move changes only the container), [test_bad_input.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_bad_input.py) (damaged chunk headers
refused, a chunk of another size than its table refused) and [test_props.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_props.py)
(the walk, what it refuses, the Kismet reader on it).

Checked: the upk suite; the bake tests of the native copies, save tiles, shell, intro copy, lights, cover blocks,
flags, effects, buildings, fractured walls, spawns, streams, transplant and clear; quick and baked Build outputs of
ten real project inputs (scratch builds, relight stubbed) byte for byte those of the code before; on installed maps,

Left for a later step: the other walkers of tagged properties (props.read_props, typed_props, map_inventory,

  landing zone, light and piece rows, which wrote the same twenty lines each (two more went with finding 63).

  used by poserule.js, floors.js, cover.js, spawns.js, walls.js, ground.js and app.js; prefabs.js's and floors.js's own
  unused copies are gone. In app.js the bare 96s and 64s that mean a tile or a level (grid steps, snaps, the builder's
  floor, the tile-grid defaults, the ground grid's shader) and the four quarter turns are written with them; numbers
  that only happen to be 96 or 64 (sweep heights, canvas sizes, probe heights, recursion limits) and the words shown
  to users stay as they were.
- **Written once now:** the picture-key hash (`api.js` `hex16`, for library.js's effect pictures and look_picker.js's
  samples, giving the same keys as before, so kept pictures are found); `linear` and `toView` (lighting.js, imported
  by lights_view.js); the clock (build_queue.js's, for app.js's build window and wave player and precache.js).
- **[storage.js](../tools/viewer/web/storage.js)**: every setting the page keeps is `workshop.<name>`. The keys of
  the older styles (`viewer.stats`, `viewer.pivot`, `viewer.flyKeys`, the camera speeds, `viewer.fold.*`,
  `gameMapsGroup`, `xcom-map-workshop.manager.projectFiles`) are read once and moved to their new names. app.js,
  manager.js and gamemaps.js read and write through it.
- **The effects preview's allocations** ([effects_preview.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_preview.js),
  [effects_sim.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_sim.js)):
  - a replay binds each emitter's next run to the geometry, material and mesh it has, where it used to release and
    remake them all;
  - a sprite takes the shared quad's index and corners off before it is disposed, so they stay for the others;
  - a mesh emitter's instanced meshes are disposed with it;
  - the simulation uses one `own` function per emitter, not one per particle per step.

Checked: two new node tests, [api_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/api_test.mjs) (answers, refusals and their words,
JSON sent only with a body, the picture key unchanged) and [storage_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/storage_test.mjs)
(old keys moved once, blocked storage); the node suite; the import check; the full browser smoke on URB_Bar with
`--projects`, and the named checks for the library, effects, prefabs, the builder and the prefab test.

### Export 37: what nothing read is no longer written, and each mission says its kind

Review findings 63 (written into every export and read by nothing; the piece study) and 55 (the council mission
kind). One version bump, so every map is exported again once, on its first open
([export.py](../tools/viewer/export.py) `EXPORT_VERSION` 37).

**No longer written** (each searched for across the repository first: the page, the server, the compiler, the tests,
the browser checks and `take_shots.py`):
- the map's own `content` (every level actor and Kismet record). A streamed or previewed layer still reads its own,
  for the stream's count of rebuild volumes and a preview's `inheritedPatches`;
- `effectsMetadata`;
- a material's `render.compiledTextures` (the compiled shader's textures are still read for the colour, and the
  diagnostic still names them);
- `scenes.json` (previews open by address, `?scene=preview-<n>.json`).

**No longer worked out:** a streamed package's buildings, van buildings, playable bounds, tile grid and tactical data,
which `stream_layers` dropped (it keeps the stream's pieces, lights, effects and level records).

**The piece study is gone:** the `sample` scope and its three URB_Bar actor names; `viewer.py export --scope` takes
`map` only ([viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py)). An earlier export's study is still read by the cache's pruning,
but [catalogue.py](../tools/viewer/catalogue.py) no longer opens one, not even as an exact generation.
`Exporter.effects` takes no scope.

**Each mission says its kind** (`missions[].kind`, `missions.kind_key`: `Special/Bomb` for a council bomb...).
[missions.py](../tools/viewer/missions.py) `kind_of_export` and the page's
[missions.js](../tools/viewer/web/missions.js) `kindKey` read it, and fall back to the label for an older export,
so rewording a council label no longer turns its missions into plain special ones.

**[audit_clear.py](../tools/upk/audit_clear.py)**, the clear survey, which read `content` from the export, reads
the level's records from the package instead (`level_content`; on URB_Bar the same 1,557 records the export had).

Measured (exported into a scratch cache before and after; compact `scene.json`):

| Map | Export 36 | Export 37 | Less |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| URB_Bar | 3,779,847 bytes | 3,507,314 bytes | 272,533 (7.2%) |
| TempleShip, the largest in the cache | 8,712,902 bytes | 8,031,251 bytes | 681,651 (7.8%) |

Both scenes are otherwise the same, key for key, once the dropped fields, the new `kind`, the version and the
package's path are set aside. The export took as long (22 and 17 seconds).

Checked:
- the viewer tests that read the export (`test_streams`, `test_material_rules`, `test_effects_metadata`,
  `test_damaged_inputs`, `test_catalogue`, `test_prune`, `test_composition`, `test_precache`, `test_play`), now
  checking the compiled shader's colour by the material's texture and diagnostic, a layer's guarded level records, each
  mission's kind and the refused piece study;
- `missions_test.mjs`;
- the export 37 Bar on a test server: `browser_smoke.py --only zoom,spawns,effects` passed with no errors.

Known gap: `browser_smoke.py`'s full run still fetches `scenes.json` to list a map's previews (the browser checks'
owner changes that). The contracts' and the viewer README's mentions are updated.

### The Build's code in modules named for what it does, not in audits, fixtures and experiments

Review finding 53. The release shipped modules named and documented as audits, fixtures and experiments because the
Build and the editor imported parts of them. Each part moved to a module named for what it does; the surveys and lab
tools import it from there, and nothing about what the code does changed.

- [lighting_records.py](../tools/upk/lighting_records.py): the lighting records every relight and copier reads (a
  mesh component's LOD records, a texture's mips, the properties an object saves, a file's SHA-256, and the viewer
  reader's names), out of [audit_lighting.py](../tools/upk/audit_lighting.py), which keeps its census and imports
  them. The product's importers in [tools/bake](../tools/bake) and [lights.py](../tools/viewer/lights.py),
  and the tests of the product, import the new name.
- [floor_listing.py](../tools/upk/floor_listing.py): which floors list a piece (`touched`, `listing`, `MARGIN`), out
  of [audit_buildings.py](../tools/upk/audit_buildings.py); [buildings.py](../tools/bake/buildings.py) lists by
  it.
- [kismet_links.py](../tools/upk/kismet_links.py), the Kismet reader, now holds `intro_anchors` (where the dropship
  intro puts its flight for each map), out of [audit_clear.py](../tools/upk/audit_clear.py);
  [intro_copy.py](../tools/bake/intro_copy.py) reads it there.
- [lightmap_writer.py](../tools/bake/lightmap_writer.py): the writer every baked Build's relight writes through
  (`Fixture`, its redirect, setscale, image and gray operations, the cache name's rules). The stage C0-C2 experiment's
  noop, scale and paint and its command line stay in [lighting_fixture.py](../tools/bake/lighting_fixture.py), as a
  subclass, and re-export the writer's names. The relight, the copier and the Build
  ([build.py](../tools/editor/build.py): its named copy and its manifest's tool list) use the new module.
- [lightmap_textures.py](../tools/bake/lightmap_textures.py): the readers of an original bake's top mip, out of the
  EXP-16 statistics tool [lightmap_stats.py](../tools/bake/lightmap_stats.py), and the texture clone, out of the
  gate C6 tool [grow_fixture.py](../tools/bake/grow_fixture.py). The kept mips no longer go into the package
  object's `__dict__`: a weak table of the module's holds them for each package while it is open.
- [mapsini.py](../tools/viewer/mapsini.py): the game's config lines (`lines_of`, `is_record`, `field`, `set_field`,
  `unquoted`, `add_stream`, `slot_record`, `plan_lz`, `check_change`, `write_checked` and the rest), out of the lab's
  fixture installer [deploy_fixture.py](../tools/bake/deploy_fixture.py), which imports them for the lab.
  [installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py), [gamemaps.py](../tools/viewer/gamemaps.py) and
  [manager.py](../tools/viewer/manager.py) import them there (their import lines alone changed), and
  [test_install_recovery.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_install_recovery.py) stands in for the writer there.
- The helpers used across modules are public: `light_factory.class_of`, `tagged_property` and `preamble`;
  `cover_blocks.recipe_imports` and `export_template`.
- The relight's piece cache is keyed on `lightmap_textures.py` and `lighting_records.py` in place of the old two, so
  a project's kept pieces are relit once more after this change.

The release: nothing it ships imports `tools/lab` any more, and
[test_release.py](../tools/release/tests/test_release.py) now checks that, and that the new modules ship.
`make_release.FOLDERS` still lists `lab` for the embedded Python's path; that entry can go.

Checked: the upk and release suites; the bake tests of the fixtures, relight, faster bake, intro copy, buildings,
cover blocks, lights, map picture, the lab installer, inline lighting, shadow maps, walls and measurers; the viewer's
install, manager, game maps, deploy, lights, play, output names and pack tests.

### The compiler's spawn point edits in a module of their own

Review finding 23, as far as its first step: one bounded edit family moved out of the `Compiler` class.

- **[spawn_edits.py](../tools/editor/spawn_edits.py)** is new: `SpawnEdits` holds the spawn family's methods, moved
  from [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) with their names and bodies unchanged but for where they read the
  compiler (a script compared the two, whitespace aside): `spawn_of`, `spawn_values`, `spawn_box`, `spawn_override`,
  `spawn_names`, `spawn_delete`, `free_pod_index`, `volume_add` and `spawn_add`. It owns the family's state, which was
  the compiler's: the spec's `spawns` operations (`ops`), the next free pod index and the base map's spawn points by
  actor (`index`, filled where `index_export` filled them).
- **The compiler** makes one for each `Compiler` and hands it each spawn record from `overrides` and `added`; `spec`,
  `projected_spawns` and the report read its operations and points. Diagnostics still go through the compiler's
  `error`, `warn` and `note`, so a refused record is left out and the build goes on as before. The module imports the
  compiler's tables (`SPAWN_*`, `FAMILIES`, `EPS_LOCATION`, `short`, `tidy`), so the compiler imports it when a
  `Compiler` is made.
- **State the stages of `run()` set is now made in `__init__`**, with a comment giving the order: the map's package,
  the clear and what it keeps outside, the drop-in rule, the larger grid, the zones and the map's own landings. The
  `getattr` reads with defaults that stood in for it (`stage_grid` eight times, `cleared`, `zones`, `own_count`,
  `own_landings_found`, `spawn_rules`, `keep_outside`) read the attributes directly, with the same defaults.

Checked:

- the editor suite;
- `compiler.py` run as a script on a recorded case gives the same lane.

lights and area lights, made walls, slabs and ground, floors and flags, buildings, landing zones and missions,

`_map_buildings`, `_building_records`, `_missions_kept`).

### A wall's gap never closes up to nothing, and a drag the wall tool can't make isn't applied

Review finding 32, the page's item.

`movedOpening`'s "a gap never takes the whole wall" fallback put a side `least` in from the wall's end. On a one-tile
wall moved by whole tiles, that is the full length, so dragging a side gave `{x0: 96, x1: 96}` or `{x0: 0, x1: 0}`.
`toolWall` refuses those numbers, yet the drag still applied them and asked the server for a mesh.

- [walls.js](../tools/viewer/web/walls.js): the fallback keeps the gap at least `OPENING.width` wide. Where the step
  in would shrink the gap rather than move its side outwards, the side stays where it was. A gap that already reached
  both ends is cut back to the narrowest gap.
- [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js): a wall handle's drag applies only numbers the wall tool makes. A step that
  `toolWall` refuses leaves the drag at its last good state.
- Checked:
  - [walls_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/walls_test.mjs) drags a one-tile wall's gap sides by whole tiles. The gap
    stays as it was and stays a wall the tool makes. A whole-wall gap cuts back to 16 wide, and a two-tile wall still
    stops a tile in. The first case gave `{x0: 0, x1: 0}` before this change.
  - The browser check `walls` passes (on `?map=URB_PoliceStation`, the map it is written for), and so does the node
    suite.
- Not in this change: the slab and compiler items of the finding (a floor whose holes cover it all, overlapping holes),
  which belong to the Build's side.

### Old build work is pruned after a failed build too, and as the server starts, with the variants no project ships as

Review finding 49 (the Build's part), with finding 62's prune test.

- **After every build.** [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py) pruned old work folders only after a build that
  packaged, so a failed build kept its 60 to 150 MB and so did every older one of its variant. The prune now runs in
  the build's `finally`, built or failed, leaving that build's own work folder and kept pieces as they are; a prune
  that fails is a line in the log, never the build's outcome.
- **One prune, shared.** [builds.py](../tools/viewer/builds.py) `prune_work` holds the rule for both: every
  variant keeps its 3 newest work folders whole (`KEEP_WORK`; a bug report reads the newest) and older ones keep their
  logs and their files up to 1 MB; the rest of `.work` (patchtool's, the publish journals, the snapshots the build
  queue prunes) is left.
- **As the server starts.** `BuildRunner.prune` runs beside `recover`, in a thread of its own (the first prune of a
  folder that never had one may free gigabytes), and knows the variants the projects ship as (`owned_variants`, read
  from the projects folder; an unreadable folder or file means none is taken for unowned). A variant no project ships
  as keeps no work folder whole once its last build is 14 days old (`ORPHAN_DAYS`).
- **Kept pieces get an age limit.** A variant's kept relit pieces (`.work/pieces/<Variant>`, one build's worth) are
  deleted once neither they nor the variant's work folders have changed for 30 days (`PIECE_DAYS`), or 14 days for a
  variant no project ships as; the next build of it relights everything once.
- Checked: [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py) prunes after a failed build, keeps that build's own
  kept pieces however old and leaves a variant no project ships as; [test_builds.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_builds.py)
  starts a server on a builds folder with owned, unowned and recently built variants, old and recent kept pieces and
  patchtool's work, then prunes again and finds nothing; another test spares a running build's folder and checks
  `owned_variants`. Known gap: the game folder's backups and history (the rest of finding 49, installs.py) are not
  this change's.

### The launcher asks before it stops an editor that is building, and knows when the editor it started is up

Review finding 47. [xcom_editor.cmd](../xcom_editor.cmd) with no argument (a double-click) restarts the editor,
and that was a `taskkill /F`: a running bake or a queue of builds died without a question.

- **Before it stops a running editor** (restart, stop), it asks the editor whether it is building:
  [launch_check.py](../tools/viewer/launch_check.py) `busy` reads `GET /manager.json` (each project's `building`:
  a build from the build window or the queue's) and `GET /manager/queue.json` (a queue running, between its builds
  too). When something is building, or the editor does not answer, it says what and asks "Stop the editor anyway?
  [y/N]". It stops the editor only on a yes. Declined, a restart opens the running editor in the browser instead.
- **After the stop**, the launcher checks the editor actually stopped. It failed if `taskkill` failed, and it fails
  when the port is still held after ten seconds, instead of saying "Stopped" and starting a server that can't bind.
- **After a start** it waits until the editor answers on its port (`launch_check.py wait`, up to 5 minutes, saying
  every 15 s that it waits). It no longer looked for a listening port for 15 s, which said "did not start" of a main
  server still preparing its cache. A server whose process ended (a port in use, a bad argument) is said so at once:
  the server and the helper are both children of the launcher's cmd.
- **A `VIEWER_CACHE` ending in `\`** gets it doubled, where it escaped the closing quote.
- **`VIEWER_ARGS`** adds arguments to `serve` for tests: scratch `--projects`, `--builds`, `--squad`, `--dry-play`,
  `--install`.

Checked:
- [test_launch_check.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_launch_check.py) runs `busy` against stand-in servers: idle,
  building, a queue between builds, no queue, an error, and nothing listening. It runs `wait` against a server that
  listens late, against nothing, and against a server whose process ended.
- By hand on port 8792 with scratch folders and a `VIEWER_CACHE` ending in `\`:
  - `start`, `status`, `restart` and `stop` of an idle editor;
  - a stand-in "viewer.py serve" that is building, with no answer, "n" (to stop and to restart) and "y";
  - a server that refuses its arguments, which was reported in about a second.

Not checked: the port still being held after a stop, which can't be made to happen on purpose.

### One unreadable record no longer ends a map's export, and the server's smaller reads say why and are not kept failed

Review findings 50 (the items for the server, the exporter and the package readers) and 31 (area lights at export,
the compiler's message, the script defaults).

- **Damaged packages**: [lzo1x](../tools/upk/lzo1x.py) raises `ValueError` for a block cut short (it raised
  `IndexError`, which no guard expected) and for one that gives another length than its table says.
  [export.py](../tools/viewer/export.py)'s per-piece guards (components, textures, particle meshes, piece flags,
  streamed packages) catch one set of errors (`UNREADABLE`), and the readers that were outside any guard (buildings,
  lights and their metadata, area lights, landings, effect carriers, script defaults, effects and their drawings,
  cursor volumes, the level's records) go through `Exporter.guarded`: a failure is a diagnostic and an empty answer,
  not the end of the whole export. A damaged or modded install would end it; valid game files never did.
- **`Package.cls`** names an import's own class ([package.py](../tools/viewer/package.py)); a negative index read
  an unrelated export's class through the list's wrap. 0 is 'None', and a reference outside both tables a
  `FormatError`.
- **`upkinfo.load`** ([upkinfo.py](../tools/upk/upkinfo.py)) takes `raw` as an argument instead of reading
  `--raw` from whatever program's command line it runs in, puts its folder on `sys.path` once when it loads instead of
  at every compressed package (the server's path grew as it ran), and checks a whole-compressed package's blocks and
  total.
- **`viewer.py export`** defaults to `--scope map` ([viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py)): the old default, the
  piece study, worked on URB_Bar only and died with a bare `KeyError` on any other map.
- **A level's actor list** has one reader ([scene_metadata.level_list](../tools/viewer/scene_metadata.py), which
  [effects_metadata](../tools/viewer/effects_metadata.py)'s now calls) and one answer when it can't be read: every
  actor counts as listed. Before, the effects carried by pieces took "none listed" while the effects' own records took
  "all listed", so one scene.json disagreed with itself; the spawn points' records still say `listed: null` (not read).
- **The build queue's file of another version** ([buildqueue.py](../tools/viewer/buildqueue.py) `_load`) is told by
  its `schemaVersion`, not by the words of the error: a newer editor's queue is left for it, and an older one is now
  restored from the last good copy.
- **scene.json** is written compact (the largest was 15.6 MB indented against 8.3 MB), with the previews and
  `scenes.json`; the map's SHA-256 is worked out once per export (the folder's name and the scene's source both take
  it). The export's version is unchanged.
- **Costs on each use**: the setup dialog's doctor starts PowerShell once per pwsh file, not at every opening
  ([settings.py](../tools/viewer/settings.py); a failed start is not kept), and each pack zip in Map packs is read
  once per size and time ([packs.py](../tools/viewer/packs.py)), not at every `packs.json`.

### Each project file is read once until it changes; a save that can't be written says why

Review finding 20, and the save half of finding 46.

- **Reads** (finding 20). The project manager's listing read each project four times, the build status read the
  project on every poll (every 2 s), and the queue view and the map names' check read projects again.
  - [projects.py](../tools/viewer/projects.py) keeps what each file in the folder said, by its modified time,
    size and file id: its id, rank, summary, name, revision and output names. A file is read again only when that
    stamp changes, and a file renamed or changed outside the editor is seen at the next listing.
  - `listing()` gives the [project manager](../tools/viewer/manager.py) each project read once, its summary made
    from the very document it gives.
  - `cached()` answers the build status ([builds.py](../tools/viewer/builds.py), two lines) and the queue view's
    name and estimate ([buildqueue.py](../tools/viewer/buildqueue.py)).
  - `claimed()` gives [outputnames.Claims](../tools/viewer/outputnames.py) every project's output names.
  - Prefabs' summaries, which validate and measure the whole prefab, are kept the same way.
- Measured on ten projects, with the store before this change and after:
  - a project manager refresh read project files 40 times, now 10 (20 the first time a server lists them);
  - five build status polls read 10 times, now none.
- **Save errors** (finding 46). A save that can't be written (a full disk, a file open in another program, a
  read-only folder) is a ProjectError that says which, so the page shows "Not saved:" with the reason. Before, the
  connection dropped.
  - The temporary file goes, and the revision before stays the project.
  - A draft write says the same. A renamed project whose old file can't be removed is saved, and the page says the
    old file is listed as a copy until it is deleted.
- Checked: [test_projects.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_projects.py) counts the reads:
  - a listing, a second listing, the polled lookups, the manager's listing and a load;
  - a file renamed and one changed outside the editor;
  - a full disk, a refused copy of the revision before and a refused draft write.

### A made piece's change of look is one undo step of its own, and keeps the piece's flags and blasts

Review finding 30. `setMadeLook` deleted the old pieces, waited for the new mesh from the server with nothing holding
input, and then joined "the last two or three" undo steps by count. Anything undoable done during that wait was
joined to the look change, and the delete was left as a step of its own. A Ctrl+Z in the wait undid the delete, so the
old and new pieces both stood. If the mesh failed, the delete stayed alone and the rejection went unhandled.

- `setMadeLook` ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js)) has the new pieces made first, with nothing changed. After
  that one wait it deletes the old pieces, places the new ones and mends their group in one go, with no wait
  between, joined as one step.

  - So does a piece that was moved or deleted during the wait: its hint asks for the look again.
- `pasteSnapshot` takes `whole` (all or nothing) and `first` (run just before the paste is recorded, and able to
  call it off) for this.
- A look change now keeps the piece's flags, tint and blasts. Only its look changes. Before, it dropped them.
- Checked: the new browser check `look-undo` ([browser_editing.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_editing.py),
  through `browser_smoke.py --only look-undo`) runs on the Bar with the server's made meshes held back a second and a
  half. It gives a made wall (with flags and a blast) the look of one of the map's own walls, and deletes another piece

### The editor's Build captures the project and its map picture before it starts, as the build queue does

Review finding 12.

- **What a build reads is captured first.** The editor's Build (and Play in game's) launched build.py on the
  project's own file, so a save, a rename or a new map picture while it ran could reach the build half way, and the
  job, the manifest and a bug report could name different bytes. [builds.py](../tools/viewer/builds.py) `capture`
  now reads the saved project whole under the store's lock into a snapshot of its own,
  `<builds>/.work/queue-attempts/<attempt>/project.json`, with the map picture the project names copied beside it
  (`project.picture.png`, only when the kept file's SHA-256 is the one named), and build.py builds the snapshot
  (`--saved-file` names the project's own file, `--projects` its folder). A capture that can't be written is an error
  before anything is launched, and its folder is removed.
- **The build queue captures the same way.** [buildqueue.py](../tools/viewer/buildqueue.py) calls the same
  `capture`, so its snapshots carry the picture too; the row's attempt and the job name the picture's SHA-256 beside
  the project's (`digest`, `picture`), and the bug report's summary carries both.
- **The Build reads the picture captured.** [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py) reads the project's bytes once
  (the manifest's `project.sha256`), and a build of a snapshot takes only the picture beside it: one chosen since,
  kept with the project, is not that build's (with none beside it, the build says the picture is missing).
- The snapshots of both are pruned by the build queue's existing rule (`ATTEMPT_DAYS`, 14 days, those no row names).
- Checked: [test_builds.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_builds.py) saves under another name and chooses two new
  pictures after the capture, and the build, the package and the bug report keep the captured bytes; a retry after
  Cancel captures again. [test_buildqueue.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_buildqueue.py) does the same for a queued
  build; [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py) builds a snapshot with a newer picture in the store.

Review findings 26 and 25.

**Finding 26.** Three removal paths reported a record they could not take out, then deleted its map's files anyway.

### Exports, library scans and the cache job are contained as builds are, and the install waits for them

Review finding 48.

- **Contained**: a map export ([exports.py](../tools/viewer/exports.py)), a library scan
  ([library.py](../tools/viewer/library.py)) and "Cache everything"'s pieces process
  ([precache.py](../tools/viewer/precache.py)) start through `procs.launch`, as builds do: each is a process tree in
  a job object of its own, so Cancel ends the whole tree by its job (never `taskkill` of a bare process id that may
  have been reused), the cache job's workers end with it, and a server that dies takes them with it instead of leaving
  them writing into the cache with no owner. When a process ends, what it left running is ended before its result is
  taken. An export, a scan or the cache job that can't start says so (500 with the reason) instead of failing the
  request.
- **The pieces folders are locked across processes** (`library.donor_lock`: the operating system's lock on
  `<cache>/library/locks/<map>.lock`, `publication.FileLock`). The server's piece requests and the cache job's workers
  write a donor's pieces, effects and drawings under it, and a piece is read again once the lock is held, so the two
  never export the same piece into the same files. Reading a kept piece takes no lock.
- **Temporary files have names of their own** (`library.part_of`): piece, effects and drawing records, the library's
  index (two scans at once no longer write the same `index.json.part`) and thumbnails.
- **Choosing another game install** is refused (409, saying what runs) while a map export, a library scan or the cache
  job runs, as it already was while the build queue runs (`viewer.install_busy`); before, the old runner's job went on
  into the old catalogue beside a new runner that allowed a second. When the server can't load the new install, the
  setting is put back as it was ([gamesetup.py](../tools/viewer/gamesetup.py)), so the settings file and the server
  agree, and the page is told why.
- Checked: [test_contained_jobs.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_contained_jobs.py) (new) cancels an export that
  started a child of its own and sees both processes end, an export that can't start, a donor's lock held by another
  process (409, another donor free, free again once it ends), unique temporary names, the install refused for each of
  the three jobs, and a failed switch putting the setting back. [test_precache.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_precache.py)
  checks the stopped cache job is not killed. The viewer suite passes.
- Not done: `builds.stop_process` stays for the code that still uses it (builds.py, which this change does not own);
  nothing here uses it any more.

### The Build's drop-and-retry of untried pieces agrees with its compile step

Review finding 40. When the transplant or the copy stage fails with copies the Build has not made before in the edit
(the compiler's `untried`), [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py) `drop_untried` takes them out and runs the stages
again. Three things in it disagreed with the rest of the Build:

- **One "has work" test.** Its "nothing left" test left out mission objects' moves and hides and the spawn rule, which
  the compile step counts, so dropped copies beside a mission object's move failed with "nothing of the project can
  be built". Both now ask `Build.has_work` (which also counts the missions list and the map picture, finding 39).
- **What depends on a dropped piece goes with it.** The glow lights a dropped copy would copy, or a dropped move would
  move, are taken out of the edit's area-light operations, and a break group a dropped copy was in that can't break
  together without it (the compiler's rule: two breakable pieces, or one and a cover block, or a made wall with a prop
  or a block) has its number taken off what is left and its map pieces out of `breakOriginals`
  (`unlinked_groups`; the `leftout` stage lists them as `groupsUnlinked`). Before, the group stayed and named a copy
  that was not made.
- **A retry only for a failure about those pieces.** Only the untried copies the failure names (its message, or the
  last 40 lines of the failing tool's log, where a traceback ends: `untried_named`) are dropped, and only then are the
  stages run again; a failure that names none is the build's own and is said at once, without a second full bake. A
  second failure that names another untried copy drops it too, and the `leftout` stage lists every one dropped.
- Checked: [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py): a failure naming none is not run again; of two
  untried copies the named one goes first with its glow light and its group, the other with the second failure; a
  mission object's move left keeps the build going; the two existing drop-and-retry tests now fail the way `_run`
  does (a log that names the piece). The editor suite passes.

### A project whose only change is its missions or its picture builds; a part the compiler can't read is left out, not a refusal

Review finding 39.

- **Missions and picture are changes.** [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py)'s "the project changes nothing" test
  (now `Build.has_work`) counted no missions list and no map picture, so a project that only narrowed its missions, or
  only gave its map a picture (the LWR 3 map packs' use), was refused. Both count now; such a project builds the map
  unchanged with them, its lighting kept.
- **One bad part no longer refuses the whole project.** [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `leave_out`
  puts a row in the report's `leftOut` (the Build's window and manifest show it) and the rest builds:
  - an area-light binding it can't use, or a bindings value that is no list (the light follows the export's
    association);
  - a malformed group, or a groups value that is no list (it doesn't break together); a group's nesting is a note
    (`group-nesting`), since nothing of it reaches the game;
  - a building record it can't read or whose id an earlier one has, or a value that is no list
    (`building_records`: the groups and the floors a copy stands in read the same records);
  - a map size it can't build (`stage`: the map keeps its own; the Build's shell stage then reads nothing of it);
  - a spawn rule it doesn't know (the drop-ins as the install has them);
  - `cleared` or `clearKeepsOutside` that is not true or false (not cleared; the clear takes out what lies outside);
  - a landing zone it can't read or whose id an earlier one has (the rest are the variant's; a value that is no list,
    or whose zones are all left out, is as no list, so the base map's lines are copied);
  - a missions entry the Build can't write (`missions_kept`; a value that is no list, an empty list or one with no
    entry it can write is as no list: every record). The report's `missions` is the list the Build writes records
    for.
  Still refused, as nothing can be built from them: the schema, the source, a source that doesn't match, the output
  names, an export without the light data or the tile grid the edit needs.
- **A map picture that can't be written is a note**, where it failed the build after its whole bake. The picture is
  looked up once as the build starts (`Build.find_picture`); missing or unwritable, the map is built without one and
  the manifest's `pictureNote` says why.
- The rule is written in [editor-contracts.md](../research/editor-contracts.md) ("What refuses a build"), with the
  rows for nesting, landing zones, missions and the spawn rule changed to match.
- Checked: [test_compiler.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_compiler.py)'s tests of each part now check the part is
  left out and the report good (a bad zone among good ones, a bad missions entry among good ones, one bad building
  among good ones); [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py) builds a missions-only and a picture-only
  project, writes the compiler's missions list, reads no `stage` the compiler left out, and keeps a bake whose
  picture fails. The editor suite passes.

### The relight uses the workers it is allowed, keeps pieces only for the code they came from, and reads a 0 as 0

Review findings 41, 42 and two relight items of 44, all in [relight.py](../tools/bake/relight.py).

- **Workers (41).** The worker count was cut to the number of pieces before a large piece was cut into bands, and
  bands were made only with more than one worker: an edit that reached one large floor ran on one worker, unbanded,
  and two large floors ran their bands on two. `plan_jobs` now cuts the queue for the workers allowed, then gives it
  no more workers than it has jobs. Measured on URB_Bar's pool-table floor (61,628 texels, 5 bands) with the Build's
  settings: with the pool table taken out, the pieces' stage went from 24.1 s on one worker before the change to
  13.6 s on five after it; with the ceiling spot over it off, from 28.9 s on one worker to 10.6 s on five, and the
  relit images and the map came out byte for byte the same. Not done: preparing a large piece once and handing its
  bands their texels. Each worker that takes a
  band prepares the piece again, but that preparation measured 0.7 to 1.2 s against 4.2 to 6.0 s for one of its bands
  (the bands run side by side), so it would save about a second a large piece for a change to how jobs are handed out.
- **Kept pieces (42).** The piece cache's key hashed six files. It now hashes every module of the tools the relight
  loads (the decode of the original bake, the map's, meshes' and materials' readers among them), but the writer of the
  variant, and the release's version as well, so an upgrade never takes a stale piece as good.
- **A source size of 0 (44).** A light's `lightSourceRadius` or `lightSourceAngle` of 0 was read as the default (100
  units, 3 degrees), so the reach tests grew the edit boxes more than meant; the dominant light's quick shadow-map test
  (angle 0) included. `light_source_radius` and `light_source_angle` take the default only when there is no value.
- **A piece that covers no texel (44)** is left out of the relight ("covers no texel of its lightmap") whatever the
  scene; a direct-only relight of one raised `AttributeError`.
- Checked: [test_faster_bake.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_faster_bake.py) tests `plan_jobs` (one large floor gets
  its bands and a worker each; two get as many workers as allowed), that every module the relight loads is in the
  key's list and that the key changes with the release, and a 0 source size against the default in `shadow_meets`
  and `texel_reach`; [test_relight.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_relight.py) relights a piece with no texel and no
  scene. Each failed before its change.

### A project folder of the old layout never writes over a newer project

Review finding 5. The store moved a folder of the layout before 8 November 2026 (`<id>\project.json`) onto the file
of the same project with no comparison, so a revision-1 backup restored beside a revision-2 library replaced
revision 2.

- [projects.py](../tools/viewer/projects.py) `_migrate` now ranks the folder's document against the file that
  holds the project, as the listing ranks copies: the higher revision, then the later save, and the file there wins
  a tie. The other is kept beside it as `<name> (kept copy).json` (numbered when taken), which the listing shows as a
  copy of the project. The same bytes twice keep one.
- A previous revision or a draft whose name is taken is kept under a name of its own: a draft as another page's (so
  both are offered), a previous revision as `project.prev (2).json`.
- Each step is one rename, so a stop halfway leaves the folder to finish at the next listing.
- The listing's ranking and the migration's are one function (`_rank`).
- The [contract](../research/editor-contracts.md) and the [viewer README](../tools/viewer/README.md) say so.
- Checked: [test_projects.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_projects.py) covers both revision orders, equal revisions
  going by the later save, a tie, a second copy, the same bytes twice, drafts and previous revisions beside those
  there, and a stop between the two renames that the next listing finishes.

### A change of the game install's files is undone whole when it stops part-way, and its config files are never cut short

Review findings 2 and 50.

- **Every config write goes through a temporary file.**
  [deploy_fixture.write_checked](../tools/bake/deploy_fixture.py), which writes `DefaultMaps.ini`,
  `DefaultLZMutator.ini` and `DefaultRandomSpawns.ini` for every install path, wrote the game's file in place and
  only then read it back. It now writes a temporary file beside it, reads that back, and puts it in place with a
  replace. A crash or a forced stop mid-write leaves the game's file as it was, and so does a bad read-back.
- **Each change of the install keeps a journal.**
  [installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py) wraps each change in a `_Change`: a play's install, a map play's
  record, a campaign install, a play's clean-up, Remove from game, records switched on or off, and an earlier
  version's intro taken out. The journal (`<game>\XCOM Map Workshop\change.json`) is written before the change's
  first write and holds both ledgers' text as they were. Before each later write it records what that write is:
  - for a config file, its hash before and after, with its old bytes kept beside the journal;
  - for a package file, the file it copies in or takes out. A file it replaces or takes out is moved aside
    (`.<name>.change.tmp`) instead of deleted, and a copy goes in through a temporary file.

  A change that ends in an error is rolled back at once. One stopped by a crash or a forced stop is rolled back by
  the next look at the install (`ready`, which every operation and the page's status calls run, and
  `recover_change` at the start of each operation). Rolling back puts back the config bytes, the files and the
  ledgers, and the ledger's history records it (`interrupted`, `rolledBack`). So `DefaultMaps.ini` never again has a
  record the ledger doesn't know: the stop between the config write and the ledger write, which listed the variant
  as a game map and refused its next install, can't leave that state any more.
- **A config file changed by hand between the stop and the recovery is left as it is.** It is named in the
  history's `left`, and its text from before is kept in `backups\interrupted-<stamp>`.
- **"Is the game running?" no longer starts tasklist.** The question was asked about five times a play, on every
  status poll and every 3 s through a game session. [procs.running](../tools/viewer/procs.py) answers it from one
  snapshot of the process table, and both copies use it: `installs.game_running` and `deploy_fixture.game_running`.

Checked: [test_install_recovery.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_install_recovery.py) runs four changes: a play's
install, a campaign install in place of the map, a play's clean-up, and Remove from game after both. Each is
stopped after every file copy, file taken out, config replacement, ledger write and journal write. Then Remove from
game runs, and every file of the install (the editor's folder aside) must be byte for byte as before, with nothing
of the change left. The test also covers:
- the first review's case, a campaign replacement stopped at its final ledger write: the next look undoes it, the
  variant is no map of the install, and it installs again;
- a hand edit made in between, which is kept and reported;
- an error part-way, which is undone at once;
- no tasklist started.

Without the journal, the stop cases fail. The bake suite's
[test_deploy.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_deploy.py) checks the write is whole or not at all. The viewer suite,
the bake tests of `deploy_fixture` and the lab suite pass.

Known gap: the play's commands file and the play's kept config and save copies are not part of the journal. They
have their own clean-up.

### Drafts for recovery belong to the page that keeps them; Replace saves over the revision it showed

Review findings 3 and 4, and the waiting change of finding 34.

- **Drafts for recovery** (finding 3). Each page makes an id as it loads, and keeps its unsaved changes in a draft of
  its own: `.workshop\<id>\recovery-<page>.json` in [projects.py](../tools/viewer/projects.py), for prefabs too
  ([prefabs.py](../tools/viewer/prefabs.py)). Two tabs on one project keep a draft each.
  - A page deletes only its own draft (on saving, discarding or leaving), or the one it showed the user and the user
    restored or discarded, and that one only while it is still the one shown. A clean tab leaving deletes nothing.
  - A save deletes the saving page's draft only. The `DELETE` route must say whose draft (`?owner=`, plus `savedAt`
    for one shown) ([viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py)).
  - A draft based on an older revision than the saved one (another tab saved meanwhile) is kept, answered as stale,
    and the page says so once. Prefabs refused such drafts, and the page dropped the refusal silently.
  - Opening offers the newest draft, with the revision it was made on when that is older and how many more are kept.
    Restoring makes it the page's own. Discard offers the next. A draft that equals the saved state goes.
  - A draft write that fails is said in a banner for projects as for prefabs, once until a write goes through.
  - An owner-less `recovery.json` from before is listed and goes only when shown and discarded or restored.
- **Replace** (finding 4). Save as onto another project saves over the revision the confirmation showed
  ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js) `saveProject`). One saved since is asked about again, with its revision
  now ([project_files.js](../tools/viewer/web/project_files.js)). A prefab file imported over one of the library's
  names the revision its question showed (`expectedRevision`): a bare replace is refused, and one saved since is a
  clash again, with its new revision ([prefabs.js](../tools/viewer/web/prefabs.js)).
- **A failed save keeps the waiting change** (finding 34). A map or prefab change waiting for the Save dialog waits
  through a refused save: the next save that succeeds goes on to it, and Cancel calls it off.
- The [contract](../research/editor-contracts.md) and the [viewer README](../tools/viewer/README.md) say how
  drafts are kept now.
- Checked:
  - [test_projects.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_projects.py): two pages' drafts, a clean page leaving, saves and
    discards in either order, a stale draft, a draft refused once kept again, owner-less drafts and bad owners, and
    the routes.
  - [test_prefabs.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_prefabs.py): the import's revision.
  - [test_prefab_builder.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_prefab_builder.py): a prefab's stale draft kept.
  - A new browser check, [browser_documents.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_documents.py), on a test server:
    - two windows: two dirty pages and a clean third, saves and discards in either order, a stale draft and its
      banner, a lost tab's draft restored in another page, a failed draft write and reopening after it;
    - Replace after another window saved the target, and a prefab file replaced after the library's copy changed;
    - a save refused, then a save that goes on to the waiting change.

    It runs on its own or as [browser_smoke.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_smoke.py) `--only documents`
    (with `--projects`). The builder check passes as it was.
  - [browser_builder.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_builder.py) names the revision its import replaces.

### Packages the server opens are freed, and the collision cache keeps a bounded number by package

Review finding 19.

- [package.py](../tools/viewer/package.py): `Package.properties` kept its answers with `@lru_cache` on the method,
  whose key held the package, so no package the server opened was ever freed (on URB_Bar 61 MB after its properties
  were read, still alive after `del`). The answers are now kept in a dictionary on the package itself and go with it.
  The sound cache's limit of 8 packages, and the library's packages opened per request, now free what they let go.
- [collision.py](../tools/viewer/collision.py): the collision cache is keyed by the package's SHA-256, so a
  re-export of the same file reads nothing again (before, it opened a second copy keyed by the export's folder), keeps
  only the last two decoded packages open and the answers of the last sixteen, and answers a mesh it has from those
  without opening the package. The collision route ([viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py)) reads each export's
  scene.json once per size and time for its mesh list and source, not on every request.
- Checked: [test_package_lifetime.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_package_lifetime.py) (new) opens a small package
  made by `pack_card`, reads its properties, lets it go and checks with a weak reference that it is freed; checks that
  the collision cache opens a file once for two generations, lets the first package go at a limit of one, gives the same
  answers after, and that the route's scene is read once. The viewer suite passes.

### Two windows saving the favourites at once no longer lose one's change

Review finding 21, in [library.save_state](../tools/viewer/library.py).

- The revision check and the file's replacement are one step under a lock on `library.json.lock` beside the file (the
  operating system's, so it holds across threads and across servers). Two saves from the same revision get revision 1
  and a 409 with that revision; the page already reloads and applies its change again on a 409. Before, both could
  read revision 0 and both be told revision 1, and the first star was lost.
- The temporary file has a name of its own for each save, so two saves never write the same one (a fixed name could
  also fail the replace on Windows), and it is removed if the replace fails.
- Checked: [test_library.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_library.py) holds two saves (a star and a recently used
  piece) until both have read revision 0: one wins with revision 1, the other gets a 409 with revision 1, the file
  holds the winner's change, the merged save gets revision 2, and no temporary file is left.

### A prefab saved from a selection keeps its made pieces and broken copies; one conversion for a piece's record

Review finding 6. A drawn wall, floor, roof or ground shape saved into a prefab from a selection was stored and placed
again as a plain copy of its donor, and a broken copy of a map's fracturing piece lost its blasts, with nothing said.
Test in game built them as their donors too.

- [piece_records.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_records.js) is the one conversion between a piece as the page holds
  it (its tint, flags, made numbers and blasts) and its record. The clipboard (`snapshot`, `pasteSnapshot`), a project
  (`editState`, `applyState`), a prefab saved from a selection (`prefabRecords`), the prefab builder's document and a
  prefab placed (`prefabClip`) all use it, so none of them can leave a field out. It is the first module taken out of
  [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js), which also takes `PIECE_FIELDS`, `MADE_KINDS` and `cloneBlasts` from it.
- A clip's entry now carries the piece's `state`. The placing preview draws a prefab's made pieces from their own
  meshes, which `prefabClip` asks for before the preview shows.
- Prefab files are schema 4: a copied piece may have `generated`, `blasts` and `breaksFurther`, as a project's added
  record has them. [prefabs.py](../tools/viewer/prefabs.py) reads schema 1 to 4 and stores 4. It checks a made
  piece's numbers as data only (a kind it knows, then numbers, words and short texts, bounded), and the compiler
  checks what they mean. [prefabs.js](../tools/viewer/web/prefabs.js) writes 4. The
  [contracts](../research/editor-contracts.md) say so.
- [prefab_stage.py](../tools/editor/prefab_stage.py) passes the three fields to the test's project, so Test in
  game builds the pieces as they are.
- Checked: [piece_records_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/piece_records_test.mjs) round-trips a wall with an
  opening and a blast, a floor with a hole, a ramp, a rock with moved points and a broken copy.
  [test_prefabs.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_prefabs.py) saves and reads them back and refuses malformed ones, and
  [test_prefab_stage.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_prefab_stage.py) checks they reach the test's project. The new
  browser check `made-prefab` ([browser_editing.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_editing.py), through
  `browser_smoke.py --only made-prefab`) pastes those pieces on the Bar, saves the selection as a prefab, places it
  again and compares every record. It also compares the placing preview's size with the pieces placed, and checks
  that the builder opens the prefab unchanged. Two prefab checks in `browser_smoke.py` now expect schema 4. The
  `prefabs`, `prefab_effects`, `builder` and `prefab-test` checks pass. The `prefab-test` check's stand-in play status
  now carries the game install that the Game menu's Installs section reads
  ([browser_prefab_test.py](../tools/viewer/tests/browser_prefab_test.py)). Before, the check failed on every page
  it opened with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'folder')".
- Not checked in the game: a prefab holding a made wall and a broken copy built through Test in game.

### The main server takes its port before it prunes, and the map list, the pruning and the Build choose the same generation, of the install's own file

Review findings 16, 17 and 18, and the `SystemExit` item of finding 44.

- **Port first** ([viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py)): `serve` binds the port before it prunes the cache or
  reads its catalogue, and sets the routes once everything is ready (`serve_cache`). A second start while the editor
  runs (the release launcher's `serve --reuse` on every launch, or a double start) finds the port taken and opens the
  browser on the running editor, or stops with the reason, having deleted and read nothing of the cache the running
  server serves. The port also listens at once, so `xcom_editor.cmd`'s 15-second wait no longer runs out while a large
  prune runs. The [release launcher](../tools/release/XCOM%20Map%20Workshop.cmd) needed no change.
- **One check of a generation** ([catalogue.py](../tools/viewer/catalogue.py)): `check_scene` decides what is
  usable for the map list, [prune.py](../tools/viewer/prune.py) and the Build's
  [compiler.find_export](../tools/editor/compiler.py): the scene reads whole, is of schema 1, names its map and
  exporter version, and a folder named as a generation agrees with its scene's package, version and scope. Prune keeps
  the newest readable generation of each package and scope and deletes only older ones; a newer one it can't read
  (truncated, another schema, another package's under this one's name) is left, never taken as the newest. Before, it
  ranked folders by name and could delete the generation the map list served. `find_export` passes over a candidate
  that can't be used for the next one instead of stopping on a `JSONDecodeError`. A scene.json is read once per size
  and time for the map list and the pruning together.
- **`find_export` raises `ExportMissing`**, not `SystemExit`, with the same words (the page's Prepare prompt matches
  them). [Build.snapshot](../tools/editor/build.py) turns it into a `BuildError`, so the build's own "build
  failed:" line is written; [prefab_stage.py](../tools/editor/prefab_stage.py), the compiler's command line and
  [library.donor_area_lights](../tools/viewer/library.py) catch it.
- **Maps of the install's own file**: with a game install, each exported map serves its newest export made from the
  install's file of it (`with_install` with each map's SHA-256), and is listed unprepared, so exported on first open,
  when the cache holds only other files' exports of it, such as the other install's copy. Before, another install's
  export was offered as ready and the Build then refused it. The SHA-256 of each package is kept by size and time in
  the cache root (`.package-digests.json`), so a start hashes only the exported maps whose file changed. Choosing
  another install chooses again; `/maps.json` rechecks each file's size and time (`ExportRunner.recheck`), so a
  package changed in place is served from its own export or exported again.
- **"Cache everything"** deletes a donor's older piece generations of the same file only
  ([library.precache](../tools/viewer/library.py), prune.py's rule); the other install's stay, so switching between
  the Long War and plain copies no longer exports every piece again.
- Checked: [test_prune.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_prune.py) runs the map list, the dry run and `find_export`
  together over truncated, foreign-schema, foreign-package and wrong-version generations, an equal-version re-export
  and a pinned one, and runs `viewer.py serve` (with and without `--reuse`) against a held port with a spy on prune
  and the catalogue: nothing deleted or read, both generations there, the running server still serving.
  [test_catalogue.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_catalogue.py) chooses between two installs' copies of a map,
  switches back, a third file with no export, and a file changed in place; [test_precache.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_precache.py)
  keeps another file's piece generation; [test_export_choice.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_export_choice.py) (new)
  checks the Build's error; [test_compiler.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_compiler.py)'s `find_export` test passes
  over four unusable candidates. The viewer and editor suites pass.
