every writer adds a name new to the map to the grower's table, past the end of the map's. The next walk over that
object then stopped with "bad property name". Ten call sites patched the walker's names by hand, nine more used
`buildings.grown_walker`, and the rest did not. A Build stopped on it where it was reproduced: a copy with "Mouse picks
it" off on a map no object of which saves that flag's property (URB_HighwayFallen; CB2_MP_Blank and Command1 lack it
too), in `link_children`; and a light changed in two values it does not save where the first is new to the map, on
CsmallScout_Farm (a point light's falloff exponent) and CBattleship_01 (a spot light's inner cone).

- [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py)'s `Walker(p, g)` takes its names from the grower `g` when it is
  given one; every site with a grower in hand passes it, in [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py),

  [stream_copy.py](../tools/bake/stream_copy.py). The hand patches and `buildings.grown_walker` are gone. A walker

- Checked: [test_native_lights.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_native_lights.py)'s fake package keeps its own copy

### A play's saves are put apart from a campaign's without losing either, and a stopped restore can be run again

Review finding 1. After a play, [playsaves.restore](../tools/viewer/playsaves.py) moves a play's save off a slot it
wrote over and puts the campaign's save back from its copy. Two ways lost a save:

- With one occupied slot (or when the play wrote the highest of contiguous slots), the slot the play's save moved to
  was its own, and the copy going back then overwrote the play's save. The fresh slot is now worked out from every
  slot in use, the play's own and the copied ones included, and never names a file that is there.
- A restore that stopped part-way (a failed copy, a stopped server) and was run again went only by the slots still
  there, skipped the empty one and deleted the copies. Restoring is now driven by the copies as well: a copied
  save whose slot is empty goes back through a temporary file (not a `save<N>` name, so the game never lists it),
  checked against the hash recorded when it was copied, and a copy is deleted only once its slot holds its bytes. A
  copy that is not the save copied is kept and said so (`left`, also in
  [installs.restore_saves](../tools/viewer/installs.py)' `lastSaves`).

A copied save whose slot is empty at the end of a play is put back even when the play did not empty it (a campaign
save deleted from the game's menu during the play comes back): keeping a campaign's save is the safer mistake.

Checked: [test_playsaves.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_playsaves.py) runs one slot, contiguous slots (the play on
the lowest and the highest) and gaps, then a restore stopped before and after each of its moves and copies, run again,
and compares both saves byte for byte. The first review's two cases fail on the old code. The play tests' save test
passes as before.

### The server checks every request's Host, refuses network paths in its static routes and answers every failure

Review findings 45 and 46, in [viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py).

- **Static routes** (the page's files, `/cache/<map>/`, `/cache-library/`): `contained` refuses a part that is
  absolute, names a drive or a network share, starts with a slash or backslash, or holds a colon or a NUL, before
  anything is joined, and compares the joined path with the root without resolving it. Before, `GET
  /%5C%5Chost%5Cshare%5Cf`, `/C:/Windows/win.ini` and `/cache/<map>///host/share/f` were resolved (so opened) before the
  containment test refused them. Only the one slash a request path starts with is taken off.
- **Host and Origin on every request**: `parse_request` checks them once, before any route, for reads as well as
  writes. A page elsewhere, or one that rebinds its name to 127.0.0.1, now reads nothing (the projects, the settings,
  `/play.json`) and gets a 403 with the reason. 127.0.0.1 and localhost with the server's port both pass, as the
  release launcher, the browser tests and the guide's shots use them. A refused request's body is read, so a kept-alive
  connection's next request starts clean.
- **Every failure answered**: one wrapper (`answer`) around every route turns an exception a route does not answer into
  a JSON 500 with its text (the traceback still goes to the server's window). Before, anything but a `ProjectError` on
  five route groups (a Save on a full disk, a failed export start, a game folder that fails to load) dropped the
  connection with no reason.
- **Content-Length**: `body_length` checks a raw body's length on every route that reads one (400 for a value that is
  not a whole number of 0 or more, 413 over the route's limit). A bad value raised with no answer, and a negative one
  made `rfile.read(-1)` hold the handler's thread until the client closed.
- Checked: [test_server_guard.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_server_guard.py) (new) replays the three paths and three
  more over HTTP (404), checks `contained` touches nothing on disk for twelve refused forms, checks Host and Origin on
  reads of every kind of route, a route that raises (500 with its text, and the server goes on), and bad and negative
  lengths on two raw-body routes. The viewer suite passes.

- Checked: [test_compiler_malformed.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_compiler_malformed.py) puts each of the six cases

### A build runs from a folder whose name the system's code page lacks

Review finding 35. The server reads a build's output as UTF-8, and the Build reads each tool's the same way, but
nothing told those Python children to write it: a piped Python child writes in the system's ANSI code page. The Build
echoes each tool's command line, which holds the builds and work folders under Documents, so a user name the code page
lacks (Cyrillic or Chinese on a Western system) stopped a build at its first tool with `UnicodeEncodeError`, and an
accented one gave garbled logs.

- [procs.py](../tools/viewer/procs.py): `utf8_env()` gives a child's environment `PYTHONUTF8=1` and
  `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`, and `launch`, which starts every build, prefab-test build and queued build, uses it. Every
  process below a build inherits it.
- [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py): `_run` starts each tool with it.
- Checked: [test_procs.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_procs.py) launches a child from a folder with a Cyrillic name
  and [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py) runs a tool through `Build._run` from one, each with the
  test's own environment stripped of both variables. Both failed before the change (`cp1252`, `UnicodeEncodeError`).
- Not changed here: exports, library scans and the cache job still start with a plain `Popen` (finding 48).

- [package_edit.py](../tools/upk/package_edit.py): `compressed_layout` puts an uncompressed package in the compressed
  cooked maps' layout (the same logical bytes in literal-LZO chunks; the summary with a chunk table, PKG_StoreCompressed
  and LZO; the header's tables whole in the first chunk; the export data cut into chunks of up to 1 MB only where an
  export's data starts). `package_bytes` reads a package that way, and `write_edited` reads through it (or takes the
  bytes from its caller). `chunk_cuts` and `literal_chunk` moved here from the grower.
- [package_grow.py](../tools/upk/package_grow.py): the grower reads through `package_bytes`, so every build step that
  grows a map takes an uncompressed one and writes it compressed; its chunks come from `literal_chunk`; `sizeChange`
  is against the file as it was.
- Tests: [test_package_edit.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_package_edit.py) makes the bar uncompressed and checks the layout
  against the bar's own (every summary field, the first chunk, cuts at export starts, decoding) and an edit written
  from it; [test_package_grow.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_package_grow.py) grows the uncompressed bar (an edit, a name, a
  moved export) and the install's Furies (which failed on the old writer with the user's error).
- Checked: the user's project, built here with the 0.6.0 error first, now builds whole (cover blocks seeded, both
  flags written, the intro copy made; the map reads back with LZO chunks, `0x228a0009` flags as the cooked maps have).
  Suites: upk, bake and editor. Not played in the game.

  one back:
  - `parse_record` reads a `Maps=`, `Pictures=` or `LZArray=` ini line (keys without regard to capitals, nested
    brackets, `key[n]`);
  - `card` writes the package: every field of every line, a gap in a line's streamed maps filled with empty
    elements, the ship type as a number, and names ending in `_<number>` stored as the engine keeps them (a base and
    the number), so a map family such as `CSmallScout_Farm_2001` equals the name the game makes from text;
  - the same lines give the same bytes (the package's GUID comes from its contents);
  - `read` gives the lines back, and `enum_warnings` names enum values the game's script lacks.
  - Checked: [test_pack_card.py](../tools/upk/tests/test_pack_card.py) (26 tests): lines parsed, cards written and read
    back, a fixed card's bytes, every map and landing line of the configured LWR install through a card and back with
    its enum values found in the game's script, and both ways against the LWR team's reference writer (a private
    copy; those tests skip without it).

- **The Build writes the project's map picture into the map** (LWR map packs plan, stage C5; branch
  `lwr-map-picture`). [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py):
  - `Build.picture`, the step after the seeds in `Build.package`, in quick and full builds alike: the picture file
    the project names (kept by [pictures.py](../tools/viewer/pictures.py)) is written into the package's map as its
    `MapPicture` by [map_frame.py](../tools/bake/map_frame.py), before the files are hashed. The seeder wants the world
    data last in the map it reads; the picture is written after it has run, by a writer that appends, so nothing of
    the seeds moves.
  - The manifest gets `picture: {sha256, format}` (absent when the map has none) and the stage `picture`; the README
    names the picture; map_frame.py is among the manifest's tools.
  - A project that names a picture whose file is not on the computer builds without one: a note (`note:` in the log,
    the manifest's `pictureNote`, a README line), never a refusal or a warning.
  - A changed picture is an ordinary rebuild. No picture-only shortcut was built: a build does not record which of
    its inputs still hold (the install's config, the donors, the tools), so "only the picture changed" can't be told
    safely from the last package.
  - Checked: [test_build.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_build.py), five tests (with a picture: the stage after the
    seeds, the map's bytes, the manifest entry and hash, the README, a quick build too; without: none of it; a
    missing file and a malformed record: the note; a changed picture builds again; the real writer on
    URB_TruckStop_Stream, skipped without the game). The `editor` and `repo` suites, `viewer -k build`. A real quick
    build of a scratch project on URB_Bar (one piece deleted, a picture) from the command line into a scratch builds
    folder: the built map's last export is `MapPicture` with the next net index, read back whole by `native_fields`,
    its pixels the kept file's.
  - Not checked: the game showing the picture (no game was started).

    - **One row of icon buttons** under the name: Copy, Delete, Select all of a kind (its count beside the icon, the
      kind's name in the tooltip), and at the right Reset piece and Save as prefab. The horizontal scrollbar came from
      the Select all button carrying the piece's name; the panel also keeps its scrollbar's room
      (`scrollbar-gutter`).

      **sections that fold to one line** saying what they hold: Group, Align, Flags ("as the map has them",
      "2 changed"), Place (the position and yaw) and Source (the class). Each keeps how it was left
      (`viewer.fold.<name>`); Flags and Source start folded, the others open. Position and rotation are one row each.
    - **How-to text is out of sight until asked for**: a section's info button shows its `.how` notes (the handles,
      "made from numbers", what a group does, why Break together is greyed, the Flags note). What a thing is stays in
      sight on one line (`wallState`, `slabState`, `groundState`, `roomState`), and so do warnings.

      marked), where every row carried its own sentence.
    - **Gaps and holes**: one line each with a warning mark where it plays oddly and a small remove button; its
      sentence is the row's tooltip and shows with the section's info. Add gap, Flip sides and Reshuffle share a row.

- **Flags on made walls, floors and ground** (the user: the Flags group was greyed on them; branch
  `fracturing-wall-poc`).
  - Why: a made piece takes its flags from its donor's record, and pieces of other maps (the library's export,
    namespace `lib-`) carried none. [export.py](../tools/viewer/export.py) `piece_flags` left them out of every prefixed
    export, though the library's were meant to have them since piece version 9. Now only streamed and inherited
    packages' pieces go without. [library.py](../tools/viewer/library.py) `PIECE_VERSION` 10: old piece records are made
    again on first use.
  - [piece_flags.py](../tools/viewer/piece_flags.py) `made_settings`, `made`, `MADE_GROUND` (in the contract with the
    class defaults; [piece_flags.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_flags.js) `madeSettings`, `made` are the twins): a made
    piece's flags are planned on what the Build makes of its donor.
    - Every made piece has simple collision of its own: no note that the donor's mesh has none.
    - A ground shape collides. On a static mesh actor it is an XComLevelActor (frac_walls' retype), so walking, cover,
      sight and the mouse are its settings too: what the donor saves keeps its value, the rest is the level piece's
      default (cooked maps' static mesh actors have no archetype), then `ground_collision`'s writes.
  - Where it is used:
    - the page's Flags group and chip ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js) `flagSource`);
    - the compiler's `flag_plan` and `copy_flags` ([compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py));
    - the Build's `set_roles` ([native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py)). Its ground writes are now the constants
      `GROUND_ON` and `GROUND_SAVED`, and a ground copy no longer claims a bPathColliding it wasn't given.
  - Checked:
    - new tests: `MadePieces` in [test_piece_flags.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_piece_flags.py) (the rule against
      frac_walls' and native_copy's own constants, the contract); the exporter's namespaces (install); 81 made cases
      in [piece_flag_cases.json](../tools/viewer/tests/piece_flag_cases.json), which the page's twin meets
      ([piece_flags_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/piece_flags_test.mjs));
    - the compiler on a block made on a static mesh actor and on a made wall
      ([test_compiler_flags.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_compiler_flags.py));
    - the Build on URB_CommercialAlley's asphalt with walking and cover off: written before the retype, read back as
      an XComLevelActor's ([test_frac_walls.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_frac_walls.py));
    - the viewer, editor and node suites, and the Build's native flags and made-wall tests;
    - on a test server: the five rows enabled on a made floor, a ground block on a static mesh actor and a made wall;
      Blocks sight turned off on the wall; a quick Build of that project.
  - Not played in the game.

    of a look whose bottom is -16 kept z0 -16 in one whose bottom is 0 (here Melt Tut Int B), and the page's check
    (`toolWall`) refused a gap below the bottom, so the wall read as numbers made elsewhere.

    to the old bottom is cut to the new one; none starts below it); `toolWall` takes a gap that starts below the bottom
    (it is cut to the floor, as `openingEdges` and the Build already had it), so walls saved that way get their handles
    back. [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js) `setMadeLook` uses it.

    - the plate's heights (a flat or thick slab's from its main level faces up and down; a pitched roof made flat at

      faces inside;

    - fragment shares set so a made slab has about the donor's fragments a tile; the colours; the lightmap's
      density from the placing's own lightmap.

    sections, slots, faces inside, texture maps, colours, lightmap density, fragments a tile and footprint must
    agree; triangles a tile (within a tenth) is told but doesn't fail it, a made slab's fragments being cut another

### Walls in the look of any of the game's walls (custom geometry M4, work order A, step 2)

- [frac_wall.py](../tools/bake/frac_wall.py) builds from any recipe the measurer gives. A wall's `look` is an id of
  wall_looks.json, built as before, or a look by its donor, `{mesh, measure, recipe}`, built by a general path:
  - each side's own outline (the two sides may differ), ledges included;
  - every segment's slot and texture: faces take their side's face slots by height, the other segments (trims,
    steps, ledges, a donor with no trim slot, the UFOs' one unwrap for the whole outline) their own;
  - the top's and bottom's slot and texture, the donor's collision across the wall, its slot count (`sections`: the
    mesh has as many, in slot order, an empty one with no triangles; the Bar's look keeps 6);
  - one storey for a taller donor: 192 taken out of the longest stretch that is straight up on both sides
    (`storeys_of`, `storey_cut`, `lowered`).
- [wall_measure.py](../tools/bake/wall_measure.py): `measure(package, what)` gives a look's entry: its recipe, its
  warnings in plain words ("its window frames and ledges aren't made" for a modelled wall, as D12 says) and its facts
  (size, the storeys it can be made at ([1], [2] or [1, 2]; [3] or [1, 3] for the taller donors), the sweep's verdict,
  inside or outside). It measures each segment's slot and texture over the cuts and fits them over its triangles.
  `twin(recipe)` builds the wall at its donor's length and measures it again: its outline, what each side shows (read
  off the made mesh), its caps, colours, cells, collision, lightmap, slots and storeys against the recipe.
- [frac_walls.py](../tools/bake/frac_walls.py), only for the looks' generality:
  - a wall's shortest length, its storeys, its box and its doorways' boxes follow its look;
  - a made wall's copy stands at scale 1 where its donor is scaled (made_matrix, unscale; a donor at scale 1 keeps its
    bytes);
  - a measured look's paint is taken in the wall's own frame (in_frame: the donor turned and centred as measured, a
    longer wall repeating the donor's paint with the ends' paint at its ends).

  - All 344 donors measured and built four ways: the twin, a 4-tile wall with a doorway and a window, a 16-tile wall

### Custom geometry, stage M6 (item 2): the ground materials audit and six ground looks

- [ground-audit.py](../research/evidence/ground-audit.py) (read only; output
  [ground-audit-2026-11-18.json](../research/evidence/ground-audit-2026-11-18.json)) reads every plain piece at least a
  tile across in the install's 97 base maps: 49,871 placings, 2,278 meshes, 1,297 materials. For each ground or rock
  material it records:
  - its root and blend mode;
  - its texture channels;
  - its repeat on the placings' tops;
  - its lightmaps;
  - its painted colours;
  - a donor.
- What it found:
  - Most of the game's main ground blends layers by painted vertex colours.
  - Lightmaps are textures, at 0.13 to 0.2 texels a unit in play areas.
  - Repeats are 320 for the 960 planes, 384 for concrete tiles and pavers, 192 for sidewalks.
  - No material needs a third channel. There is no sand.
  - Many donors are backdrop planes saved with their collision off.
- [ground_looks.json](../tools/bake/ground_looks.json) and [ground.js](../tools/viewer/web/ground.js) list six looks. Each
  donor is placed at scale 1 with one material, in a map the editor reads:

  - Concrete (URB_StreetHurricane);

  - Dirt (URB_MilitaryAmmo).

  cover and climbing, whatever its donor saves.
  - Actor: bCollideActors, plus bPathColliding on an XComLevelActor.
  - Mesh: CollideActors and BlockRigidBody.
  - Where the donor saves them otherwise: bIgnoreForCover off, bCanClimbOnto and bIsValidDestination on.

### Custom geometry, stage M6 (item 3): general convex hulls, as the game's cooker writes them

- [hull-audit.py](../research/evidence/hull-audit.py) (read only; output
  [hull-audit-2026-11-18.json](../research/evidence/hull-audit-2026-11-18.json)) rebuilds the install's convex collision
  hulls from their corners. There are 18,195 elements, 3,337 unique by value.
- **The cooker's rules**, read from the game (`FKConvexElem::GenerateHullData`):
  - PhysX gives the hull's vertices and triangles.
  - UE3 derives the rest:
    - the face normals and planes, with its dedupe thresholds;
    - the edge directions, in first-met order;
    - the element box;
    - the permuted vertex rows.
  - At load the game cooks physics from the vertices alone.
- **Results.**
  - From the saved vertices and triangles, every element's box and permuted rows come out byte for byte. So do all
    but 4 face-direction sets, all but 3 edge-direction sets, and 82% of plane sets (the rest differ in the
    distance's last bits).
  - From corners alone (an emulation of PhysX 2's incremental hull), 56% are byte-exact in every field.
  - Wedges: 51 of 54 are exact from vertices and triangles, and 43 from corners. All 10 of the farm ramp's hulls are
    exact from their vertices and faces.
- The writer `hull_element` (in the script for now, with `wedge()` and a self-check) gives `cover_blocks`' hull form
  for any convex shape. For M6's ramps it is recommended over thin steps: thin steps would give flat tiles that give
  cover.

Checked: `--self-check` (a box equals `cover_blocks.convex_hull`; the farm ramp; a wedge closed and bounded; the
inverse square root table against the saved unit lengths); the run over the install; the `repo` suite.

- A made wall standing in one of the map's own buildings is listed in that building's floors by the game editor's
  rule for its own box: the floors whose volumes it touches, with their CutdownFloor. So it hides and cuts down floor
  by floor as a piece placed there in the game's editor would, and a two-storey wall lands in both floors.
  - Code: [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py) `list_made_walls`. The manifest gains `madeWallFloors` and the
    Build's log names the floors.
  - Before this, a made wall took its donor's listing, moved (`edit_floor_caches`): another shape, and nothing at all
    when the donor comes from another map. Made walls now skip that path.
- Buildings made in the editor and buildings edited in place list a made wall by its own box too
  ([buildings.py](../tools/bake/buildings.py) `piece_box` takes a candidate's `box`), not by its donor's mesh.

Checked: test_frac_walls `MadeWallInBuilding`, a Build on URB_Bar:
- the twin of the Bar's inside wall at the donor's place is listed exactly where the Bar lists the donor (floor 0,
  CutdownFloor 2);
- a one-storey wall there is in the ground floor only;
- an editor building takes a candidate's own box.

### Custom walls, stage M4 (items 2 and 3): wall looks measured, and which of the game's walls a generator can make

- [wall-look-measure.py](../research/evidence/wall-look-measure.py) measures one of the game's fracturing walls into a
  look entry with `frac_wall.RECIPE`'s keys:
  - the cross-section and its trim v;
  - face heights and storey split;
  - slots' roles, texture repeats and offsets;
  - colours, fragment size and lightmap density.
  `--check` measures the Bar's donor back to RECIPE: 22 of 22 keys within tolerance. The cells' jitter and the
  packing margin are not measurable.
- [wall-look-audit.py](../research/evidence/wall-look-audit.py) measures every wall mesh of the listed maps (output
  [wall-look-audit-2026-11-18.json](../research/evidence/wall-look-audit-2026-11-18.json); the Bar check and four
  candidates in [wall-looks-measured-2026-11-18.json](../research/evidence/wall-looks-measured-2026-11-18.json)):
  - It tests each mesh by cuts across its length: swept as the Bar's, swept with openings, framed openings, mostly
    swept, or modelled.
  - Of 246 meshes named as walls, 202 are swept in some form and 44 modelled (mostly outside walls with window
    frames). 98 more wall-shaped meshes are found (ComKit cores, office and outpost walls), all swept.
  - It recommends 12 candidates across settings: shop and office interiors, brick and pub shopfronts, concrete, the
    pier's metal panels, the police station, the outpost, and two UFO walls (the alien base has no fracturing pieces).
  - All are base-game walls.
  - What a generator needs beyond the Bar's recipe: slots by look, side B's own outline, other heights and tops, ends
    on or past the tile edge, per-look cells and densities.

Checked: `--check` on the Bar's donor; the audit over all 151 maps; the `repo` suite.

### Custom geometry, stage M5 (item 1): the game's fracturing floors and roofs

### Custom walls, stage M3 (items 2 and 3): joined ends, and neighbour lists by the game's rule

- **End styles.** A made wall's end is free, joined at an L, or end to end, as the game's walls meet (the joint audit):
  - [frac_wall.py](../tools/bake/frac_wall.py): `ends` in a wall's numbers, `END_INSETS`. A free end stops 8 short of
    its tile edge as before; so do a T's stem and the wall that butts at an L. `through` reaches the far face of the
    wall it meets, so the corner square is filled. `line` ends on the tile edge.
  - [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `wall_joins` and `join_made_walls` work out the ends from where the
    project's made walls stand:
    - an end within a unit of another wall's end or line, on the same floor, is joined;
    - at an L, the taller wall runs through, then the longer, then the one along x;
    - ends leaving one point in opposite directions are end to end;
    - an end on a wall that passes through the point is a stem.
  - The copy's Build request becomes version 2 with `ends`, and its box follows its solid. The project file is
    unchanged: ends are never saved.
  - [frac_walls.py](../tools/bake/frac_walls.py) `check` takes versions 1 and 2.
  - The page works ends out the same way ([walls.js](../tools/viewer/web/walls.js) `wallJoins`, the twin, and
    `joinWords`; [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js) `refreshJoins`, run after every change). A wall whose ends
    changed is drawn anew, and the Wall panel says how it is joined.
  - [generated.py](../tools/viewer/generated.py) draws the ends.
- **Neighbour lists** ([frac_walls.py](../tools/bake/frac_walls.py) `neighbour_columns`, `lists_column`;
  [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py)). A made wall and every fracturing piece it touches list each other's
  columns by the game's rule: other made walls, the map's own pieces and copies, the roof slab over its top. So a
  break passes between them where they meet, as between the game's walls. The manifest gains `neighbourListings`, and
  the Build's log names each pair. An index of 0 is left out of an entry, as the game saves it. The compiler's note
  on a made wall says a break passes on.
- The manifest's copies carry their labels. The made-wall group test committed earlier read them and failed without
  them.

### Custom walls, stage M2 (Build side): light that fits, one-storey walls

- A made wall's lightmap is a rectangle of its own size: [frac_wall.py](../tools/bake/frac_wall.py) packs its charts at
  the donor's density on its faces (0.196 texels a unit, measured on URB_Bar's donor in a baked Build) into the
  smallest rectangle of whole DXT1 blocks it finds (`pack_rect`, `lightmapRect`; the old square left about 30% empty),
  and [frac_walls.py](../tools/bake/frac_walls.py) gives the copy's lightmap that rectangle in its own cloned atlas, which
  the relight fills (`set_light`). A 16-tile wall gets 300 x 260 texels.

  ShadowMap2D of that light and of its texture, the lightmap's rectangle), which the relight fills as a piece of
  another map's, and the light is taken off its IrrelevantLights (the donor, an inside wall, lists the Bar's moon
  there) (`dominant_shadow`, `shadow_map_export`, `irrelevant`, `add_shadow_ref`).
- A Build without baking gives each made wall one even light (D9): every vertex at one texel of the lightmap of the
  map's nearest lit piece, the texel nearest its median light (`even_light`), and that piece's shadow map of the
  dominant light at the same texel, or the light listed irrelevant where the piece has none (`piece_shadow`). The
  Build's log says which.
- One-storey walls: a wall's numbers take `storeys` (2, as before, when left out; or 1). A one-storey wall stands
  from -16 to 192, as the game's one-storey inside walls do (URB_PoliceStation's four, URB_IndustrialOffice's): the
  donor's section with its face to 180 and its cornice from there to the top; its upper storey's slots are empty
  (`shaped`). The Build checks the number.

  keeps its place for the page's materials. The Build already writes the empty section as the mesh's.

  60, high or low 88 to 104, walking 64, sight 96 over the floor; `research/native/cover-build.md`,
  `line-of-sight.md`): [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `opening_play` and `made_wall_openings` warn of a doorway
  with no door in it (a unit in it has cover toward its sides), an opening no tile's centre line passes through, a

  when a door's box (a copy's, or one of the map's own left in place) overlaps the doorway.

spawn points and no-spawn volumes, the Skyranger kept drawn on a clear, EXP-72 run 17). One conflict, this ledger:
both sides kept, main's newer entries first.

Checked: the viewer, editor, repo, node, bake and upk suites pass on the merged branch.

### Clear map: the Skyranger stays drawn with its effects; the map's ambient sounds go; the Skyranger's dust moves with it

The user, on a cleared Bar: effect and sound markers were left in the play area, and the Skyranger's effects stayed
though the Skyranger itself was gone ("either leave the skyranger and its effects on a clear or remove both").

- **The Skyranger was never taken out; the view hid it.** The clear keeps the landing's pieces, and the Build left
  the Skyranger where it was. But the page took the kept zone for moved and hid the Skyranger and the drop zone's
  frame, drawing an outline in their place, while it still drew their lights and dust. The zone is the install's line
  joined with the map's own landing, and on the Bar that line stands a unit off the frame (719 against 719.9998). The
  page's test allowed half a unit; the Build's (native_spawns.py `unmoved`) allows 4 units for the frame and the
  soldier points. Before a clear the page has no zone list of its own, so the test never ran. The clear writes one,
  and the Skyranger vanished. [spawns.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawns.js) `landingUnmoved` now follows the Build's rule,
  and [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js) `movedLandingActors` and `landingShifts` use it.
- **The map's ambient sounds go with a clear** ([native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py): the AmbientSound
  classes moved from `CLEAR_KEEP` to `CLEAR_OUT` and `KEEP_OUTSIDE`). They follow the emitters' rule: the
  landing's stay (the Skyranger's sound), so do those outside the play area when the tick keeps the scenery outside,
  one the project moved (the sounds lane's moves join `effect_moved`), and the project's copies (made after the
  clear). [effects_rules.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_rules.js) `survivesClear` no longer keeps every sound. Sounds
  stayed before because the clear came before sounds could be edited.
- **The Skyranger's dust moves with it** (export 35): the ARC_Skyranger_Ground_Periphery emitter stands beside the
  Skyranger's prefab, not in it. [scene_metadata.py](../tools/viewer/scene_metadata.py) `landing_metadata` lists it with
  the nearest Skyranger (within 2,500 units) as role `dust`. A moved zone now carries it with the Skyranger's mesh,
  lights and sound, in the Build (native_spawns `plan`) and in the view; before, it stayed where the Skyranger had
  been. The Farm's Skyrangers have none.
- **The Clear window** (`clearedEffects`) counts the effects and ambient sounds it removes and the landing's it
  keeps: on the Bar "Removes 964 pieces, 254 lights, 9 spawn points (...), 70 effects and 5 ambient sounds. Keeps the
  landing's 2 pieces and its 3 effects and sounds, ...".
- The guide ([guide.html](../tools/release/guide/guide.html)): the Clear map window's counts and what stays (the
  Skyranger's lights, dust and sound), the tick keeping sounds outside, and "Effects and ambient sounds go with the
  clear". The `clear-map` picture is retaken (its new counts; 484 by 379).
- Checked:
  - node tests: clear_map (`landingUnmoved`: the Bar's line a unit off its frame is unmoved; a tile off, or turned,
    is moved; a frameless landing by its fitted zone) and effects_rules (a sound goes, one outside stays with the
    tick, the landing's stays);
  - the viewer suite (test_spawns: the Bar's Skyranger lists its dust Emitter_0);
  - bake tests:
    - ClearLevel: the Bar's five ambient sounds go; the Skyranger's lights, dust and sound stay as the landing's;
    - BarMoved: a moved zone moves 15 actors, the dust among them;
    - Lanes: a cleared build keeps the moved sound, its copy and the Skyranger's, and takes the map's other four;
  - editor and repo suites;
  - the browser smoke `--only spawns,clear-map,effects` on a test server. After a clear no landing piece is taken for
    moved, and only the landing's effects and sounds are left. The window names the ambient sounds.
  - On the test server, a cleared Bar shows its Skyranger with its lights and dust. Not built in the game.

### Clear map deletes the map's spawn points; no-spawn volumes are edited and added; multiplayer starts hidden

The user, on a cleared Bar: the map's pods, Meld points and grey points stayed. Asked what the grey points and the
no-spawn volumes are: "If no spawn points matter then leave them in, but make them editable and allow them to be
added via the add panel".

- **Clear map** ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js) `clearedSpawns`, `clearMap`): deletes the map's pods, Meld points
  and drop-in points in the clear's one undo step, but one something names (the Build would keep it and warn: it
  stays, with its edit, and the window names it), and takes away the project's copies of them. No-spawn volumes and
  the mission streams' objects stay. The window counts the spawn points it removes and the volumes it keeps; its
  plain Enemy Within note now says to place pods with the Add panel. A pod or Meld point copied from a deleted one
  builds: [native_spawns.py](../tools/bake/native_spawns.py) no longer refuses a copy whose template the same edit
  deletes (the template stays in the package, off the level's list).
- **Deleted points hidden** ([spawns_view.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawns_view.js) `shownEntries`): a base point the
  project deletes is drawn only with the Spawns flyout's new **Deleted points** switch (off at first), pale, to be
  restored ([index.html](../tools/viewer/web/index.html)).
- **Multiplayer teams' starts** (XComSpawnPoint unit types 8 and 9, the Bar's twelve grey points) get no marker:
  single player never uses them, and Long War's landing mutator logs them as bad spawn points.
- **No-spawn volumes edited** (export 34, [scene_metadata.py](../tools/viewer/scene_metadata.py) `SPAWN_VALUES`: their
  `aliens` and `civilians` switches, AlienNoSpawnZone and CivilianNoSpawnZone, both on in the class default):
  - the Spawns view draws each as a grey box round its marker; picked, its arrows move it by whole tiles and levels
    and the Buildings view's six white face handles move a side to tile lines and levels (Alt: steps of 8), each one
    undo step; Copy (Ctrl+D, a tile east, its size), Delete, Restore, and two ticks, Keeps aliens out and Keeps
    civilians out;
  - the Add panel's **Spawn points** has **No-spawn volume** on every map: a copy of the map's first volume, its size,
    over whole tiles round the click, or on a map with none a new 3 by 3 tile, four-level volume
    ([pieces.js](../tools/viewer/web/pieces.js) draws its icon);
  - the project's records ([project.js](../tools/viewer/web/project.js)): an override with `box` [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1]
    and/or `spawn`, never a pose; an added `kind: "noSpawn"` record with `box`, `from` its template or none;
  - [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py): `noSpawn` among `SPAWN_EDIT_KINDS` and `SPAWN_COPY_KINDS`
    (`spawn_box`, `volume_add`); a pose on a volume, a box on a point, an empty box or a value of another kind is
    refused; the lane's move of a volume carries its `box`;
  - the writer: a volume's move sets its Location and DrawScale3D (unturned) so its brush spans the box; a copy is the
    template cloned over its box, and a new one the map's first plain no-spawn volume or, on a map with none, the
    rebuild volume's template retyped ([native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py) `add_volume`, `volume_pose`:
    `add_rebuild_volume` is now one of its uses); `verify` reads back each volume's scale.
- Placing a new spawn point from the Add panel lets go of the picked one, whose arrows had taken the click.
- **Pods lose Turn left and Turn right** (the user: "pods aren't aimed at anything", then "can we just get rid of
  those facing buttons ?"). Their titles said they set "the way its aliens face when they deploy", but the game's
  script (XComAlienPod.GetDistributedLocationAround) puts the first alien on the pod's place and the rest evenly
  round it from the pod's facing, each facing the middle: the facing only picks which tiles round it they take. The

  (asked why it keeps its turn: its facing is the only one that changes the game, since a unit dropped from a height,

- [spawn_rules.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawn_rules.js): a volume's In the game line says who it keeps out and that Long

- The guide ([guide.html](../tools/release/guide/guide.html)): No-spawn volumes (`#nospawn`) with a new picture

### Branch fracturing-wall-poc: main merged in

The custom walls branch stays out of main until the feature works in the editor; main is merged into it to keep it
current. This merge brings in 68 commits (release 0.5.3, effects and sounds, the spawn points, the project manager's
work).

- Both sides kept in every conflict: this ledger (the branch's entries of 17 November close that day's section, as
  they were made before main's of that day) and the [findings register](../research/findings-register.md) (F-116 after
  main's newer findings); [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) (an added record may carry `kind`, `effect`,
  `sound` and `generated`); [viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py) (the wave handler and the made walls' handler, both
  in the GET chain).
- Checked on the merged branch: the `viewer`, `editor`, `repo` and `node` suites; `bake` for `frac_wall` (28),
  `gen_mesh` (9), `native_copy` (40) and `cover_blocks` (36). Not run: the rest of `bake`, `upk`, `lab`, `release`
  (the merge touches none of their files on the branch's side), a Build of the EXP-67 project, the game.

### Hidden game runs: loads of a battle with aliens no longer crash (T-46); a crash log

- [hidden_game.py](../tools/lab/hidden_game.py) `dxvk_config`: every run gives DXVK its own `<out>\dxvk.conf`
  (`DXVK_CONFIG_FILE`) with `d3d9.textureMemory = 0`. With DXVK's texture budget on, every load of a save with aliens
  in the battle crashed on a thread of the game's own reading memory that was gone, Long War's reload of EXALT's
  missions among them ([findings register](../research/findings-register.md) T-46: not the mouse, as first thought).
- [StandInInput.c](../tools/lab/StandInInput.c), [build_stand_in_input.py](../tools/lab/build_stand_in_input.py),
  hidden_game.py `--crash-log`: the stand-in DLL stands beside the game in any case and, with
  `XCOM_STAND_IN_CRASH_LOG=1`, logs the run's first faults to `<out>\input.log` (thread, code, module and offset,
  what it touched, registers, the module addresses on that thread's stack); the run prints them at its end.
- [game-test skill](../.claude/skills/game-test/SKILL.md): a run that ends by itself with nothing in the log gets a rerun
  with `--crash-log`.
- Checked: [test_hidden_game.py](../tools/lab/tests/test_hidden_game.py) (the settings file, the crash log's plan, a fault
  on a thread of its own named by the built DLL in [StandInInputCheck.cs](../tools/lab/tests/StandInInputCheck.cs)), the
  lab suite; in the game, [EXP-72](../research/experiments/EXP-72-spawns.md) runs 15 and 16: a Bar quicksave with aliens
  loaded twice with the setting, after six crashes of six without it. Known gap: with the budget off a long session
  could run out of the game's 32-bit address space (not seen).

### Hidden game runs: the put-back waits for a crashed game's DLLs; the stand-in's trace (T-46)

- [hidden_game.py](../tools/lab/hidden_game.py) `remove_held`: a game that has just crashed can hold `d3d9.dll` and
  `dinput8.dll` a moment longer (EXP-72 run 13 left both behind and skipped the log copy). The put-back now tries again
  for up to 20 seconds, copies `Launch.log` whatever happens, and names any DLL still left.
- [StandInInput.c](../tools/lab/StandInInput.c): with `XCOM_STAND_IN_INPUT_TRACE=1` every call the game makes on a
  stand-in goes to `<out>\input.log` (the per-frame ones now and then), and so do the other devices it creates. It
  showed nothing at the load that crashed (T-46, which turned out not to be the mouse).
- Checked: [test_hidden_game.py](../tools/lab/tests/test_hidden_game.py) (a held file let go, one kept held), the lab
  suite, a traced run.

### Hidden game runs: a stand-in mouse and keyboard when Windows has none (T-45)

- [StandInInput.c](../tools/lab/StandInInput.c): a 32-bit `dinput8.dll` that hands every call to Windows' own and gives
  the game a still mouse or keyboard where Windows has none (the game's start asks DirectInput for the system mouse
  and crashed without one). No C runtime and no Windows SDK; [build_stand_in_input.py](../tools/lab/build_stand_in_input.py)
  builds it with clang-cl, lld-link and llvm-dlltool (`--llvm <LLVM bin folder>`) into `<lab>\bin`, where
  [hidden_game.py](../tools/lab/hidden_game.py) takes it from, as it takes DXVK from `<lab>\dxvk`.
- [hidden_game.py](../tools/lab/hidden_game.py) `input_plan`: with a mouse or keyboard missing in Windows the DLL goes
  beside the game for the run and comes out after (a different `dinput8.dll` already there stops the run); the DLL
  writes what the game asked for and got to `<out>\input.log`. Without the DLL, no mouse still stops the run.
  `--stand-in-input` gives the stand-ins anyway, to check them. The
  [game-test skill](../.claude/skills/game-test/SKILL.md) and the [findings register](../research/findings-register.md)'s
  T-45 say so.
- Checked: [test_hidden_game.py](../tools/lab/tests/test_hidden_game.py) (the plan's cases, the DLL placed and taken
  away, the built DLL in a 32-bit process by [StandInInputCheck.cs](../tools/lab/tests/StandInInputCheck.cs): both
  stand-ins and every call the game makes on them), the lab suite; in the game with the stand-ins forced, URB_Bar
  started to turn 1, a soldier walked two tiles by `goto` and Escape opened the pause menu, and nothing was left
  beside the game. A start with the devices really gone hasn't been played.

### Spawns, stage SP7: the base map's pods and Meld points copied, its spawn points deleted

- **The page** ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js), [spawns_view.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawns_view.js)): where the
  spawn family builds, a picked base pod, Meld point or drop-in point has Copy (Ctrl+D) and Delete (Delete) in its
  panel, and [ and ] turn a pod or a drop-in point. A copy is made only from a plain pod (no commander or secondary
  flag, no forced type, no link to another actor) or any Meld point; the button says why where it can't. It lands a
  tile east with its template's values and turn, picked, and is moved, turned and given values as the map's points
  are, its marker and panel its own ("Pod: a copy of …"; its template's saved values marked "(its template's)",
  [spawn_rules.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawn_rules.js)). A deleted point is drawn pale, its panel says whether the Build
  takes it out or keeps it (something names it), and Restore brings it back. Undo, Reset all, recovery and the
  header's count take them.
- **The document**: a copy is an `added[]` record of `kind` pod or meld with `from` its template, a pose and
  `spawn`; a delete is a deleted override ([project.js](../tools/viewer/web/project.js) `validAdded`). One the page
  doesn't take is carried and saved back unchanged.
- **The compiler** ([compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py)): `spawn_add` refuses a template that isn't plain
  (`spawn-copy-template`), one of another kind, one the export lacks, and the family off; gives each pod copy the next
  pod index above every one the map's pods and its streams' save and every pod event the export's uses name
  (`free_pod_index`; across the install's maps an event names index 1 at most, a pod 53). `spawn_delete` builds a
  delete only when nothing names the point (`spawn_names`: the Kismet, a wave place, a pod event for its index, a typed
  reference, a name list) and its uses were read; else warning `spawn-delete-named`, and the point stays. SP5's place
  counts read the copies, the deletes and the SP6 values.
- **The writer** ([native_spawns.py](../tools/bake/native_spawns.py)): a copy is its template cloned with its components
  (`native_copy.clone_actor`), placed, given its PodIndex (refused where a pod event of the map names it) and its
  values; a delete leaves its slot in the level's list empty. `verify` reads back each copy listed at its pose with its
  index and values, its template byte for byte as it was, and each delete off the list
  ([native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py) hands it the map before the edit).
- **Example** [exp72_sp7_project.py](../tools/editor/examples/exp72_sp7_project.py): URB_Bar's pods 2 and 3 copied onto
  free floor tiles near them, Meld point 2 copied and made hard, pod 4 deleted (six pods where there were five).
- **Checked** offline on URB_Bar: built twice byte for byte the same; read back with the exporter's own spawn reader:
  the copies listed as XComAlienPod_Abduction_5 and _6 with pod indices 5 and 6 and the Meld copy hard, each with
  its template's archetype and its own clones of the template's three components; pod 4 off the list; every other
  point at its place. Tests: compiler (copies, the index above a stream's pod, deletes kept back by an event or the
  Kismet, the refusals), bake (`test_native_spawns.py`: copies and a delete written and read back, the refusals),
  build (copies and deletes in a spawn-only build), node (the copy and delete rules, `validAdded`); the page tried on
  a test server with the family on (the project's copies and delete opened as saved; copy, move, value, delete,
  restore and the keys, undone back to saved; saved from the page and compiled as the page showed it).
- **Gaps**: no paste of a copied point elsewhere (a copy lands a tile east and is dragged from there); copies of
  drop-in points and of pods with links aren't made. The game check is still to come.

### Spawns, stage SP6: the base map's pods, Meld points and drop-in points moved, turned and given values

- **The family** `spawn` ([compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `FAMILIES`): off until its game check passes (a
  test server's `--family spawn` turns it on).
- **The page** ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js), [spawns_view.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawns_view.js),
  [index.html](../tools/viewer/web/index.html), [style.css](../tools/viewer/web/style.css)): where the family builds, a
  picked base pod, Meld point or drop-in point gets the Spawns view's arrows (whole tiles across, whole levels up,
  alone), Turn left and Turn right (a quarter; the picked pod or drop-in point shows the way it faces), and its
  values: a pod's Commander's place, Secondary and Use ticks, a Meld point's Difficulty, Destroyed on turn and Spawn
  group. A value back at the map's, or a point back where and as the map has it, is no edit; "As the map has it" puts
  it back. Each change is one undo step; Reset all, recovery and the header's count ("4 spawn point edits") take
  them. The panel names the project's values "(the project's)" ([spawn_rules.js](../tools/viewer/web/spawn_rules.js))
  and says what the move keeps: its name, so what uses it still does; its links stay where the map has them.
- **The document**: `overrides[]` of `target {package, level: "base", actor}` with a whole pose (only where it moved
  or turned) and `spawn`, the sparse values; [project.js](../tools/viewer/web/project.js) `validOverride` takes them,
  and a record the page doesn't take (a delete, another kind's key) is carried and saved back unchanged.
- **The compiler**: `spawn_of`, `spawn_values` and `spawn_override`: refuses a kind it only shows
  (`spawn-view-only`), an actor the level doesn't list (`spawn-unlisted`), one whose values weren't read
  (`spawn-unread`), another kind's or an out-of-range value (`spawn-values`), and a delete (`spawn-delete`, SP7's);
  notes a value of no kind (carried), a point as the map has it, and the links that stay (`spawn-links`); the moves and
  values go to the native edit's `spawns` lane; SP5's place counts read the moved places; the report counts
  `spawns {moved, valued, added, deleted}`.
- **The writer** ([native_spawns.py](../tools/bake/native_spawns.py) `apply_lane`, `set_values`, `verify`;
  [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py)): each point edited in place under its own name (a based one's
  relative place from its base's final place), each value written as a tagged property (a flag the pod saves none of
  grows its export; the Meld difficulty as its `EMeldContainerDifficulty` name), read back after the write.
- **The Build** ([build.py](../tools/editor/build.py)): spawn edits are work of their own, with no relight and the
  lighting kept; the manifest counts them (`spawnEdits`).
- **Example** [exp72_sp6_project.py](../tools/editor/examples/exp72_sp6_project.py): URB_Bar's pod 0 moved a tile and
  turned a quarter, pod 1 the commander's, Meld point 2 hard and destroyed on turn 6, Meld point 3 in spawn group 1;
  `--again` builds twice, `--cleared` and `--grid` on the cleared and the resized Bar.
- **Checked** offline on URB_Bar: built twice byte for byte the same; read back with the package reader on its own:
  the same 32 actors, export indices, names and children, every point the edit didn't touch byte for byte, each
  edited point as asked; the cleared and the resized Bar build and read back the same way. Tests: compiler (the
  family off, the lane, each refusal), bake (`test_native_spawns.py`: the value bytes; Bar edited, read back, the
  rest as it was, the refusals), build (a spawn-only project in both kinds of build), node (`spawns_view_test.mjs`:
  the edit rules, the override, a saved record read back; `project_spawns_test.mjs`: `validOverride`), the families
  table; the page tried on a test server with the family on (the project's four edits opened as saved, turned, valued,
  undone back to saved).
- **Gaps**: the plan had these points as roots of the main gizmo, with box select and free moves with snap off; they
  are moved in the Spawns view by its own arrows, one at a time, by whole tiles and levels. The game check
  (the lab copy with the pod and Meld mutators out) is still to come.

### Spawns, stage SP8: scripted drop-ins land where placed (project schema 4)

- **Project schema 4** ([projects.py](../tools/viewer/projects.py), [project.js](../tools/viewer/web/project.js),
  [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py)): read 1 to 4, written as 4; a save of 1 to 3 is refused as a stale page's.
  It adds `spawnRules`, and will hold the base spawn points' records of SP6 and SP7.
- **The rule** `spawnRules: {"dropIns": "placed"}`:
  - the page ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js), [index.html](../tools/viewer/web/index.html)): a checkbox in the
    Spawns flyout, "Scripted drop-ins land where placed (Long War)", with a tooltip on what it covers; greyed with the
    reason on plain Enemy Within and on a Long War without the drop-in mutator; a line where the install's
    ExcludeMaps names the base map (the Chryssalid Hive) and the project has no rule; saved, opened, recovered, taken
    by Reset all and undone as one step; a drop-in's "In the game" follows it;
  - the compiler: refuses any other value (`spawn-rules`), counts the rule as an edit, passes it to the Build and the
    report; note `dropins-placed` counts the scripted actions it covers over the map and the kept missions' streams
    (export 33's `uses`); note `dropins-base-excluded` for the Hive's case; `scripted_users()` reads the uses as the
    page does;
  - the Build ([build.py](../tools/editor/build.py)): the rule alone is work; the manifest's `config.dropInExclusion`
    gives the file, section and line, planned against the build's install (`why` where it can't take it), and the
    README a step for `DefaultRandomSpawns.ini`. A build whose map nothing changes (landing zones or the rule alone)
    now says lighting unchanged, where its README spoke of a texture cache it doesn't have;
  - the install ([installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py)): Play in game and the campaign install plan the line again
    against the install (`plan_variant_exclusion`, after the drop-in section's ExcludeMaps lines, under a comment
    naming the editor and the project), back the file up with the other two, note it as `playExclusions` or
    `dropInExclusions`, and take it out only where it stands as written (clearing a play, Remove from game, reset);
    a campaign install takes a play's line over; nothing is written on plain Enemy Within or without the mutator,
    and the play says why;
  - map packs ([manager.py](../tools/viewer/manager.py), [pack_scripts.py](../tools/viewer/pack_scripts.py)): a map's
    `pack.json` entry carries its lines, the README a step for the file, and the PowerShell scripts add them where
    the game's file has the drop-in section and take them out again;
  - [spawnrules.py](../tools/viewer/spawnrules.py) gains `exclusion_block`;
    [readme_install_check.py](../tools/release/readme_install_check.py) follows a README's step for the third file.
- [research/editor-contracts.md](../research/editor-contracts.md), section 4: schema 4 and `spawnRules`.
- New [exp72_sp8_sp9_projects.py](../tools/editor/examples/exp72_sp8_sp9_projects.py): EXP-72 runs 3 to 5's projects.
- Checked: new [project_spawns_test.mjs](../tools/viewer/tests/project_spawns_test.mjs); the project node tests at 4;
  [test_projects.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_projects.py) (schema 4 saved with the rule, a schema 3 page's save
  refused); [test_spawnrules.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_spawnrules.py) (another section's line, the `+` form, the
  block); [test_play.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_play.py) (the line in with a play and out byte for byte, a campaign

### Effects drawn closer to the game: fires look like fire, the night smoke is no longer pink (export 31)

- [effects_draw.py](../tools/viewer/effects_draw.py), draw version 4 ([export.py](../tools/viewer/export.py) export 31):
  - Each particle texture's traits come from its pixels (`texture_traits`): grey, an alpha that holds a shape, packed
    channels, red share, brightness. Packed means no blue with red and green unrelated, or mostly blue to pink, as the
    night smoke's `T_Roiling_Smoke_SubUV`, whose red, green and blue are its light from below, from above and its
    density.
  - The colour and the shape come from different textures (`pick_textures`: `picture`, `opacity` alpha, brightness
    or none, `mask`, `maskFrom` brightness, alpha or red). The fires' colour is their Flame picture and their shape a
    grey mask; before, names alone gave the debris the packed smoke noise and the Flame's near-empty alpha hid them.
  - A material's own colour parameters are read (`material_colours` into `colours`) and tint a see-through particle
    with no picture. The night smoke plume's are all but black.
- [effects_sim.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_sim.js):
  - Colour channels that carry data are drawn as the mean of the others (`dataChannels`). The fires' green and blue
    offsets reach 50, and the night smoke's green is scaled by up to 200 over its life (a colour scale that differs
    by channel).
  - An alpha that rises above 1.2 erodes the shape rather than making it solid (`alphaErodes`: the fire chunks).
  - A colour saved with only a vector, as URB_Bar's webbing's, is read as that vector, not white.
- [effects_preview.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_preview.js):
  - See-through and added particles are blended premultiplied, as the game lays a bright colour at a low opacity.
  - A sprite is never thinner than two pixels (`viewHeight`).
  - A solid mesh with no colour of its own is drawn charred.
  - A dark see-through colour is lifted to a dull grey: the bar's steam is a faint wisp, not black.
  - `materialTint` gives the material's tint.
  - `describe()` gives the page's `likenessOf` hook for checks.
- [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js):
  - The Add panel's pane shows the row's tip inside itself; the browser's own tooltip no longer covers the drawing.
  - Pictures and the pane frame the size-weighted bulk of the particles.
  - A vector read by a colour module is labelled r, g, b, not x, y, z.
- [effects_rules.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_rules.js): a vector parameter named Color, Colour or Tint is shown and
  edited as a colour and a strength (`colourNamed`), such as `P_Power_Core_Persistent`'s Color, which scales its
  colour over life.

### Effects drawn as they look: the likeness in the view (effects and sounds plan, stage FXV2)

- [effects_sim.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_sim.js), new, no three.js: one emitter stepped from its draw data. `sample`
  reads a distribution at a time (a table's entry blended to the next, a random range with its locked axes, a particle
  parameter through its mode's ranges); `makeEmitter` spawns by the rate and the bursts, gives each particle its life,
  place (a point, a box, a sphere, a cylinder), speed, size, colour, turn and sub-image, and changes them over its
  life by the followed modules; seeded, so the same effect draws the same; `LIMITS` (400 particles an emitter, 1,500
  an effect, 30,000 in the view).
- [effects_preview.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_preview.js), new: `makeLikeness` draws a system: each sprite emitter
  as instanced quads that face the camera (or lie along their speed), each mesh emitter as an instanced mesh, both
  through one shader with the picture and mask the export picked, blended as the material says (see-through, added,
  multiplied, solid). It starts warm (run ahead by its longest life) and a system that has played out starts again
  after two seconds.

### Effects' and sounds' values in the compiler and the Build (effects and sounds plan, stage FX5, part 1)

- An effect's size, starting state and particle parameters, and a sound's radii, volume, pitch and starting state,
  are checked by the compiler and written by the Build, behind two gates of their own: the families `effect-values`
  and `sound-values` ([compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `FAMILIES`), off until their game check, so moves,
  copies and deletes go on building as they do (`--family effect-values` lifts one for an experiment's build). The
  page doesn't offer them yet.
- The compiler (`effect_values`, `effect_parameters`, `effect_value_warnings`): a value-only override, a move with
  values and a copy with values reach the lanes' `values` (originals, in place) and each copy's `values`, as the
  writer takes them: a parameter keeps the type its effect saves it in (a scalar saved where the system's
  distribution is a vector stays a scalar), a name it doesn't save gets the distribution's kind; refused: values
  where the export's `can.values` says no (a shared cue's), a random or untyped parameter, a name the system reads as
  both kinds or lacks, a malformed value or one outside what a value may be (`EFFECT_SCALE`, `SOUND_RADIUS_MAX`,
  `SOUND_VOLUME_MAX`, `SOUND_PITCH`, `PARAMETER_MAX`), an inner radius beyond the outer one; warned of: one set to
  start off with nothing in the script to switch it on, a starting state the script switches anyway, parameters the
  script sets too. Deletion wins over values. The report counts `valued`.
- The Build ([native_effects.py](../tools/bake/native_effects.py) `set_values`, `set_parameters`, `read_values`,
  `check_values`): on the actor's own exports only (never a clone's source, an archetype or a cue asset): the
  actor's `DrawScale` multiplied (its `DrawScale3D` kept), the component's `bAutoActivate`, its `InstanceParameters`
  patched by name (an entry's value field set in place, a new name added at the end, every other entry byte for
  byte, an array added where the component saves none), a sound's node `RadiusMin`, `RadiusMax`, `VolumeMin`,
  `VolumeMax`, `PitchMin`, `PitchMax` and its actor's `bAutoPlay`; read back in the lane's verify. The native edit,
  `native_split` and the Build's dispatch carry the `values` lane ([compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py),
  [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py), [native_copy.py](../tools/bake/native_copy.py)).
- Contract: the effects' and sounds' override row ([editor-contracts.md](../research/editor-contracts.md)).

Checked: [test_compiler_effects.py](../tools/editor/tests/test_compiler_effects.py) `Values` (the gates, value-only and
mixed records, copies, a foreign copy against its donor's system, every refusal and warning);
[test_native_effects.py](../tools/bake/tests/test_native_effects.py) `ValueLanes` on the install's URB_Bar (Emitter_38's
size, starting state, a scalar on a vector distribution, a colour and a new parameter; a value it has already leaves
the component's bytes as they were; a copy's values on the copy alone, its source and the other copy as the map has
them; a simple sound's values in place and a copy's one radius; export 28 reads them all back); test_families; the
editor, viewer and bake effect, transplant and copy suites. Known gaps: no game check yet (EXP-E), no page controls.

### Effects and sounds from other maps (effects and sounds plan, stage FX4)

The Add panel's All maps lists the base maps' effects and ambient sounds, and one placed from there is brought into
the map by the Build, as a piece of another map is.
- **The library** ([library.py](../tools/viewer/library.py), index 9; [effects_library.py](../tools/viewer/effects_library.py),
  new): each base map's effects and sounds are scanned with its pieces (`scan_effects`, through
  [effects_metadata.py](../tools/viewer/effects_metadata.py)'s `describe`) into entries of family `effect` or `sound`,
  one per recipe (an effect's class, system, saved parameters, scale, component offset, starting state; a sound's
  class, cue, waves, values, starting state), from the map whose copy brings least, with the panel's kind (from the
  system's or wave's name). A stream's are not scanned; a landing's, one riding on another and one playing nothing
  are listed `unavailable` with why; the TextureMovie system's closure is refused as before. `library.effect` gives
  one as a template (its export 28 record, its system or waves), the donor described once into
  `effects-v1.json` in its pieces folder; the precache skips them. The full scan of 151 maps took 29 s and has 1,826
  effect and sound entries (1,671 effects, 155 sounds; 40 can't be placed).
- **The server** ([viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py)): `GET /library/effect.json`, `POST /library/effects.json` (a
  project's opening) and `GET`/`HEAD /library/wave.ogg?package=&id=` (the Wave preview of another map's sound, through
  the same WaveCache). The build summary ([builds.py](../tools/viewer/builds.py)) says `foreignEffects` and each donor's
  `effects`.
- **The page**: All maps' rows for them ([library.js](../tools/viewer/web/library.js): the Effects view's marker as the
  picture, what each plays, where it is placed, Starts off, Not brought), the Kind menu's Effects and Sounds with their
  kinds ([piece_categories.js](../tools/viewer/web/piece_categories.js)); placing one reads its template and places a copy
  as Ctrl+V does ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js) `chooseLibraryEffect`, `effectTemplate`), its system and waves
  joined to the map's; a project's copies of them read back on opening (`loadForeignTemplates`); the panel says where
  one comes from; the Wave preview plays another map's wave from that map; the Build window's step counts them.
  [effects_view.js](../tools/viewer/web/effects_view.js) `drawEffectIcon` draws a row's picture.
- **The compiler** ([compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `foreign_effect`, `Library.effect`): an added effect or
  sound whose `from` names another base map is checked against the library (the file it was scanned from, an entry
  of its family; `unavailable` and `closure` refused) and goes to its lane with its `donor`; the report's `donors`
  list it.
- **The Build** ([transplant.py](../tools/bake/transplant.py) `stage_edit`, [build.py](../tools/editor/build.py),
  [native_effects.py](../tools/bake/native_effects.py)): the lanes' copies with a donor are staged in the map (each donor
  actor once, outside the level's list; a system or wave the map has by path is the map's own), the copies rewritten
  to clone the staged actor (`lane_actor` takes a staged source only outside the list); an effects-only full build
  reads the staged map too. The manifest says `foreignEffects`.
- **[F-121](../research/findings-register.md), fixed:** the transplanter kept each donor's imports by `id(donor)`, which a

### Effects and sounds, stage FX2: the Wave preview

The second stage of the effects and sounds plan, on branch `effects-and-sounds`: a picked sound's waves can be heard
in the Effects view. Nothing a Build makes changes, and the export stays at 28.
- [audio.py](../tools/viewer/audio.py), new: a wave's Ogg Vorbis stream read from its PC bulk record
  ([effects_metadata.py](../tools/viewer/effects_metadata.py)'s new `pc_sound`, which `wave_record` now uses too) and
  checked before it is served: one logical stream, each page's capture pattern, version, checksum and number, the
  continued-packet flags against the lacing, the identification header alone on the first page, the comment and setup
  headers before the first audio page, the end flag on the last page, granules that never go back, at most 32 MB and an
  hour. A bounded cache (64 MB) keeps each wave read; the map's own package is used only while it is the file the map
  was exported from (its SHA-256), a stream's by its size and time.
- [viewer.py](../tools/viewer/viewer.py): `GET`/`HEAD /maps/<id>/wave.ogg?id=<soundWaves key>`, `audio/ogg` with its
  length, an ETag (`If-None-Match`: 304) and one byte range at a time (206; 416 outside it). An id the export doesn't
  list (a stale or made-up one, a path) is 404, a wave it can't serve 422 with why; one bad wave never fails the map.
- The effect panel's **Wave preview** ([app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js), [index.html](../tools/viewer/web/index.html),
  [style.css](../tools/viewer/web/style.css)): each wave of a picked sound with Play/Stop, one at a time, at volume 0.6,
  the clock while it plays; picking something else, Escape, leaving the view or opening another map or project stops
  and releases it; a refusal shows the server's reason, a decode failure says so.
- Docs: [tools/viewer/README.md](../tools/viewer/README.md) and section 8 of
  [editor-contracts.md](../research/editor-contracts.md).

Checked: [test_audio.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_audio.py), new (made-up Ogg streams: a good one, one with a packet
over a page boundary, and each of 25 refusals; Ogg's CRC check value; byte ranges; the cache's refusals; on the
install, Bar's Skyranger idle wave against its own properties, the cache and its bound, and the route: GET, HEAD,

### Effects census, version 2: copies left out, the plan's evidence gaps closed

The effects and sounds plan was checked again, at the user's ask, against the code as it stands and the packages.

- **The first census counted a copy.** A variant of one map installed in the game, and its landing intro, were
  counted as Firaxis's: a map the editor builds keeps the package GUID of the map it grew from.
  [audit_effects.py](../tools/upk/audit_effects.py) now counts only the oldest file of a GUID (`copies`,
  `copiesLeftOut`).
- **What it reads besides** (its docstring has the list):
  - which actors the level's actor list holds;
  - everything under each particle system, over all LOD levels, with its native bytes by class;
  - the parameters a system offers against the ones its effects save;
  - whether a system's emitters loop;
  - each wave's bulk records by their headers;
  - why a sound reaches no wave, and what its node saves or inherits;
  - each building floor's emitter list against where the emitters stand;
  - what a `Base` resolves to;
  - what the two carrying rules would pick;
  - whether LWR's patches name an effect as text;
  - `Engine.upk`'s class defaults for starting on;
  - the map list's and each package's SHA-256.
- **Its result:** [effects-audit-2026-11-17.json](../research/evidence/effects-audit-2026-11-17.json), for 96 base
  maps, 54 Firaxis streams and 87 LWR patches.
  - 7,138 effects in 95 base maps and 421 in streams, every one in its level's list; 849 sounds in 90 base maps;
    92 flares.

### Replace comments out only the base map's records the variant has records for (F-118)

A build has records for its project's missions only, but Replace commented out every record of its base map, so a
mission the variant has no record for lost the map. A mission that asks for its map by name then found none: a
variant of Commercial Alley Redux for covert extraction only left a new campaign's first mission without a map.
- [installs.py](../tools/viewer/installs.py): `rotation_plan` returns `standsFor` (the base map's records the build has
  records for, from `recordMissions`) and `kept` (the missions of the others); a rotation install keeps `standsFor`
  in its ledger entry, and `replaced_records` / `_sync_off` comment out only those. An entry written before still
  replaces every record of its base map. `mission_warnings` names, under Replace, the missions left to the original
  and says when the original plays the first mission.
- [pack_scripts.py](../tools/viewer/pack_scripts.py): `pack.ps1` comments out the base map's live records whose
  DisplayName is in the map's `switch`, leaving the rest; a `pack.json` without `switch` (an older pack) comments out
  every one, as before. [manager.py](../tools/viewer/manager.py) writes `switch` for the covered records only and
  `keep` for the others, and the pack's README lists both. The project manager's Replace warnings come from the last
  build's records when there is one.
- [gamemaps.py](../tools/viewer/gamemaps.py): the Game maps window marks only the replaced records.
- The [README](../tools/viewer/README.md), the [guide](../tools/release/guide/guide.html) and
  [F-118](../research/findings-register.md) say it.
- Checked: two new tests in [test_manager.py](../tools/viewer/tests/test_manager.py) (a covert-extraction-only variant
  on the first mission's map through the editor, the Game maps window, an old ledger entry, and through a pack's
  scripts, an old pack without `switch` too, each out byte for byte) and an assertion in the D4 test; they fail on
  the code before the change. The `viewer`, `repo` and `release` suites pass. Not played in the game.

### Map grid works on maps past 128 tiles at their own size (TempleShip, AlienBase01)

The user dragged the Map grid larger on a temple map. It snapped back on release and nothing changed. TempleShip's
own grid is 45 by 203 by 15 tiles, and a project's grid was capped at 128 tiles a side whatever the map's own size,
so every size dragged there failed the check. The Y handle also jumped down to 128 and left a hidden, too-small stage
in the project ([findings register](../research/findings-register.md) T-41).
- [project.js](../tools/viewer/web/project.js) `stageMax(own)`: each axis goes up to 128 tiles or 30 levels, or the
  map's own where that is more. `validStage(s, own)` checks against it. `sortState` checks only the stage's shape,
  because its size was checked when the stage was set, so a save keeps a grid like 77 by 203.
- [app.js](../tools/viewer/web/app.js) `gridRule` (the drag's bounds), `stageDims`, `setStage`, `applyState` and the
  recovery pass the map's own grid.
- [compiler.py](../tools/editor/compiler.py) `stage_max`, the twin, in `Compiler.stage`. Its comment no longer says the
  game's maps stop at 70 tiles.
- [The viewer README](../tools/viewer/README.md) gives the limits (it still said 18 levels).
- Checked: a browser run on a test server on TempleShip, before and after the fix. Before: X 77 and up 30 snapped
  back to 45 and 15, and Y went to 128 with `grid: [45, 128]` saved. After: X 77 and up 30 stay (stage and
  `editState` both keep them), and Y stays at 203. `test_compiler` (a new StageTests test on a 45 by 203 by 15 map;
  `-k Stage`, `-k Clear`), the node suite (clear_map_test asserts `stageMax`, `validStage` and `sortState` on it),
  and `browser_smoke --only clear-map` on URB_Bar.
- Gaps: TempleShip can't be made deeper than its own 203, by the rule. No Build has been run on a larger
  TempleShip.

The user's queued build of temple_improved failed at once: "the build would write names that are taken:
